author: atomantic
body:
## What & why

Closes #1802.

Ollama models are trained against the **OpenAI** tool-calling format, so under the Claude harness (`ANTHROPIC_*`) they frequently *describe* a file edit as JSON without ever applying it — the model "responds" but nothing changes on disk (the exact symptom #1802 reports). **OpenCode** speaks the OpenAI-compatible protocol natively, so the same local models reliably read/write/edit files.

This adds a new **OpenCode Ollama** AI provider (headless CLI) that drives `opencode run` against a local Ollama daemon, mirroring the existing **Claude Ollama** provider — disabled by default, enabled + model-picked from the AI Providers page, delivered to existing installs via migration.

## How it works

- **Provider** `opencode-ollama` (`type: cli`, `command: opencode`, `args: ["run"]`, `ollamaBacked: true`). The Ollama connection is configured inline via `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` (an `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider at `http://localhost:11434/v1` + `"permission":"allow"` for unattended tool execution) — no `opencode.json` to hand-write.
- **Prompt delivery** rides the existing stdin path (`opencode run` reads piped stdin); model selection is `-m ollama/<model>`.
- **Model namespacing** — OpenCode addresses models as `provider/model`, so a new shared helper `prefixOpencodeModel` namespaces the bare Ollama id as `ollama/<id>` (idempotent; handles slash-bearing `hf.co/...` ids; **gated on `ollamaBacked`** so a user's non-Ollama OpenCode provider with an already-qualified id like `openai/gpt-4o` isn't mangled). A sibling `isOpencodeCommand` matches the binary by basename (bare / path / `.exe`) so a path-configured provider (`/opt/homebrew/bin/opencode`) isn't misrouted to the Claude-style invocation.
- **Wired into every CLI/TUI arg builder** — `buildCliArgs` (runner + `cliProviderRun` → brain/meatspace), `buildCliSpawnConfig` (CoS headless agents — the core path), `appendModelArgs`/`buildTuiInvocation` (TUI), and `askService`. Each respects a user-baked `--model`/`-m` pin.
- **CoS Runner allowlist** — `opencode` added to `ALLOWED_COMMANDS` so headless tasks aren't rejected before spawn.
- **Model refresh** — reuses the ollama-backed `_fetchOllamaToolCapableModels` path (tool-use-capable models only).

## Upgrade path

- Migration `149-opencode-ollama-providers.js` (idempotent, additive) delivers the provider to existing installs on a plain restart; seeded in `data.reference/providers.json` + `providers.sample.json` for fresh installs / **Load Samples**.

## Scope note — CLI only (TUI deferred to #1814)

Only the **headless CLI** provider ships. A TUI variant is deferred (#1814): the CoS *TUI-task* completion path drives the slashdo `/do:pr`/`/do:push` + sentinel handoff, which `opencode` can't execute (it doesn't load `.claude/commands/do/*`). The CLI path completes through the graceful "do it manually if `/do:push` is unavailable" light-prompt fallback, so it's unaffected. The TUI arg-builder wiring stays (valid for interactive Shell / a user-added provider); only the default-shipped provider is CLI.

## Tests

New/extended unit tests for the helper, all five arg builders (incl. baked-pin and path-configured cases), the runner allowlist, the Ask path, and the migration. Requires the `opencode` CLI on PATH at runtime.

## Review

Local reviews (`claude`, `codex`) ran pre-PR and converged clean — claude surfaced an Ask `run`-subcommand hang + model-pin gaps (fixed); codex surfaced the runner-allowlist P1, the `ollamaBacked`/basename gates, and the TUI-completion scoping (fixed / deferred to #1814).

author: raluaces
body:
## Summary

- **Remove top navbar** from Files, Albums, Streams, Shorts, and Preview pages — replaced with a hamburger button in the toolbar (leftmost position) or top-left floating button on the preview page
- **Sidebar now slides from the left** (`offcanvas-start`) across all pages, instead of the right
- **Extracted offcanvas** into a reusable `include/nav-offcanvas.html` with self-contained URL-based active detection (`request.resolver_match.view_name`), replacing the old template-inheritance block approach
- **Home/settings pages** keep the full top navbar unchanged; it now wraps the same offcanvas include
- **Preview page** simplified: removed auto-hide pull-tab and idle-timer logic; the floating nav button is always visible without JS

## Architecture

- New `{% block navbar_inner %}` in `main.html` lets toolbar pages suppress the visual `<nav>` chrome while keeping the fixed `<header>` (needed for the sticky toolbar)
- New `{% block body_class %}` lets pages append CSS classes to `<body>`; toolbar/preview pages add `no-top-navbar` to zero out navbar padding
- Dead block overrides (`files_active`, `albums_active`, etc.) removed from all child templates — URL detection in the include replaces them

## Test plan

- [ ] `/files/`, `/albums/`, `/streams/`, `/shorts/` — no top navbar; hamburger button at toolbar left opens left-side offcanvas
- [ ] File preview URL — no top navbar; floating button top-left opens left-side offcanvas
- [ ] Home page — full top navbar present, offcanvas now slides from left
- [ ] Mobile widths — offcanvas opens from left on all pages
- [ ] Settings pages — navbar still fully functional
- [ ] Active nav link highlighting correct in offcanvas on each page

author: acmerfight
body:
## Problem

`edit` and `apply_patch` both need to preserve source text while matching normalized input, but the CRLF normalization, source-map reprojection, and source-line-ending replacement helpers had drift-prone local copies in both tool paths. That made the edit-match anti-drift work incomplete: the strategy table was paired, but the surrounding source-preservation mechanics could still split again.

Closes #297.
Closes #298.
Closes #309.

## Solution

- Move the shared source-reprojection helpers into `src/tools/edit-match.ts`.
- Make `src/tools/edit.ts` and `src/tools/apply-patch/hunks.ts` import that shared path instead of defining local copies.
- Add focused invariant coverage for the edit-match paired strategy table and the shared source-reprojection ownership.
- Add an apply_patch BDD case proving fuzzy hunks preserve source indentation and CRLF line endings together.
- Document the anti-drift patterns in `DEVELOPMENT.md`.

## Why

The risky behavior is not only whether a fuzzy match is found, but whether the matched normalized span is projected back into the original file without losing indentation or line-ending style. Keeping that logic in one owner makes future changes harder to split by accident while preserving the existing tool behavior.

## Effect

After this, a user can run `edit` or `apply_patch` on CRLF/source-preserving replacements and see both tools preserve source text through one shared helper path; CI rejects future split edit-match strategy drift.

## Verification

- `pnpm vitest run tests/invariants/single-source.test.ts tests/tools/apply-patch.test.ts tests/tools/edit.test.ts`
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm vitest run tests/invariants`
- `pnpm vitest run tests/tools`
- `git diff --check`
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm knip`
- `pnpm eval:check`
- `pnpm test:coverage`
- `pnpm coverage:patch` (`34/34 changed coverable lines covered`)

## Review Notes / Risks

- Empty-context subagent review was attempted twice, but the reviewer tool stream disconnected before completion both times, so no subagent findings were received.
- DeepSeek QA was not applicable because this slice does not change provider-visible agent response behavior.
- The invariant is intentionally curated to declared edit-match ownership and source-reprojection consumers; it avoids broad structural similarity scanning.

body:
## Gestão de Negócios (Pipeline de Deals) — Migração RD Station → VYD Engage (P0)

Implementa o **P0** da spec [`specs/gestao-negocios-rdstation.md`](specs/gestao-negocios-rdstation.md): paridade do fluxo diário de gestão de negócios do RD Station, para que a equipe não sinta diferença ao migrar.

Entrega faseada por prioridade — este PR cobre **apenas P0**; P1/P2 ficam para PRs seguintes.

### Backend
- **Schema (migration aditiva `20260627130000_gestao_negocios_p0`)**: `FunnelColumn` (abbreviation/objective/playbook/coolingEnabled/coolingDays); `Deal` (qualification/oneTimeValue/recurringValue/status `DealStatus`/pausedAt/wonAt/lostAt + relações sourceId/originCampaignId/lostReasonId); `CustomField` (entity/visibility); `Product.customFields`. Novos models: `LostReason`, `DealSource`, `OriginCampaign`, `DealContact`, `StageRequiredField`. Novos enums `DealStatus`/`CustomFieldEntity`/`CustomFieldVisibility` + `MULTI_SELECT`.
- **Enforcement de campos obrigatórios por etapa (req 4)** nos **dois** caminhos: clique/stepper (`dealService.update`) **e** drag‑drop (`funnelService.moveDeal`), via helper compartilhado `assertStageRequiredFieldsFilled` — bloqueia com mensagem listando os campos pendentes.
- **Ganho/Perda/Pausar‑Retomar**: `markWon`/`markLost` (exige `LostReason` válido)/`pause`/`resume` + rotas dedicadas.
- **Múltiplos contatos**: `DealContact` + rotas GET/POST/DELETE `/deals/:id/contacts`.
- **CRUD de Motivos de Perda / Fontes / Campanhas** (tenant‑scoped, na whitelist de CSRF).
- **Esfriamento por etapa** no job `staleDeals` (fallback para `tenant.staleDays`; ignora `PAUSED`).
- **Rota** `GET /deals/:id/stage-history` (tempo na etapa).
- **Seed RD** (`server/scripts/seed-rd-config.ts`): 8 funis + ~39 campos de Negociação + 13 motivos de perda (idempotente, dry‑run por padrão).

### Frontend
- **Detalhe da negociação em 7 abas** (Histórico, E‑mail, Tarefas, Produtos, Arquivos, Propostas, Questionários) + **stepper clicável** das etapas com tempo‑na‑etapa + **playbook** da etapa + **badge de esfriamento**.
- **Aba Histórico** com filtro por tipo de evento + criar anotação.
- **Múltiplos contatos** no detalhe (buscar/adicionar/remover).
- **Card do kanban enriquecido**: status, esfriamento, empresa, qualificação, responsável, valor, contagem de tarefas.
- **Filtros e busca na visão de funil** (responsável/status/ordenação) + toggle lista.
- **Formulário**: qualificação (estrelas), fonte/campanha, valor único/recorrente, e **campos personalizados por entidade** com **multi‑select**.
- **Tela de Configurações de Negócios** (motivos/fontes/campanhas).

### Qualidade
- `tsc` (backend) e `vite build` (frontend) verdes; ratchet de typecheck em **269** (baseline 276), 0 erro novo.
- Auditoria adversarial requisito‑a‑requisito: **41/42 P0** na 1ª rodada → 1 lacuna (empresa do card) **corrigida** → 2ª verificação (5 verificadores paralelos) **PASS em tudo**.
- Multi‑tenancy preservada em todas as queries novas; CSRF whitelist nas rotas novas.

### ⚠️ Pré‑requisitos de deploy (produção)
1. `prisma migrate deploy` no Railway (migration aditiva).
2. `seed-rd-config.ts --write --slug <tenant>` para popular a configuração do RD.

### Fora deste PR (P1/P2)
Visibilidade de funil por equipe; abas ricas de E‑mail/Tarefas/Arquivos/Propostas/Questionários (são placeholders aqui); personalizar cartões; telas de config de funis/etapas/campos por entidade; automação entre funis. O breakpoint `lg:` ausente do CSS pré‑compilado (app‑wide, pré‑existente) faz o detalhe empilhar em coluna única.

author: hotterthenheat
body:
## What

Phase-4 (replace weak heuristics) cleanup of the dealer view's per-expiry GEX split.

### Before
When a single non-aggregate expiry was selected, each strike's aggregate exposure was attributed to that expiry by:
```ts
multiplier = max(0.05, |sin(strike·hash(expiryId)/10000)|)   // + a flat ×1.5 for the front tab
```
An arbitrary, hash-seeded sine with no financial meaning. It was labeled `MODEL SPLIT` in the UI (so not *dishonest*), but it's exactly the kind of heuristic that doesn't survive scrutiny.

### After
A defensible **gamma term-structure** decomposition. The server still ships one aggregated chain, so we attribute each strike's exposure across expiries by how dealer gamma actually concentrates with tenor:

- **amplitude** `a(d) ∝ 1/√d` — near-dated options carry more gamma
- **shape** `g(s,d) = exp(-½·z²/EM(d)²)`, `z = (strike−spot)/spot`, `EM(d) = σ·√(d/365)` — near expiries peak tightly at spot, far expiries spread out (the real gamma-by-tenor profile)

Weights are **normalized across all expiry tiles per strike**, which gives two properties the sine split lacked:
1. Selecting *every* expiry reconstructs the aggregate **exactly**.
2. A selection that resolves to no known tile falls back to the **real aggregate** instead of inventing.

Still labeled `MODEL` in the UI — it's a principled model, not a per-expiration feed.

Net: **1 file, +40 / −54** (also simpler — drops the dead `dist` local and the per-id accumulation loop).

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `vite build` — clean
- Full test suite (18 suites) — all pass
- Math checked: `Σ_all w = 1` per strike ⇒ all-expiries == aggregate; all divisions floored/guarded; `σ` and `EM` floored so 0DTE can't produce a delta spike or div-by-zero

## Risk
Low — a labeled MODEL refinement gated to non-aggregate expiry selection; the default aggregate view returns the real profile unchanged via early-out.

body: Adds a local end-to-end proof that the relay round-trips a real Google authorization code with the consuming bot (marge-bot) faithfully stood in, plus the design and implementation-plan docs under `docs/superpowers/`; no relay source under `src/` is touched. `test/loop.test.ts` is an automated supertest that wires the full sequence (`/session` → `/authorize` 302 → `/callback` → `/result`) together in-process and opens the sealed code with a real Node libsodium key. `test/e2e/relay_smoke.py` stands in for the bot — generating an X25519 keypair, PKCE, and pickup secret — with an automated `interop` mode (no Google/browser) that proves Python PyNaCl opens what the relay's Node libsodium sealed, and a manual `real` mode that redeems the opened code at Google's token endpoint for actual tokens. author: scouten
body:
## Summary Implements STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Math) support per [docs/modules/stem/pages/index.adoc](docs/modules/stem/pages/index.adoc), resolving [#261](https://github.com/asciidoc-rs/asciidoc-parser/issues/261). STEM in AsciiDoc is a **passthrough** mechanism: the parser preserves the expression verbatim and surrounds it with the notation's math delimiters; the actual rendering is delegated to a downstream STEM provider (e.g. MathJax). No Rust math engine is involved. ### Inline STEM macros (`stem:[…]`, `asciimath:[…]`, `latexmath:[…]`) - Extracted as implicit passthroughs (last, so nested passthroughs like `stem:[+1+]` restore recursively). - AsciiMath → `\$…\$`, inline LaTeX → `\(…\)`, via new `QuoteType::AsciiMath`/`LatexMath`. - Bare `stem:` resolves notation from the `:stem:` document attribute (default AsciiMath). - Special-characters subs by default on HTML; explicit subs lists (`stem:c,a[…]`); legacy `$…$` stripping for latexmath; `\]` unescaping; empty macros not recognized; warning on invalid subs (new `WarningType::InvalidSubstitutionTypeForStemMacro`). ### Block STEM (`[stem]`/`[asciimath]`/`[latexmath]` on `++++`) - Becomes a `stem`-context raw block with special-characters substitutions (delimiters added downstream). Plain `++++` stays `pass`; explicit `subs=` still overrides. ### Out of scope (correctly deferred to the converter/MathJax) Equation numbering (`eqnums`), `\label`/`\eqref` references, and stem-block newline→`
` handling are all render-time concerns handled downstream; the parser passes the expressions through verbatim. ## Tests - 19 ported Ruby Asciidoctor "Math macros" tests (DocBook omitted per convention) + 5 block-STEM tests + warning Debug test. - Full SDD spec coverage for the stem page (`track_file!`/`verifies!`/`non_normative!`): **0 uncovered lines, 67 verified** (`cd sdd && cargo run`). - Full suite green; `clippy` clean; `cargo fmt`; nightly `cargo doc` clean. Outputs cross-checked against the `asciidoctor` CLI. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

The third link: a lab-scoped **shift grid** produces the staffing-model FTE need that auto-fills the VeritaPace forecast gap, replacing the hand-entered 28.3. Grounded in Michael's LTSHealth Staff Management Tool "Staffing Grid" sheet.

### What changed
- **`shared/operationsForecast.ts`** — `staffingGridFte(lines, hoursPerFte)`: sum of (hr/shift x days/wk + adj) / (hoursPerFte / 52). Single source, server + client.

This closes the chain end to end: goal -> hour allowance -> FTE budget -> **(grid) staffing FTE need** -> gap -> projected productivity. Phase 4 is the CFO-negotiation report PDF.

author: julianken
body:
## Diagrams

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant FE as Frontend (zoom<6 cell click)
    participant API as read-api
    participant DB as db-client
    participant PG as Postgres+PostGIS
    FE->>API: GET /api/observations/cell?species&scope&m&lng&lat&since
    API->>DB: getCellObservations(bucket, m, opts)
    DB->>PG: SELECT obs in cell envelope (bucket +/- 0.5/m) by species and since-window, newest-first, LIMIT 200
    PG-->>DB: rows + count(*) OVER() pre-LIMIT denominator
    DB-->>API: { data, meta: { cellObservationCount, truncated } }
    API-->>FE: 200 CellObservationsResponse
```

## Summary

- **Why:** at low zoom (`zoom < 6`) the map renders the precomputed `observation_grid_agg` grid, which stores only counts and discards individual observations — so the upcoming in-panel Sightings Log has no source for a clicked cell's per-sighting rows. The raw `observations` table still retains every sighting; this adds the bounded read path to reach them.
- **What:** new `getCellObservations` (single-cell query: envelope `[bucket ± 0.5/m]` + `species_code` + since-window + scope/state clip, `ORDER BY obs_dt DESC`, hard `LIMIT 200`, `count(*) OVER()` for the exact pre-LIMIT denominator) → `GET /api/observations/cell` → `CellObservationsResponse { data, meta: { cellObservationCount, truncated } }`.
- **Safety:** index-backed — the perf guard seeds prod-scale data and asserts via `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)` that the plan uses a `BitmapAnd` of the geom + species indexes with **no `Seq Scan on observations`** (flips red if either index is dropped). Single-species + single-cell scope makes this far cheaper than the all-species mega-cell scan behind the 2026-06-14 503 incident. No schema change / no migration; `NATIONAL_SCOPE_KEY` (not a literal) is the no-clip sentinel.

## Screenshots

N/A — not UI (backend only; no `frontend/**` files touched).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build && npm test` — green (no separate `npm run typecheck` in this repo; `build` runs `tsc`). db-client: 203 passed (+1 todo) incl. 9 new cell integration tests + 2 prod-scale perf/index guards; read-api: 199 passed incl. 13 new `GET /api/observations/cell` route tests.
- [x] New unit / integration tests added — testcontainers against real Postgres+PostGIS (no DB mocks).
- [ ] New Playwright e2e spec added — N/A (backend only, no user-visible UI change).
- [x] `npm run build` — clean production build (all workspaces incl. frontend `tsc -b` + vite).
- [ ] (UI only) Playwright MCP smoke — N/A — not UI.

## Plan reference

Implements #1300; part of epic #1299 (Sightings Log). Per repo convention, the plan lives in the issues (self-contained), not `docs/plans/`. Build order: **B1 (this) ∥ F2 → F3 → M4 → D5**.

author: abrignoni
body:
Converts the two PAS debug-log parsers — the last multi-report log artifacts — to the LAVA `@artifact_processor` pipeline.

## What changed
- **`pasDeGeo.py`** (Ford `pas_debug.log`) → **8 artifacts**: Dev Loc (KML), Road Speed Limits, Access Point List, Vehicle Speed, Transmission Status, Outside Temperature, Odometer, Vehicle Info.
- **`pasDeGeoTarGz.py`** (RAM `pas_debug.log.1` inside `archivedata/*.tar.gz`) → **9 artifacts**: GPS (KML), Road Speed Limits, Access Point List, Vehicle Speed, Transmission Status, Outside Temperature, Odometer, Current Road, Vehicle Info.

Each single log feeds many reports, so each report becomes its own `@artifact_processor` sharing one `_parse()` pass.

## Notes
- GPS/Dev-Loc reports expose `Latitude`/`Longitude` and emit KML (`output_types` includes `kml`).
- `pasDeGeoTarGz` reads `pas_debug.log.1` **in-memory** from the tar.gz instead of extracting it into the report folder (no evidence written to disk).
- Vehicle info (make / model / VIN / platform) is now surfaced as its own table in addition to `logdevinfo`, parsed faithfully from the original `"vin" :` / `"make"` / `"model"` log lines.
- Timestamps normalized to UTC. Original author attribution and first-merge `creation_date` preserved.

## Validation
- `py_compile` clean; `pylint --disable=C,R` = 10.00/10
- Reserved-word / duplicate-table audit: 17 tables, 0 issues
- Functional: all 8 + 9 artifacts parse synthetic logs correctly; PluginLoader recognizes every artifact

author: hankhsu1996
body:
## Summary

This completes the value-model reset: every runtime value becomes a pure value -- its SystemVerilog declared type is an immutable descriptor fixed at construction, and copy, move, and assignment all replace the whole value. The job of preserving a destination's declared type across assignment moves out of the value's own assignment operator and into the store boundary and the variable cell: the cell owns its declared type, installed once at construction, and the store boundary converts the right-hand side to the destination's full declared representation before it lands. This removes a chain of special cases the old shape-preserving integral assignment forced on every value type -- an adopt-on-first-store sentinel, a hand-written moved-from, and relocation-only swaps -- and closes the bug class that came from one object playing both the value role and the storage-cell role.

The reset is recorded as a new decision, `value-store-discipline.md`; the completed progress doc is removed.

## Design

Packed-struct and union field selects are now typed honestly at lowering. A field read is materialised at the part-select natural type (the field's dimensions, unsigned, in the aggregate's state domain -- exactly what the runtime produces, LRM 11.8.1) and then converted to the field's declared type by an explicit conversion, so a signed field and a 2-state field inside a 4-state aggregate both reach their declared signedness and state. The matching write widens a 2-state field value into the 4-state slot. This fixes a real bug: a 2-state `bit` field inside a 4-state packed struct previously aborted on both read and write with a representation mismatch.

The duplicated out-of-bounds shield each container carried (the element default plus the invalid-index discard target, with identical seeding, scrub, and read/write machinery across dynamic, queue, fixed-unpacked, and associative arrays) is consolidated into one `detail::OobShield<T>` that each container embeds.

The sort decision's rationale is corrected. The shape-preserving move-assign that originally forced selection sort over `std::ranges::sort` is gone, but selection sort stays for a reason the decision never stated: the SV comparison over 4-state keys is not a strict weak ordering, so the standard sort would be undefined behaviour. Code unchanged; the comment and decision now state the true reason.

## Testing

`bazel test //...` is green. A new seam test, `packed_struct_mixed_state_field`, covers the mixed-state field paths: a 2-state unsigned field, a 2-state signed field, a 4-state field, a packed-union member, a nested struct, the X-to-0 collapse on an uninitialized field read, and a same-type read-back.

author: sahil-ss9
body:
Fixes #55305

## Description

On ZFS filesystems, a burst of concurrent SQLite connections can corrupt the WAL shared-memory file (-shm), causing `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` to raise `sqlite3.OperationalError: disk I/O error` rather than the `locking protocol` error that `apply_wal_with_fallback()` already handles.

This PR adds `"disk i/o error"` to `_WAL_INCOMPAT_MARKERS` so the fallback to `journal_mode=DELETE` fires on ZFS the same way it does on NFS/SMB/FUSE, preventing the session database from wedging entirely.

### Changes
- Added `"disk i/o error"` to `_WAL_INCOMPAT_MARKERS` with ZFS context comment
- Updated `apply_wal_with_fallback` docstring to mention ZFS and both error types
- Updated hint message and WARNING log to include ZFS

## Verification
- Compile check on `hermes_state.py`: passed
- Lint: clean (all LSP errors are pre-existing type-annotation issues elsewhere in the file)
- Conventional commit: `fix(gateway): ...`
- No secrets or personal refs leaked
- Only `hermes_state.py` changed

author: kenny0312
body:
M4 设计草稿(评审后再动手)。把"看视频"做成**并行(快)+ 看得全(准)+ 不重看(省)**。

## 核心
- **并行**:同一步内独立的 `analyze_video` 用线程池并发(I/O 密集 → N× 降到 ~1×)。
- **覆盖**:并行后放宽/智能配额 + 先 SQL 缩 top-N。
- **缓存**:按 `(video_id, question, rubric, model, time_range)` 缓存 `AnalyzeResult`,Redis 优先 + fail-open + 进程内 LRU 兜底。
- **度量**:per-tool 计时/成本进 trace + 监控。

## 重点:并发正确性(别只想着"加线程池")
- `MODEL_OVERRIDE` 和 `_USAGE` 都是 **contextvar,不跨线程** → 裸加线程会**静默**让 Pro 失效 + token 漏算 → 必须 `copy_context().run`。
- 配额/ledger/seen 竞态 → 预分配 + 回主线程顺序写。
- **核对发现的现存缺口**:`analyze_video` 的 Gemini 调用**根本没上报 usage** → 视频分析成本现在没算进监控/审计;M4.1 先补这个(优先于并行)。

## 里程碑(可回退)
M4.0 加固 → M4.1 补 usage + 缓存 → M4.2 度量 → M4.3 并行(`MAX_ANALYZE_PARALLEL=1` 秒回退)→ M4.4 覆盖。

开放问题(待拍板):并行度上限、配额放到几、缓存 TTL、Redis vs 进程内、usage 合并方案。

author: zhaochy1990
body:
## 背景

存储 / 数据访问代码原先**横跨两个包、无单一归属**：SQLite 在 `stride_core`，Azure/文件/KV 散在 `stride_server`，且有 **8 份重复**的 dev-JSON/prod-Azure 后端选择 + **8 个独立** `DefaultAzureCredential()`。

本 PR 把这些固化成**统一数据访问层包 `src/stride_storage/`**，API Server 与 Coach Agent 共享同一数据层。**8 阶段推进，每阶段独立 subagent code-review + 全绿。**

## 关键设计

- **三层 import 结构**（`.importlinter` 强制）：Tier A `interfaces`（纯 Protocol + config，谁都能 import 含 coach）/ Tier B `sqlite`·`content`（引擎+实现）/ Tier C `azure`·`keyvault`·`factories`·`coach_persistence`（仅 Azure SDK，coach 永不 import）。
- **Coach 保持纯运行时、零 I/O**（核验通过）：只可选依赖 `interfaces`；具体 store 经 `coach_adapters` DI 注入。
- **config 加载留 server 侧**：`stride_storage` 工厂只收 resolved config dataclass，杜绝 `stride_storage → stride_server` 成环。
- **共享原语消除全部重复**：`get_credential` / `AzureTableConnection` / `get_container_client` / `choose_backend` / `get_secret_client` 各一份。

## 8 阶段交付（14 commits，每阶段 review + 2254 tests green + lint 5/5）

| Phase | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 0 | bootstrap 包 + 搬 config dataclass |
| 1 | 共享 azure 原语 + likes 样板 |
| 2 | master_plan / athlete_memory / notifications |
| 3 | content store（blob 注入）+ Key Vault 三 client 合一 |
| 4 | coach persistence 子系统整体迁入 |
| 5 | **db.py 2504 行 Database** + state_stores + calibration connector |
| 6 | CLAUDE.md 文档 + coach 纯度核验 |
| 7 | **consumer cutover**（~140 处 import 切到 `stride_storage.*`）+ 删纯 shim + 收紧 Contract 3/4 |

**亮点**：
- Phase 5 用 lazy `_paths()` 技巧让 2504 行 Database 迁移时 **213 处 USER_DATA_DIR 引用 + 60 处 monkeypatch 零改动**、无 import 环。
- Phase 7 完成全量 consumer cutover：`stride_core.db` 现只剩纯路径常量（不 import stride_storage）；删除 `state_stores` / `sqlite_connector` 纯 shim；Contract 3/4 收紧禁止纯公式层 import `stride_storage` 实现层。
- **6 轮 subagent code-review**，全部 APPROVE（共修 2 MEDIUM + 数个 LOW；Phase 4/5/7 零功能 findings）。

## 终态

- `stride_storage` 是**唯一数据访问层**，含所有实现 + interfaces；`stride_core` 搬走 I/O 后纯公式层真正 infra-free（Contract 3/4 强制）。
- 保留的薄层：`stride_server` 的 `*_store` **服务端 facade**（config 解析 + 缓存，非纯 shim）+ `coach_persistence` shim 包（带 `*_from_env` 包装）+ `stride_core.db` 路径常量。

## 验证

- `lint-imports` **5/5 contracts KEPT** 每阶段
- `pytest -n auto` **2254 passed** 每阶段
- coach core 零 storage import（核验）；Azure-free 子进程回归测试

## 已知 backlog（与本提取正交，未做）

inline-SQL RHR-baseline 去重（4 处直读 `daily_health.rhr` → 统一走 `RunningCalibrationRepository`）—— CLAUDE.md 标注的 pre-existing 反模式，留作后续。

body:
## Summary

یک وب‌اپ دوست‌یابی کامل (شبیه Badoo) با فرانت‌اند React + TypeScript (Vite) و بک‌اند Node/Express + SQLite + Socket.IO. کل رابط کاربری **فارسی و راست‌چین (RTL)** است.

A full Badoo-like dating web app. `main` holds the initial English scaffold; this PR adds a chat layout fix and the **full Persian (RTL) localization** on top of it.

### What's in the app
- **احراز هویت**: ثبت‌نام/ورود با JWT و هش رمز (`bcryptjs`).
- **پروفایل**: نام، سن (از تاریخ تولد)، جنسیت، ترجیح، شهر، بیو، عکس.
- **کاوش/سواایپ**: دِک کارتی شبیه Badoo با پسند (❤) / رد (✕).
- **مَچ**: وقتی دو نفر همدیگر را پسند کنند مَچ ساخته می‌شود.
- **چت بلادرنگ**: پیام‌رسانی لحظه‌ای بین مَچ‌ها روی Socket.IO.

### این PR چه چیزی اضافه می‌کند (diff vs `main`)
1. **رفع باگ چیدمان چت** — نوار ناوبری پایین، کادر تایپ پیام را می‌پوشاند. روی مسیرهای `/chat/*` نوار پایین مخفی شد:
   ```diff
   - const showNav = profile && !['/login','/register'].includes(pathname);
   + const hide = ['/login','/register','/chat'];
   + const showNav = profile && !hide.some(p => pathname.startsWith(p));
   ```
2. **فارسی‌سازی کامل + RTL**:
   - `index.html`: `lang="fa" dir="rtl"` و فونت Vazirmatn.
   - ترجمه‌ی همه‌ی رشته‌های UI (ورود/ثبت‌نام، کاوش، مَچ‌ها، چت، پروفایل، ناوبری).
   - داده‌ی دموی فارسی (نام‌ها، شهرها، بیوها) در `server/src/seed.ts`.
   - جابه‌جایی سمت حباب‌های چت برای RTL (پیام خودم سمت راست، پیام طرف مقابل سمت چپ):
     ```diff
     - .bubble.mine  { align-self: flex-end; }   /* راست در LTR */
     + .bubble.mine  { align-self: flex-start; }  /* راست در RTL */
     - .bubble.theirs{ align-self: flex-start; }
     + .bubble.theirs{ align-self: flex-end; }
     ```

### ساختار
```
dating-app/
├── server/   # Express + Socket.IO + SQLite
└── client/   # React (Vite) SPA
```

### اجرا
```bash
npm run install:all
cp server/.env.example server/.env   # JWT_SECRET را تنظیم کنید
npm run seed                          # کاربران دمو (رمز همه: password123)
npm run dev                           # client:5173  ·  server:4000
```

### تست
به‌صورت دستی در مرورگر تست شد: ثبت‌نام، سواایپ، نمایش پاپ‌آپ «مَچ شدید!»، ارسال پیام، دریافت بلادرنگ پاسخ از طرف مقابل، لیست مَچ‌ها و پروفایل — همه فارسی/RTL. `lint`، `typecheck` و `build` برای هر دو بسته سبز هستند.

### نکته
این یک پروژه‌ی نمونه/آموزشی است؛ برای استفاده‌ی واقعی موارد امنیتی (آپلود عکس، محدودیت نرخ، پاک‌سازی ورودی، HTTPS، refresh token) باید اضافه شوند.

author: b-j-karl
body:
## What & why

The project had **two competing R package mechanisms** wired in at once:

- a dated **PPM snapshot** (`sync_r_packages.R` + `DESCRIPTION` `Config/Repo/Snapshot`) installing into the **default library**, and
- **renv** (`renv.lock` + `activate.R`), which the pipeline scripts activate at runtime, pointing at the **renv project library**.

They targeted different libraries, so a fresh clone that followed the docs (`sync` → default lib) would break the moment the pipeline activated renv and switched to an empty project library. This consolidates on **renv as the single source of truth**.

## Changes

- `.Rprofile` activates renv unconditionally (standard renv), so plain `Rscript` (CI, interactive) uses the renv library too.
- `tests.yml` → `windows-latest` via `renv::restore` (`setup-renv`); Copilot Linux setup workflow removed. `renv::restore` deadlocks on `openxlsx`↔`zip` on Linux, so restore runs on Windows (the pipeline ships to Windows anyway).
- Installer build restores `renv.lock` into the bundled R library (cache disabled → real copies) instead of `sync`.
- Removed `sync_r_packages.R`, its test, and `Config/Repo/Snapshot`.
- Docs (README, usage, launcher) rewritten to renv-only.

## Verification

Local (Windows): R suite **624 pass / 0 fail**, launcher Pester **57 pass**, `renv::status()` consistent, `run_data.R --validate` exits 0. This PR triggers the `tests.yml` Windows CI run to confirm `renv::restore` on a clean runner.

> **Base note:** targeted at `feature/pipeline-launcher-gui` because this change depends on launcher-branch files; retarget to `develop` if preferred.

author: vedanthchamala
body:
## Problem
Tally was recording application stages that **never happened**. The flagged example was a phantom **IBM Interview** that the account holder never received. Cross-validating the classifier against the real inbox showed this is a *class* of bugs in the rules engine, not a one-off.

## Root cause
`classifyWithRules` assigns a stage by matching a single high-priority keyword **anywhere** in the email, first-match-by-priority. So:
- IBM's **assessment** invite — *"The next step in the **process** includes one or more assessments"* — matched an `interview` pattern, and because `interview` outranks `oa`, was filed as an **Interview**.
- An anti-fraud **newsletter** — *"the authenticity of your job **offer**"* — matched a bare `offer` pattern → phantom **Offer**.
- A "thank you for applying" **confirmation** — *"if you are **not selected**…"* — matched a `rejected` pattern → false **Rejected**.
- Role extraction captured sentence fragments (`"At IBM"`, `"Specific Requirements Of The"`), which fragmented one application into many cards.

On the real IBM mail this produced **5 junk cards** (incl. fake Interview + fake Offer) for **2 real applications**.

## Fix — one file, `src/lib/classifier.ts`
- **`detectStage`** is now evidence-based (the stage with the most pattern hits wins), but decisive terminal stages (rejected/offer) still override when genuinely present — so a rejection that *also* says "thanks for applying" isn't downgraded.
- **interview**: the "next step" pattern only matches interview-specific phrasing, not generic "next step in the process/application".
- **offer**: dropped bare `your job offer`; kept `your offer letter/details` + `congratulations … offer`; same tightening on the LLM offer-guard.
- **rejected**: requires a past-tense auxiliary, so a conditional "if you are not selected" in a confirmation isn't a rejection.
- **role extraction**: added an ATS requisition-line parser (`Ref: 58806 - AI Foundations - Software Engineer…`), strip leading prepositions, null a "role" that's just the company name, and raised the length cap so good long titles aren't dropped to a junk fallback.

## Validation (against real Gmail)
- **IBM** (21 emails): board now shows exactly **2 correct cards** — `OA · AI Foundations - Software Engineer - Research Internship` and `Rejected · Associate Developer Intern` — down from 5. 13/13 relevance + stage correct.
- **Non-IBM regression** (14 real funnel emails — Snowflake, Oracle, Palantir, TD, Turing, Western Union, General Dynamics, …): **12/14**. The 2 misses (a Turing OA, an ambiguous networking intro-call) are **pre-existing under-detections — identical on `main`** — and are *under-calls*, not invented statuses.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `classifier.ts` lint-clean. (The 2 lint errors in CI are pre-existing in `dashboard.tsx`, untouched here.)

## Notes / follow-ups (not in this PR)
- **Forward-only.** This fixes *future* syncs. Phantom cards already in the DB won't auto-correct — sync dedups by Gmail message id and never re-classifies stored events. They need manual cleanup or a one-time re-classify backfill.
- **Gemini.** The optional LLM pass would catch most of this, but it **silently falls back to rules on any failure**. Worth confirming it's actually active in Vercel (env vars in Production *and* Preview, valid key/quota) and adding a `console.warn` on failure.
- Pre-existing under-detection (Turing-style "complete your `<company>` assessment"; networking intro-calls) left for a follow-up.

TMDB is fetched with `&language=<PreferredLanguage>` → German overviews/titles where TMDB has them.

## Shikimori provider (no key)
Keyed by the MAL id every anime work already carries (priority 22 gap-filler): poster, genres, episode count. Its Russian synopsis is kept only as `OverviewTranslations["ru"]` — never the default overview.

## More cross-ids round-trip
AniSearch / Notify / LiveChart / Annict / Syobocal are now wired through all three id maps (stamp + resolve), so a work linked only to one of those is still resolvable.

## Settings expansion: per-source toggles
New **"Sources"** section on the config page to switch individual providers (AniList / Jikan / TMDB / Kitsu / fanart.tv / Shikimori / Annict) on or off. Backed by `Enable<Source>` config -> `EnrichmentOptions.DisabledSources` -> `EnrichmentService` skips disabled providers.

## Tests
Shikimori parse (real shape, RU→translation, host-prefixed poster). **176/176 green, 0 warnings**; Release build clean; config-page HTML verified well-formed.

author: alrubinger
body:
## Summary

`buildStartQueryExecution` (connector/helpers.go) only set `ClientRequestToken` when the caller supplied a non-empty one, otherwise omitting it. This connector hand-builds the AWS-JSON-1.1 body with **no AWS SDK**, so there is no client-side token auto-generation — Athena received a null token and rejected `StartQueryExecution` with `400 INVALID_INPUT "clientRequestToken is null or empty"`, breaking `run_query` and `start-query-execution` out of the box (the headline synchronous Flight Plan path).

Fix: when `client_request_token` is absent or empty, synthesize a deterministic pure-Go token = `hex(sha256(canonical request))`. The hash covers `QueryString` plus the execution context, result configuration, and work group, so the token is a true function of the request (avoids same-SQL/different-output-location collisions) and is reproducible on the `wasip1` target with no clock or randomness. A caller-supplied non-empty token is still honored verbatim (passthrough preserved). The 64-char hex token sits within Athena's 32-128 length bound and valid charset.

Because the token is now a deterministic function of the request, both actions flip to `idempotent = true` per ADR-0010 (identical requests carry the same token, so Athena collapses them onto a single execution rather than duplicating work). Docs and the README operations table updated to match.

### Changed
- `connector/helpers.go` — synthesize token via new `deriveClientRequestToken`; add `crypto/sha256` + `encoding/hex` imports; updated doc comment.
- `connector/helpers_test.go` — flipped the empty-optionals test to assert a 64-char hex token IS synthesized when absent (plus determinism + no-collision assertions); kept verbatim passthrough assertion; updated the minimal-body test (token is now always emitted).
- `actions/run-query/action.md`, `actions/start-query-execution/action.md` — `idempotent = true`, rewritten `client_request_token` input description and idempotency narrative.
- `README.md` — operations table + prose: `start_query_execution` and `run_query` now idempotent.

## Test plan
- `task test` (connector unit tests + wasip1 smoke build): PASS, coverage 96.8%.
- `gofmt -l` clean, `go vet` clean.
- New regression assertions fail against the old passthrough-only behavior (which omitted the token) and pass with the fix.

Closes #41

## What

Inverts `READ_LEGACY_FALLBACK` from opt-out (`!== 'false'`) to opt-in (`=== 'true'`). Default is now false. Customer-owned reads go exclusively to `tenants/{ctx.tenantId}/...`.

The data migration prerequisite was met on 2026-06-29 (Spec 031 / PR #35): 12 legacy `projects/` documents were copied into `tenants/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/projects/` via `pnpm migrate:legacy-projects --execute`.

## Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `apps/api/src/infrastructure/firestore/tenant-path.ts` | one-line inversion + extended comment |
| `apps/api/specs/033-flip-read-legacy-fallback/{spec,plan}.md` | NEW |

## Verification (manual, parallel API on :3105)

Fresh API with the flipped code, default flag (`READ_LEGACY_FALLBACK=false`), JWT with real userId from Firestore (`24748b1c-...`, role owner):

```
GET /projects -> 12 documents
[Umbral de Luna, Artefacto Backend, kundala000,
 Los documentos de Elias Montoya, Lingua Fractum,
 Cioran Diario, AI Orchestrator, Umbral Tone,
 Umbral Sur, Umbral Vision, Noosfera, Artefacto App]
```

Same data as before the flip — the user-perceived behaviour is unchanged.

## Reviewer note

Per ADR-004 §4: tenant path layout, requires explicit owner review before merge.

After merge, restart the user's local API (`pnpm dev:api`). `/projects` continues to work; the legacy top-level collection is now read-orphaned (write-orphaned? — no, dual-write is still on for new documents via `DUAL_WRITE_TENANT_PATHS=true` default).

If anything breaks in production (no production today), set `READ_LEGACY_FALLBACK=true` in the runtime env to re-enable the fallback, then investigate.

## Out of scope

- **Pruning the legacy top-level documents.** A separate spec, after a soak window (suggest 1 week of `READ_LEGACY_FALLBACK=false` in production) to confirm no consumer depends on the legacy reads.
- **Flipping `DUAL_WRITE_TENANT_PATHS=false`.** Separate concern.
- **Phase 4 strict (`TENANT_CLAIM_REQUIRED=true`).** ADR-005 §2/§3; separate rollout.

body:
## Summary

Enables `elsar` to drive **sub-national / regional** analyses (a custom boundary rather than a single ISO3 country) and makes raster outputs **valid Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs**. All changes are backward-compatible — standard national workflows behave exactly as before; the new behaviour is opt-in via parameters/inputs.

Motivated by migrating a standalone regional script (Ecuador GEF 8: El Oro / Loja / Zamora Chinchipe) onto the pipeline, which surfaced several places where the package assumed *one ≤3-char ISO3 country with WDPA-shaped data*.

## Changes

**Regional / custom-boundary support**
- **Accept regional ISO3 codes** (e.g. `ECU_REG`, `ECU-GEF8`). New internal `is_valid_iso3()` validator (3 letters + optional `[_-]`suffix) replaces the hard `nchar(iso3) == 3` assertions in `gee_helpers.R`, `utils.R`, `utils-elsa.R`, `make_kbas.R`, `make_threatened_ecosystems_restoration.R`. Standard 3-letter codes are unaffected.
- **`make_custom_projection()` tolerates `iso3 = NULL`** — previously `glue()` collapsed the WKT to length-zero, breaking `st_crs()`. Falls back to a generic label for the projection name/filename.
- **`make_boundary()` decouples filtering from projection** — new `filter_by_iso3` (default `TRUE`) and `dissolve` (default `FALSE`). Lets a custom regional boundary (no ISO3 column, possibly multiple features) be used whole and dissolved into one planning region, while still passing `iso3` for the projection name.
- **`make_protected_areas()` tolerates custom local PA layers** — `STATUS`/`SITE_TYPE`/designation filters now apply only when those columns exist, so a non-WDPA `sf` (e.g. a national SNAP shapefile) no longer errors with `.data$STATUS %in% status`. WDPCA downloads are unchanged.

**Output / COG correctness**
- **`save_raster()` now builds overviews** (`OVERVIEWS=AUTO`) so outputs are conformant COGs accepted by strict readers/servers (rio-cogeo, TiTiler). Previously `OVERVIEWS=NONE` produced files those tools reject.
- **Overview resampling is data-type aware and overridable** — `AVERAGE` for float, `NEAREST` for integer, with a new `resampling` argument so categorical layers (e.g. land cover) can pass `"mode"` to keep the dominant class.

## Backward compatibility
- New `make_boundary` args default to current behaviour (`filter_by_iso3 = TRUE`, `dissolve = FALSE`).
- New `save_raster` arg defaults to current resampling; the only behavioural change is that overviews are now written (intended fix).
- ISO3 validation only *relaxes* — every previously-valid 3-letter code still passes.

## Testing
- `devtools::load_all()` clean.
- `save_raster()` writes COGs with overviews confirmed via `describe()` for both float (AVERAGE) and integer (MODE).
- `make_protected_areas(from_wdpca = FALSE)` on a column-less polygon layer returns a raster without error.
- `make_boundary(filter_by_iso3 = FALSE, dissolve = TRUE)` on a multi-feature boundary returns a single projected geometry; `make_custom_projection(iso3 = NULL)` returns a valid WKT.
- Rd docs hand-synced for the changed signatures (repo `RoxygenNote` 7.3.3; not regenerated with the locally-installed 8.0.0 to avoid a mass reformat).

author: tolldog
body:
Fixes the multi-source provenance limitation tracked in `bug_khonliang-researcher_a905176b` (surfaced by PR khonliang-researcher#58 — blog triple extraction).

## Problem
`TripleStore` held one `source` per (subject,predicate,object) and overwrote it on re-add. When two contributors asserted the same fact, `strike()` was order-dependent (removing the recorded source dropped a triple others still supported), and confidence collapsed to a single `max()` with no way to lower it on retraction.

## Change — per-source provenance
- **`triple_sources(triple_id, source, confidence)`** side-table is the source of truth; `triples.source` (newline-joined tokens) and `triples.confidence` (max over sources) stay as **backward-compatible denormalized caches**. Invariant: every triple has ≥1 source row (anonymous adds get a `""` row).
- **`add()`** unions sources, each keeping its own max confidence (no more overwrite).
- **`remove_source(s,p,o,source)`** drops one contributor, recomputes confidence from survivors, deletes the triple only when none remain — and does **not** reset the decay clock.
- **`apply_decay()`** decays the authoritative per-source confidences so decay persists across later recomputes; `remove()`/decay prune orphan rows.
- **Additive backfill migration** seeds rows for legacy triples on first open (idempotent). `Triple.sources` exposes the parsed token list; `.source` unchanged for single-source rows.

## Review & tests
- Cross-vendor: `codex review` (codex-auto-review) — converged clean over several passes (per-source confidence, decay persistence, anonymous-evidence preservation).
- 12 new tests; full suite **517 passed** (2 pre-existing `test_reporting` markdown-sanitizer failures are unrelated — they fail on clean main too).

Follow-up: a researcher-side PR will consume `remove_source` in `strike()`/ingest and drop the interim skip-if-exists mitigation, closing the bug.

body:
### Checklist

The following lists affects Pub Points on pub.dev when the package is published.
* [ ] Passed the all tests.
* [ ] Verified that the example app works.
* [ ] Executed the `dart format` command.
* [ ] Added the API description is added if necessary.

## Summary
A POSIX/undetermined platform locale crashed Persian (equinox) date formatting,
and the active locale wasn't normalized consistently. This normalizes such
locales to `en-US` everywhere and makes the astronomical data locale-independent.

## Problem
- On some platforms the device locale resolves to `C`/`POSIX` (Linux desktop) or
  `und` (undetermined — common on embedders like webOS).
- That value flowed into `currentLocale` un-normalized, so `ILibAstro._getData()`
  fetched `ilib.data.astro` via `getLocaleData(currentLocale)`, got no data, and
  **cached the empty result permanently** → every Persian/equinox calc then threw
  `null as List` in `ILibAstro.equinox`.

## Changes
- **`ilib_utils`**: add `normalizeLocale()` mapping `C`/`POSIX`/`und`/empty/`null`
  → `en-US` (only bare `und`; `und-US`/`und-Hans` fallbacks preserved). Make
  `currentLocale` a getter/setter so every read/write is normalized — no code
  path (init, `setLocale`, direct assignment) can observe `C`/`und`.
- **`ilib_init`**: apply `normalizeLocale` in `loadJSON` / `loadILibLocaleData`
  (so an undetermined/POSIX locale loads `en-US`, not root-only data); add a
  `getRootData()` accessor + `_rootPath` constant.
- **`ilib_astro`**: read `ilib.data.astro` from `ILibLoader.getRootData()`
  (root.json, locale-independent) instead of `getLocaleData(currentLocale)`, and
  never cache an empty map so a too-early call can recover.

## Tests
- `flutter_ilib_utils_test`: `normalizeLocale` (C/POSIX/und/empty/null → en-US;
  und-US/und-Hans preserved) and `currentLocale` always-normalized.
- `testastro_extra_test` (new): `getRootData()` exposes astro coefficients;
  `equinox()` resolves astro from root regardless of the active locale.

## Verification
`flutter analyze` clean; astro / Persian / utils test suites pass.

body:
…shapes, add SE Asia

Follow-ups from playtest feedback on the Ancient-World growth frontiers.

1) Neutral frontiers are now attackable from bordering territories.
   The backend already lets you capture a neutral garrison in era-advancement
   games (executeLandAttack carve-out), but the attack UI filtered out unowned
   neighbors — so a bordering frontier showed no attack button and was
   unreachable. computePhaseAdjacencyTargets now offers neutral neighbors as
   attack targets when era_advancement_enabled (world-scoped callers still pass a
   territoryFilter, so off-world Moon/galaxy neutrals keep their access race).
   Also wired the connections the frontiers were missing: Scandinavia↔Britannia,
   Volga↔Pontic Steppe, Volga↔Scandinavia.

2) Volga Bulgaria and the Sahara now use real geometry instead of blocks.
   - Volga: real central/European-Russia geometry, bounded by Russia's actual borders with the Baltic/Belarus/Ukraine/Kazakhstan so it fills the gap between Scandinavia, Sarmatia, the Pontic Steppe and the Central Steppe.
   - Sahara: a natural desert band — Sudan fills the gap between Egypt and Aksum, and the northern deserts of Mauritania/Mali/Niger (carved from West Africa) and Chad (carved from Central Africa) give it shape. West/Central Africa are clipped to their southern halves at the SAME boundary latitudes, so the carve is seamless (no gaps/overlaps).

3) New "Southeast Asia" frontier on the Ancient board (unlocks at the Medieval
   era, like Scandinavia/Volga/Sahara). Real mainland-Indochina geometry
   (Myanmar/Thailand/Laos/Cambodia/Vietnam), its own region (bonus 2), connected
   to southern China, southern India and (once it unlocks) Nusantara. Uses a
   distinct territory id (`indochina`) so it never collides with the maritime
   `southeast_asia` territory on the Medieval map or the Ancient `nusantara`.

author: bluebugs
body:
Phase 4b adds the **J4 (J-core) family** to the LLVM SH MC backend, completing **full non-DSP coverage** of `docs/insns.json`: after this, the only excluded instructions are the DSP family.

### Coverage added (J4-only, `HasJ4`)
- `ldtlb.rn` (`0x0078`)
- `stc {pteh,ptel,asidr,tsbptr},Rn` (`0x0053/0x0063/0x0073/0x0043`)

### Mechanism
- **Lowercase normalization:** the J4 rows carry uppercase mnemonics (`STC`, `LDTLB.RN`) in `insns.json`; `ir.CanonMnemonic` now lowercases (then alias-normalizes), so the backend emits canonical lowercase AsmStrings — matching the gas track and LLVM convention.
- **Control regs as literal tokens:** `pteh/ptel/asidr/tsbptr` added to the parser's `SpecialRegs[]` (like `sgr/dbr`), no new registers.
- **Encoding-collision handling:** `stc ptel` (`0x0063`) and `stc asidr` (`0x0073`) reuse SH4A `movli.l`/`movco.l` encodings. The generator now emits `isAsmParserOnly=1` for a J-core-only instruction whose fixed bit-pattern collides with an emitted standard-SH instruction (driven by the `collides` field + a position-aware `fixedBitPattern`), so the SH4A instruction keeps the disassembler slot and there is no decode conflict. Encoding-aware: `ldtlb.rn`'s `collides:['nott']` is at a different opcode, so it is correctly NOT marked.

## Summary

author: felipefuhr
body:
## What & why

Part of the ffreis.com **content-mocks + extended-languages** effort (plan: \`jiggly-twirling-prism\`). The dev site will carry content declaring languages the site does **not** render (e.g. \`de\`, \`ja\`) for realistic variance. Today \`ValidatePostLangs\` (#76) hard-fails the build on any \`available_languages\` code outside the rendered \`language_variants\` set, so such content can't exist.

This introduces a **content-language superset**: rendered languages (\`language_variants\`) ∪ \`content_languages\`. Codes in that set are first-class; codes outside it (a typo like \`br\` for \`pt\`) still fail the build — the #76 guard is preserved, just widened.

## Changes

- \`allowedContentLangs(siteData)\` — new superset helper; \`knownLangPrefixes\` renamed to \`renderedLangPrefixes\` (the set the site actually builds pages for).
- \`ValidatePostLangs\` validates against the superset; allows content-only \`de\`/\`ja\`, rejects true typos.
- **Latent-bug fix:** \`redirectTarget\` now only ever redirects to a *rendered* language. A \`de\`/\`ja\`-only item previously redirected to a non-existent \`/de/\` route; it now falls back to the language home via the existing empty-target path.
- New \`internal/buildcmd/langutil_test.go\` covering the superset, content-only allowance, typo rejection, and rendered-only redirect targets.

## Backward compatibility

With no \`content_languages\` key in site data, \`allowedContentLangs\` falls back to the rendered set — identical to the prior strict behaviour. The companion \`content_languages: [en, pt, de, ja]\` data key lands in a separate \`ffreis-website-data\` PR.

## Testing

- \`go test -race -shuffle=on ./internal/buildcmd/ ./internal/posts/ ./internal/courses/\` — green
- \`gofmt -l\`, \`go vet\`, \`golangci-lint run\` — clean (0 issues)

author: geromegrignon
body:
DatePicker rebuilt its month model whenever minDate or maxDate received a new Date object, even when the timestamp was unchanged.

Getter-backed bindings such as [minDate]="today" can create a fresh Date during every change detection pass. In inline desktop mode that DOM churn can replace the month navigation button between pointer events and prevent the arrow click from navigating.

Compare previous and incoming date bounds by timestamp before recreating months, while preserving rebuilds for real minDate and maxDate changes.

Add regression coverage for inline range DatePicker with a getter-backed minDate to verify equivalent date inputs do not recreate months or replace the next navigation button.

Fixes primefaces/primeng#19562

### Defect Fixes
When submitting a PR, please also <ins>**create an issue**</ins> documenting the error and [manually link to an issue](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue#manually-linking-a-pull-request-or-branch-to-an-issue-using-the-issue-sidebar).

Due to company policy, we are unable to accept feature request PRs with significant changes as such cases has to be implemented by our team following our own processes.

## Summary

Closes the upper-bound execution loop: **paper → strategy → backtest → live signal → on-chain trade**. The "Place Trade" button on /dashboard/execution now wires to a real \`openTrade\` call against the GNSMultiCollatDiamond on Base mainnet, signed client-side via MetaMask. The server never holds keys.

## Stack
- \`viem\` for ABI encoding (~+200KB to package-lock)
- MetaMask via \`window.ethereum\` — client-side signing only
- Native USDC on Base as collateral (6 decimals)

## Module — \`lib/execution/gtrade.ts\`

- BASE_MAINNET network config + \`ensureBaseMainnet\` helper (switch or add)
- USDC allowance + balance reads via \`eth_call\`
- \`sendUsdcApprove\` (ERC-20 approve to the Diamond)
- \`sendOpenTrade\` (encodes the Trade struct + maxSlippageP and submits)
- \`positionSizeUsd\` / \`dollarsPerPoint\` UI preview helpers

### Verified constants

Pulled live from \`https://backend-base.gains.trade/trading-variables\` on 2026-06-30:

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Trading Diamond | \`0x6cD5aC19a07518A8092eEFfDA4f1174C72704eeb\` |
| USDC (Circle on Base) | \`0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913\` |
| collateralIndex for USDC | \`1\` |
| DIA/USD pairIndex | \`89\` |
| Max leverage | \`100×\` |

## ExecutionClient UI changes

- Network indicator + **Switch to Base** button (replaces the prior Arbitrum Sepolia stub)
- USDC balance row when wallet is on Base
- Trade panel (only when signal != HOLD):
  - Collateral USDC (default \$5, min \$1, max \$100)
  - Leverage (default 5×, range 2× – 100×)
  - Slippage tolerance % (default 1.0)
  - Override entry price input
  - Position size + \$/point + max loss preview
  - Single button that: checks allowance → approves if needed → polls until visible → calls openTrade
  - Basescan link on both approve and openTrade transactions

### ^DJI ↔ DIA scale handling

The strategy prices signals in ^DJI index value (~38000). gTrade's DIA pair tracks the DIA ETF (~\$380). They differ by ~100×. The trade panel auto-divides ^DJI prices by 100 before encoding, and surfaces a note to the user. Other tickers pass through unchanged.

## Risk surface for the demo

Real USDC. Per-trade financial risk is bounded by collateral — at default settings (\$5 collateral, 5× leverage), one trade caps at \$5 max loss. Gas on Base is sub-cent. At \$5 × 5× = \$25 notional, 1 point on DIA at ~\$380 ≈ \$0.066/point.

body:
## Summary

- **Fix 1 — Webhook secret lost on reconnect** (`routes/jira/oauth.ts`): `onConflictDoUpdate.set` was missing `webhookSecret`, so reconnecting Jira silently kept the old secret in the DB while registering a new one with Atlassian, breaking all subsequent webhook signature checks.
- **Fix 2 — Status history dedup** (`db/schema/jira.ts` + `lib/jira/sync.ts`): Added a unique constraint on `jira_status_history(ticket_id, changed_at, to_status)` and wired it as the conflict target in `onConflictDoNothing`, so repeated syncs no longer insert duplicate history rows. Migration generated (`0001_amazing_stick.sql`).
- **Fix 3 — Cycle time always 0** (`lib/jira/sync.ts`): `toStatusCategory` was set to the ticket's current status for every historical row. Added `deriveStatusCategory()` heuristic on `item.toString` so each row reflects the status it transitioned to, enabling accurate cycle time calculations.
- **Fix 4 — Rate-limit retry** (`lib/jira/client.ts`): `get`, `post`, and `getAgile` now use `fetchWithRetry()` which retries on HTTP 429 with exponential back-off (up to 3 retries, respecting `Retry-After`), preventing a single rate-limit response from failing an entire SQS message.
- **Fix 5 — Token refresh race condition** (`lib/jira/client.ts`): `getValidToken` now uses an optimistic lock — it only updates the DB token if `accessToken` still matches what it read. If a concurrent Lambda refreshed first, it re-reads and uses the fresh token, avoiding Atlassian's single-use refresh token failures.
- **Fix 6 — Throughput undercounts tickets** (`lib/metrics/tickets.ts`): Throughput now falls back to the earliest "Done" status-history transition date for tickets that lack a `resolutiondate`, eliminating the silent undercount.
- **Fix 7 — sprint_created webhook no-op** (`lib/jira/sync.ts`): `handleSprintEvent` used to return early if the sprint didn't exist in the DB. It now inserts the sprint on `sprint_created` events by looking up the project via `originBoardId`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Typecheck: `pnpm typecheck` — passes
- [ ] Lint: `pnpm lint` — passes
- [ ] Tests: `pnpm test` — 99 passed, 1 expected fail (org membership gap tracked separately)

## Summary
- Avoid building the full daily summary list in memory when writing viewer output from `30_route_performance.py`.
- Write viewer data directly as lightweight route geometry JSON plus per-date/hour summary shards during analysis.
- Add streaming conversion for old large `*_viewer.json` files so `30-2_route_performance_viewer.py` can rebuild a viewer without loading the full summary array at once.

## Why
The user launches `30-2_route_performance_viewer.py`, but that viewer imports `30_route_performance.py` and calls `build_viewer_from_output()`. The previous PR improved the browser-side loading format, but old existing large JSON still had to be parsed by Python during rebuild, and fresh analysis still briefly built a large summary list before sharding.

## File roles
- `30_route_performance.py`: core analyzer and viewer HTML/data generator. This is where the data format must be optimized.
- `30_UI_route_performance.py`: analysis UI. It imports `30_route_performance.py`, so re-running analysis through this UI uses the optimized output writer.
- `30-2_route_performance_viewer.py`: viewer launcher. It imports `30_route_performance.py` and rebuilds the HTML from an existing `30_route_performance` output folder.

## Validation
- Ran Python syntax compilation with `py_compile`.
- Built a sample viewer from an old-style JSON payload and verified it was converted to a slim route JSON plus date/hour summary shards.
- Ran `git diff --check`.

## Notes
For the best result on very large datasets, re-run analysis so the output is written in the optimized sharded format from the start. The standalone viewer also has a streaming fallback for old-format outputs.

author: newhoggy
body:
## Description

This PR eliminates the cross-module environment-variable race condition (issue #821) in `claude::context::discovery` by applying dependency injection (STYLE-0028) to all functions that previously read `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `OMNI_DEV_CONFIG_DIR` directly from the process environment.

Each env-reading function is split into a thin public wrapper that passes `&SystemEnv` and `dirs::home_dir()`, and a pure inner seam that accepts `env: &impl EnvSource` and `home: Option<&Path>` as parameters. The public API is completely unchanged, so all CLI/git callers are untouched.

The root cause of the race was that tests in the discovery module mutated `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `OMNI_DEV_CONFIG_DIR` via `std::env::set_var`, but those writes raced against `AUTH_ENV_MUTEX` in a different module that also locked over the same process-global vars. After this change, `OMNI_DEV_CONFIG_DIR` has **zero** writers across the entire codebase and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` has a single writer behind one canonical lock, making the module fully lock-free.

Verified: 56/56 discovery tests pass, clippy clean, 10× full parallel `cargo test` green (5337 tests/run).

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [x] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [x] Test coverage improvement
- [ ] CI/CD changes
- [ ] Dependency update

## Related Issue
Fixes #821
Relates to #1030

## Changes Made

**Core Changes (`src/claude/context/discovery.rs`):**
- Split `xdg_config_dir()` into a thin wrapper and pure inner seam `xdg_config_dir_with(env: &impl EnvSource, home: Option<&Path>)`
- Split `resolve_config_file()` into a thin wrapper delegating to `resolve_config_file_with(dir, filename, env, home)`
- Split `config_source_label()` into a thin wrapper delegating to `config_source_label_with(dir, filename, env, home)`
- Split `resolve_context_dir_with_source()` into a thin wrapper delegating to `resolve_context_dir_with_source_env(override_dir, env)`
- Split `resolve_context_dir_with_source_at()` into a thin wrapper delegating to `resolve_context_dir_with_source_at_env(override_dir, repo_root, env)`
- All public function signatures remain unchanged; callers pass `&SystemEnv` and `dirs::home_dir()` in production
- Added `use crate::utils::env::{EnvSource, SystemEnv}` import

**Testing:**
- Deleted `static ENV_MUTEX: std::sync::Mutex<()>` that previously serialized 18 tests touching `OMNI_DEV_CONFIG_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`
- Replaced all `std::env::set_var` / `std::env::remove_var` calls with `MapEnv::new().with("KEY", "value")` injected into inner seams
- Added `xdg_env(path: &Path) -> MapEnv` test helper to build an env pointing `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` at a temp dir
- Updated all affected tests to call `*_env` / `*_with` inner seam functions directly
- All 18 formerly serialized tests now run fully in parallel with no locks

## Testing

**Automated Testing:**
- [x] All existing tests pass (56/56 discovery tests, 5337 tests total)
- [x] New tests added for new functionality (inner seam functions covered by refactored tests)
- [x] Integration tests updated/added
- [ ] Performance tests (if applicable)

**Manual Testing:**
- [x] Tested happy path scenarios
- [x] Tested error/edge cases (empty env vars, missing home dir, CLI flag overrides)
- [ ] Cross-platform testing (if applicable)
- [x] Backward compatibility verified (public API is unchanged)

### Test Commands
```bash
# Core test suite — run in parallel to exercise the lock-free behaviour
cargo test

# Run discovery-specific tests
cargo test claude::context::discovery

# Code quality checks
cargo clippy -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check

# Stress-test for races (run 10x as done in verification)
for i in $(seq 1 10); do cargo test; done
```

## Review Focus Areas

**Please pay special attention to:**
- [x] Architecture changes — the seam pattern (STYLE-0028) applied consistently across all five functions
- [x] Backward compatibility — public signatures are thin wrappers; confirm no callers were broken
- [ ] Security implications
- [ ] Performance impact
- [ ] Error handling
- [ ] User experience

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
- [ ] Any dependent changes have been merged and published
- [x] I have read and followed the [PR Guidelines](../.omni-dev/pr-guidelines.md)

## Performance Impact
- [ ] No performance impact
- [x] Performance improvement (describe below)
- [ ] Potential performance impact (describe below)

The `static ENV_MUTEX` previously forced all 18 env-related discovery tests to run serially. Removing it allows full parallel test execution, reducing test wall-clock time for this module.

## Security Considerations
- [x] No security implications

The change is purely structural. No secrets, tokens, or authentication paths are involved. The same environment variables (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `OMNI_DEV_CONFIG_DIR`) are read; they are simply sourced through an injected `EnvSource` trait rather than `std::env::var` directly.

## Breaking Changes

None. All public function signatures (`resolve_config_file`, `resolve_context_dir_with_source`, `resolve_context_dir_with_source_at`, `config_source_label`) are unchanged. The inner seam functions (`*_with`, `*_env`) are private.

## Deployment Notes
- [x] No special deployment requirements

## Additional Notes

**Future Enhancements:**
- The `EnvSource` / `MapEnv` injection pattern established here (STYLE-0028) can be applied to other modules that still use `std::env::var` directly in test-covered paths, particularly any remaining callers that hold mutex locks over process-env mutations.

**Known Limitations:**
- The CWD walk-up tier in `resolve_context_dir_with_source_env` still consults the (read-only) process working directory; this is intentional and safe since no test mutates CWD.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- Unifying all env-related tests under a single global mutex: rejected because it would still serialize tests across modules and would not address the fundamental cross-module lock ordering issue.
- Using `std::env::set_var` with a per-module mutex and accepting the risk: rejected because the EACCES race on PR #1014 demonstrated real failures under parallel test execution.

body:
Replaces hardcoded light-mode colors in `scss/dropdown-checklist.scss` with Bootstrap CSS custom properties so the filter dropdown renders correctly in night mode.

## Problem
The `.checkbox-menu` styles used literal hex values:
- `background-color: #fff` — renders as a bright white rectangle in dark mode
- `color: #333` — near-black text that may clash with a dark background
- hover/focus `background-color: #f5f5f5` — same issue

These values were set unconditionally, so night mode had no way to override them.

- Replaces `#fff` with `var(--bs-body-bg)`.
- Replaces `#333` with `var(--bs-body-color)`.
- Replaces `#f5f5f5` hover background with `var(--bs-tertiary-bg)`.

## Risk & testing
Bootstrap's default light-mode values for these variables match the original hex literals, so there is no visual change in the default theme. Night mode behavior was verified to render correctly. No JavaScript is touched.

author: dgaffney
body:
## Summary

Fixes #141.

A user went through machine onboarding, picked `mlx-community/gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit`, and hit **"Provisioning failed"** — the machine came online but only served the no-op `stub` engine.

The reported error message is the right one (the runtime already classifies this case as `model-multimodal-incompatible`):

> The model(s) [mlx-community/gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit] couldn't load: this looks like a merged or multimodal checkpoint whose weights are nested (e.g. under `language_model.*`), which the runtime can't map onto a text model…

The real defect is that the model was **offered in the picker at all**. `gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit` is a merged/multimodal ("E4B") checkpoint whose tensors live under `language_model.*`; the provider's text runtime can't key-map those onto its module tree, so loading it always fails. It can never be served as a text model — yet it was listed as a *recommended* rotation entry.

## Changes

Removed the entry from all three places that surface the curated catalog:

- `provider/src/pricing.rs` — the Rust `RATES` table (source of truth)
- `packages/console/src/lib/recommended-models.ts` — the TS mirror served via `/v1/recommended-models`
- `provider-shell/Sources/CoCoreShell/ModelsView.swift` — the menu-bar app's offline fallback catalog

Each site keeps a short comment explaining why it was removed and that only standard MLX **text** models belong in the rotation.

Removed entirely rather than demoted to the "legacy (still servable)" tier — legacy entries are by definition still servable, and this checkpoint is not servable at all. Any machine that had already pinned it was stub-only anyway, so dropping its catalog price/RAM-floor entry is harmless.

## Testing

- `cargo test --lib pricing` — all 15 pricing tests pass (including `recommended_set_is_the_rotation`).
- No test referenced the removed id; no hardcoded catalog counts to update.

## Summary

Replaces Portkey OSS with [agentgateway](https://github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway) as the data plane and ships it as a clean v0.1 reference solution. The control plane (gwcore Lambdas, DynamoDB, Cognito, Firehose to Iceberg) and the identity layer are unchanged; the swap is contained to the data-plane container, the rendered agentgateway config, and the integration seams. 17 commits, +2,878 / -4,604 (net ~1,700 lines removed).

See **ADR-017** for the full decision record.

## What changed

- **Data plane** is the pinned upstream agentgateway image (`v1.3.1`, digest-pinned multi-arch), re-tagged into ECR. The Node/npm Portkey build and its CVE-patch apparatus are gone.
- **Config** is a YAML file delivered inline via `-c`, rendered from `agentgateway-config.yaml.tftpl`: `ai.groups` priority-group failover (Bedrock primary, Anthropic fallback), `modelAliases`, native prompt caching on the Bedrock path, the `budget_enforcement` webhook, and inline Bedrock Guardrails (detect/log-only by default).

author: xpoes123
body:
Adds an in-process cache to the SSI middleware so each HTML page is read from disk and string-substituted only once per server lifetime instead of on every request.

## Problem
`routes/ssi-middleware.js` called `fs.readFile` and ran two `String.replace` operations on every page view. Because the HTML files and SSI partials (`head.html`, `nav.html`) are static between deploys, this work is entirely redundant after the first hit per path.

## Changes
- Introduces a `Map` keyed by resolved file path.
- On a cache hit, returns the pre-rendered string directly with `res.send`.
- On a miss, reads the file, applies SSI substitutions, stores the result, and responds as before.
- Errors (file not found, etc.) fall through to `next()` unchanged and are never cached.

## Risk & testing
The cache is populated lazily and is scoped to the server process lifetime, so a deploy naturally clears it. Error paths are unaffected. The directory-traversal guard runs before the cache lookup, so that protection is preserved. `node --check` passes.

author: eemlis7-ke
body:
Closes #439.

## Problem

`MediaLightbox` could zoom in but had no way to see the parts that scrolled out of view — the wrapping container is `overflow-hidden` and there was no pan state or pointer handlers. `draggable={false}` even disabled the only native fallback. KeEem hit this while pixel-peeping the full-resolution cold-test screenshots.

## Fix

Adds pointer-driven pan with the minimal surface area needed:

- `translate` state `(x, y)` composes with `scale`/`rotate` in the inline transform.
- `onPointerDown` captures the pointer and snapshots the origin; `onPointerMove` updates translate; `onPointerUp` / `onPointerCancel` release the capture.
- `canPan = scale > 1 && !fitWidth` — at fit-to-frame there's no off-screen content, so panning would just expose empty bands.
- Cursor flips between `grab` ⇄ `grabbing` while `canPan`.
- `touchAction: 'none'` is only applied while `canPan`, so the lightbox can still let touch users swipe past it at scale 1.
- The CSS `transition-transform` is dropped mid-drag — 60+ updates per second through an ease curve would feel "swimmy".
- Translate resets to 0 whenever the image returns to scale ≤ 1, on rotate, on fit-width toggle, on Reset, and on asset / open change.

No new props, no variant key change, no SSOT impact beyond the source file.

## Verified
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm run design:verify` passes
- [x] `npm run build` succeeds (`/cold-tests/[round]` SSGs 170 pages with the updated lightbox bundled)
- [x] Local: at scale > 1 the image element gets `cursor: grab`, `touch-action: none`, and `transform: translate(...) scale(...) rotate(...)`; at scale 1 those revert and the cursor / touch handling go back to defaults.

author: psenna
body:
Closes #2

## What

M1 passthrough skeleton: a smart-HTTP proxy that terminates the agent's git
traffic and reverse-proxies `upload-pack`/`receive-pack` byte streams to a
configured upstream git server, with **no policy yet**. It also introduces the
reusable integration test harness (`test/integration/harness.go`) that every
later milestone extends.

## Files

- `internal/port/{transport,gitconn,upstream}.go` — `Transport`, `GitConn`,
  `Upstream` interfaces (the extensibility seams).
- `internal/config/config.go` — YAML config (listen, upstream URL, repo map)
  with validation; defaults to deny on missing required fields.
- `internal/upstream/plain/plain.go` — `port.Upstream` impl against a plain git
  HTTP server. POST bodies are buffered to set an explicit `Content-Length`
  (git http-backend over CGI rejects chunked request bodies).
- `internal/gitproto/proxy.go` — streams upload-pack/receive-pack bytes through
  without inspection (Task 3 inserts inspection here).
- `internal/transport/http/frontend.go` — routes the three smart-HTTP endpoints;
  `/info/refs` is reverse-proxied (preserves the service query), the two POST
  endpoints stream through the gitproto Proxy. gzip request bodies are
  decompressed so the upstream receives raw git protocol. Implements
  `port.Transport` with ctx-driven graceful shutdown.
- `cmd/git-proxy/main.go` — wires config → plain upstream → frontend, with
  SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown.
- `test/integration/{harness.go,passthrough_test.go}` — reusable harness + real-git
  clone/push/fetch tests.

## Integration harness

The harness stands up a real upstream git HTTP server by serving
`git http-backend` over `net/http/cgi` behind `httptest.NewServer`, backed by a
bare repo in `t.TempDir` (`http.receivepack=true` enables push). The proxy runs
on an ephemeral listener. The real `git` client routes through the proxy via
`git -c url.<proxyURL>.insteadOf=<upstreamURL>`. Tests verify clone, push, and
fetch work through the proxy and that pushes reach the upstream bare repo
(checked directly via the filesystem).

## TDD

Red: the integration test was written first and failed to compile (the
`internal/transport/http` and `internal/upstream/plain` packages did not exist
yet). Green: implemented config → plain → gitproto → frontend → main wiring
until all three real-git tests passed.

## Local verification (all five CI commands green)

```
go vet ./...              # ok
go build ./...            # ok
go test -race ./...       # ok (config unit tests + integration clone/push/fetch)
golangci-lint run         # ok (no issues)
govulncheck ./...         # No vulnerabilities found.
```

## Commits

Seven Conventional Commits, one logical change each, every commit keeps the
build green.

body:
## Summary

The reviewed **design pass for RTR-1** — the `register_nodus_workflow` registration surface that lets apps register/select Nodus workflows **by name, at boot, without editing runtime**. New doc `docs/runtime/NODUS_WORKFLOW_CONTRACT.md`; implementation follows in a separate PR against this contract.

Design grounded in three code-mapping passes of the live tree (2026-06-29); every claim cites `file:symbol`.

## Key design decisions
- **Persist `.nd` source, recompile on register + boot.** Sidesteps the in-memory condition-closure serialization wall that `compile_nodus_flow` / `register_dynamic_flow` hit today (closures "are not serialised to the database"). Source is the durable, versioned artifact; the compiled flow is ephemeral cache.
- **Mirrors the canonical extension pattern** (manifest → `bootstrap()` → `registry.register_*`, owner-class gated). Reference: `runtime_agent_defaults.register()`. Two entry points: imperative `register_nodus_workflow()` + declarative `nodus-workflow` manifest kind (alongside the existing `dynamic-node`/`webhook-subscription`/`dynamic-flow` kinds).
- **Both kinds in Phase 1** (per design review): `flow-graph` (multi-node `flow.step()` DAG) and `script` (arbitrary `.nodus` via `nodus.execute`).
- **New `nodus_workflows` table** (source/version/content_hash) → schema-contract bump + Alembic `0006`; boot rehydration recompiles active rows into `FLOW_REGISTRY`.
- **Consolidation, not a 4th mechanism:** subsumes `nodus_script_store` (adds versioning), folds in `compile_nodus_flow`, coexists with `register_dynamic_flow` (data-only DAGs).
- **Reuses the canonical execution path** (`PersistentFlowRunner` → `FlowRun` + `SystemEvent`); no new execution machinery.

## Phasing
- **P1 (next PR):** surface + table + rehydration + run-by-name + tests.
- **P2:** agent-plan → `.nd` mapping + VM-backed agent adapter (retires the `AGENT_FLOW` shim).
- **P3:** content-hash bytecode cache; `NodusTraceEvent` wire-or-drop.

## Files
- `docs/runtime/NODUS_WORKFLOW_CONTRACT.md` (new; full 5-key frontmatter for CI).
- `TECH_DEBT.md` — RTR-1 links the contract.
- `docs/runtime/RUNTIME_DOC_INDEX.md` — doc listed under "Developers writing Nodus scripts."

Docs-only; no code paths touched.
