author: slauger
body:
## Problem

The pre-download dedup matched only `(name, version, arch)` and short-circuited (`continue`) **without comparing the upstream `C:` control checksum**. apk package identity is the **control checksum**, not name+version — so when upstream **replaced a package's bytes keeping the same version string** (a rebuild that didn't bump `-rN`), chantal kept serving the **stale** package and never re-downloaded.

## Fix

Require the `C:` checksum to match for the skip. When it differs (a content replacement), unlink the superseded package from this repository and fall through to download the new bytes — so the published APKINDEX keeps exactly one current entry per name+version+arch.

## Test

A same-version sync with a new `C:` re-downloads and replaces the stale package (it was skipped without the fix).

author: jessebeard
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability:
Unsanitized URLs provided to `window.open` in VaultView could execute malicious scripts if an attacker supplied protocols like `javascript:` (with bypass techniques like spaced protocols `j a v a s c r i p t :` or prepended control characters).
🎯 Impact:
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). An attacker could craft an entry with a malicious URL that executes arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the user's application when the 'Launch' button is clicked.
🔧 Fix:
Implemented a robust `sanitizeUrl` method that strips control characters. It specifically strips space characters just for protocol checking (via `new URL()`) to accurately detect malicious protocols (`javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`) without failing on standard whitespace obfuscation.
🧪 Security Test:
Added `test/security/url-sanitization.test.js` which includes Property-Based Testing (PBT) to assert that arbitrary strings can never be parsed as malicious protocols.
✅ Verification:
All tests pass (`node test/runner.js`). Verified property tests successfully shrink and catch bypasses.

author: erikfrerejean
body:
## What & why

`GridController` exposed pairs of routes that were essentially one operation parametrised by data, forcing the frontend to pick between endpoints. This unifies them at the wire boundary so the frontend posts discriminating data instead.

Two merges (the rest of the route pairs were deliberately left alone — see below):

### 1. `publish` + `unpublish` → `PATCH api/setPublished`
- Body `{ element: NodeRef, published: boolean }`.
- One action branches on `published`: `true` → `canPublish()` + `publishRecursive()`; `false` → `canUnpublish()` + `doUnpublish()`. Permission difference is intrinsic to the state transition, so this is one behaviour parametrised by data, not two behaviours behind a flag.

### 2. `create` + `createContent` → `POST api/create`
- Presence-based discriminator: `containerType` → container path, `className` → content path; both-present or neither → `400`.
- `apiCreate` is a thin dispatcher delegating to private `createContainer()` / `createContent()` helpers. Both `RequestBodyParser` validation paths are kept intact behind the endpoint — the frontend never learns there are two flows.

### Frontend
- `publishElement` / `unpublishElement` / `createContentElement` repointed to the new endpoints. Names and signatures are unchanged, so hooks, components, and E2E specs needed no code changes (only test-assertion updates).
- `client/dist` rebuilt (Node 26.4.0) so the shipped vendor bundle posts to the new routes.

## Out of scope (intentionally not changed)
- `readTree` / `readTreeAtVersion` — versioned route stays separate.
- `duplicate` / `duplicateTo` — these fundamentally differ (service method, permission target, error→status mapping).

## Verification
- PHPStan (level max, 100% type coverage): no errors.
- PHP functional suite: green (the only 2 failures are pre-existing `FixtureControllerTest` cases unrelated to this change — they fail on the base too).
- JS suite: 1105/1105.
- `client/dist` parity gate clean (committed bundle matches a fresh build).
- No remaining references to `api/publish`, `api/unpublish`, or `api/createContent` anywhere in `src/`, `tests/`, or `client/src/`.

## Docs
- `docs/architecture/backend.md` route table updated for the unified endpoints.

## Notes for reviewers
- No backward-compat shims: this API is internal to the module's own React frontend, so both sides change atomically.
- `requireElementRefFromRequest()` is retained (still used by `apiDuplicate`).

author: subhsubh24
body:
## What & why (SIDE-EFFECT INTEGRITY)

The same-market / cross-market arbitrage strategies emit an opportunity with `outcome_idx == -1` (BUY several outcomes at once). Such a basket has **no single token to trade**, yet the orchestrator's single-order execution path built ONE `OrderRequest` with an **empty `token_id`** and called `executor.execute(...)`. In paper mode `_simulate_fill` reports **FILLED for any order** (confirmed: it never validates `token_id`), so the bot:
- incremented `total_executions` for a trade that never happened,
- booked a meaningless empty-token position, and
- wrote a "filled" audit/persist record.

That is precisely the **fake fill** the SIDE-EFFECT INTEGRITY rule forbids ("a reported order/fill must reflect a real execution that actually traversed the order path").

## The fix (DECISION COROLLARY — don't fake an unbuilt loop)
Real per-leg execution (place + confirm each leg, all-or-nothing) is the named, not-yet-built **B1** follow-up. Until it exists we don't fake it: a multi-leg opportunity is now **recorded honestly as skipped** (audit event `skip_multi_leg`, reason `multi-leg basket — per-leg execution not yet built (B1)`) and never executed. **Single-outcome opportunities are completely unaffected** — the skip is gated strictly on `outcome_idx < 0`.

This also makes paper PnL / attribution honest: no phantom basket positions pollute the resolved stream.

## Test
A multi-leg opportunity that passes data-quality + risk + Kelly is asserted to be **skipped with the multi-leg reason** (proving it reaches the new branch, not an upstream reject), with **0 executions** and **no empty-token position** booked. Full prediction-markets + arb-cost + learning-loop suites pass (86 + 1 xfail).

## Disjointness
Touches only `orchestrator.py` + `test_prediction_markets.py`. No new credential; no capability added.

author: stubbi
body:
## Thinking Path

A forked, exposed app needs its own public URL at config or build time (origin allowlists, OAuth redirect URIs, CORS, base URLs), but Mitos assigns the subdomain dynamically as `<label>.<expose-domain>`, so the app cannot hardcode it. This is part 1 of #476: the URL injection plus `mitos.yaml` templating.

The resolved public URL becomes known in `runservice.Run` (`https://<label>.<exposeDomain>`). The golden pool is shared across a tenant's forks and is built once, so it gets the stable per-pool URL `https://<pool>.<domain>` at build time, which reaches a `run.ready` gated serving workload that starts during the snapshot build (the OpenClaw gateway case). The per-fork Sandbox gets its own per-instance URL `https://<label>.<domain>` in `Spec.Env`, for exec sessions and processes started after the fork. For a single-instance app these coincide.

Mechanisms:
- `MITOS_PUBLIC_URL` injected into the golden `Template.Env` (and the captured-running workload env), and into the per-fork `Sandbox.Spec.Env`.
- `${MITOS_PUBLIC_URL}` substitution over `run.command`, `run.env`, and `workdir`: one well-defined braced token only, no shell or arbitrary variable expansion (no injection surface). A bare `$MITOS_PUBLIC_URL` is not substituted; an empty URL injects nothing and leaves the token literal.
- The value is a non-secret URL, never a credential, so it is safe to bake into the shareable golden snapshot. Threat-model note added.

Threaded the per-pool canonical URL into `GoldenPool(namespace, publicURL)` and the per-instance URL into `Provision(..., publicURL)`; `runservice.Run` computes both.

## Verification

Commands run in the worktree:

- `go build ./...`: clean.
- `go test ./internal/runmanifest/ ./internal/runservice/`: PASS (new tests: `TestExpandPublicURL`, `TestGoldenPoolInjectsPublicURL`, `TestGoldenPoolNoURLLeavesLiteral`, `TestProvisionInjectsPublicURL`, `TestProvisionNoURLNoInjection`, `TestRunThreadsPublicURL`; all pre-existing tests still PASS). TDD: tests written first, confirmed RED (signature/symbol compile failures), then GREEN.
- `go vet ./internal/runmanifest/ ./internal/runservice/ ./internal/controller/`: clean.
- `gofmt -l internal/runmanifest/ internal/runservice/`: empty.
- `golangci-lint run --timeout=5m ./internal/runmanifest/... ./internal/runservice/...`: exit 0.
- `GOOS=linux golangci-lint run --timeout=5m ./internal/runmanifest/... ./internal/runservice/...`: exit 0 (authoritative).
- em/en dash scan over all touched files: clean.
- envtest: assets installed via `setup-envtest use 1.31`; the full `./internal/controller/` suite is slow and exceeded a 2 minute bound, but the relevant subset `go test ./internal/controller/ -run 'AutoUpdate|Workload|RunWith'` PASSED (4.8s). No controller production code changed in this PR.

## Model Used

Claude (subagent) via Claude Code

## Summary

Implements part 1 of #476: inject `MITOS_PUBLIC_URL` into the build and run env and add `${MITOS_PUBLIC_URL}` `mitos.yaml` templating over `run.command` / `run.env` / config. Docs updated in `docs/preview-urls.md` (new "Self-configuring with MITOS_PUBLIC_URL" section) and `docs/threat-model.md` (non-secret URL, bounded substitution, no new exposure surface).

Tracked follow-up (part 2, out of scope here): the auth bridge, forwarding the caller's verified Mitos Expose identity into the app via forward-auth headers and an optional signed identity assertion (deep SSO). It moves a trusted identity surface and needs its own threat-model delta and a named human reviewer.

Refs #476

`aw.yml` manifests that include a GitHub Actions `branding` block fail schema validation with `Unknown property: branding` because the field was absent from `aw_manifest_schema.json`. The field is accepted and ignored at runtime — gh-aw has no use for marketplace branding metadata beyond passing schema validation.

# now valid in aw.yml
name: My Package
branding:

includes:

body:
## 概述
导航重构 + **邮局投递 P1–P4** + **邮局根因重构（投递记录层）**。

### 1. 导航
商品管理独立一级导航；物流管理改子菜单（ZTO-MF / 收件人 / 邮局投递）。

### 2. 邮局投递 P1–P4（订单驱动，历史迭代）
批次 / 投诉工单 / 改地址·回访 / 收款发票，迁移 `d0e1f2a3b4c5` `e2f4a6b8c0d1` `f3a5c7b9d1e2` `a4c6e8b0d2f4`。

### 3. ⭐ 根因重构：邮局 = 投递方式（投递记录层）— 迁移 `b5d7f9a1c3e6`
用户澄清定架构：**邮局投递是一种投递方式（等同中通 ZTO-MF）**，数据源自平台订单，但**邮局明细本身是投递记录、不是订单**——只 CBJ/淘宝/中经报有赞 有订单详情，其余平台只有投递数据；中通/邮局明细都可能有订单里没有的数据。核实现有 `shipping_details` 本就是「投递记录，可挂订单/可独立」，邮局照它。

| 从 | 到 |
|---|---|
| 每行造 `post_office` 订单（污染订单列表/客户管理、与电商单双算）| 独立 `PostalDelivery` 投递记录（不造订单，不进订单列表/客户管理）|
| 批次从订单目标归批 | 从投递记录按起投月归批（`postal_delivery_rows` 加 `postal_delivery_id` 溯源）|
| 工单「挂订单」| 「已关联读者 / 未匹配」（经 `delivery_map` 按 编号+年度 挂投递记录，挂真实订单才继承 order_id）|

## Summary
Cron script output no longer leaks secrets when redaction itself fails — `_run_job_script()` now fails closed instead of silently passing raw stdout/stderr through.

Root cause: the redaction block swallowed any exception with `except Exception: pass`, leaving `stdout`/`stderr` unredacted. If `redact_sensitive_text()` ever raised (import failure, regex bug), API keys/tokens could leak into cron delivery messages and logs.

Salvage of #25904 by @sprmn24, cherry-picked onto current main with authorship preserved.

## Changes
- `cron/scheduler.py` — redaction block in `_run_job_script()`: log the failure via `logger.warning` and replace both `stdout` and `stderr` with `[REDACTED - redaction failed]` instead of `pass`.

## Validation
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| redaction raises | raw output (secrets leak) | `[REDACTED - redaction failed]`, logged |
| redaction succeeds | redacted | redacted (no change) |

E2E: patched `redact_sensitive_text` to raise → confirmed neither stdout nor stderr secret survived and the fallback marker was present; patched it to a working redactor → confirmed real redaction applied and the fallback did not fire. author: nic-6443
body:
### Description

`ai-prompt-guard` returns 500 when a chat message's `content` is a structured array instead of a plain string.

OpenAI Chat Completions allows `messages[].content` to be either a string or an array of typed parts, e.g.:

```json
{ "role": "user", "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "hello" } ] }
```

The root cause is in the protocol layer: `openai-chat.get_messages()` returned `body.messages` verbatim, so a table-valued `content` leaked to consumers. `ai-prompt-guard` then concatenates message content with `table.concat`, which raises:

```
ai-prompt-guard.lua: invalid value (table) at index N in table for 'concat'
```

The canonical `{role, content}` contract is that `get_messages` returns content already flattened to a plain string. This PR makes every adapter honor that contract and keeps the flattening in exactly one place per adapter:

- **openai-chat** / **anthropic-messages**: `get_messages` now reuses the adapter's existing `append_message_text` helper instead of re-implementing the flatten loop.
- **bedrock-converse**: adds `append_block_texts`, replacing six copies of the content-block text extraction across `extract_response_text`, `extract_request_content`, `extract_user_content` and `get_messages`.
- **openai-responses**: adds `append_item_text` shared by `extract_request_content`, `extract_user_content` and `get_messages`. This also fixes `get_messages` silently dropping structured (array) input content parts — the same class of bug, previously masked because it dropped the content instead of crashing.

Non-text parts (e.g. `image_url`) are dropped, consistent across all adapters. Every `get_messages` consumer (`ai-prompt-guard`, `ai-lakera-guard`, `ai-cache`) then receives flattened text without re-implementing the extraction; `ai-lakera-guard.normalize_messages` is reduced to filtering empty turns.

Regression tests cover structured content in conversation history, the latest user message, mixed text/non-text parts (openai-chat), and structured input parts (Responses API); they fail before the fix and pass after. The `ai-prompt-guard`, `ai-lakera-guard`, and `ai-cache` suites are green locally.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #

- [x] I have explained the changes or the new features added to this PR
- [x] I have added tests corresponding to this change
- [ ] I have updated the documentation to reflect this change

## Summary

Fixes #55130.

When the bundled `basic` username/password provider is the only interactive dashboard auth provider, unauthenticated HTML navigations should render `/login` so the password form can POST to `/auth/password-login`.

author: diana-ab
body:
# Issue 21 — Question Generation System / Gameplay Question Foundation

## Summary

This PR adds the internal backend foundation for generating multiple-choice math questions in QuizWheelz.

The goal of this issue is to create a production-ready question generation core that can later be used by the student question delivery flow, answer validation, scoring, race progress, and adaptive gameplay systems.

This PR does **not** expose a student question endpoint yet, does **not** persist generated questions yet, and does **not** validate submitted answers yet. Those responsibilities belong to the next issues.

---

## Why this change is needed

QuizWheelz is a racing learning game where students progress by answering questions. The server must generate questions, own the correct answer, and later use that information to validate answers and update race progress.

The project requirement is not to use a fixed bank of ready-made questions. Instead, the database stores reusable `QuestionTemplate` rows, and the server generates real questions from those templates.

This PR builds that foundation in a clean way:

- Questions are generated from templates.
- The server owns the correct answer.
- The frontend will not receive correctness data.
- The generator is testable and separated into focused services.
- The architecture is ready for Issue 22, where generated questions will be persisted and delivered safely to a `RacePlayer`.

---

## High-level system meaning

Before this PR, the system had `Subject`, `QuestionTemplate`, `QuestionType`, and `Difficulty`, but it did not yet have a complete internal flow that could turn a template into a real generated multiple-choice question.

After this PR, the backend can internally do the following:

```text
QuestionPlan
    ↓
QuestionGenerationService
    ↓
QuestionTemplateSelectionService
    ↓
QuestionPlan rebuilt from selected QuestionTemplate
    ↓
MathQuestionGenerator
    ↓
MathQuestionPlanValidator
    ↓
MathOperandGenerator
    ↓
MathQuestionData
    ↓
AnswerChoiceGenerator
    ↓
InternalGeneratedQuestion
```

This means the backend now has a complete internal generation pipeline, but the result is still server-side only.

---

## Main flow added in this PR

### 1. A `QuestionPlan` describes what kind of question should be generated

`QuestionPlan` is an internal DTO that carries the generation request details:

- subject
- question type
- difficulty
- min/max value range
- time limit
- number of choices
- generation pattern
- adaptive mode
- assistance level

The plan is used as an internal instruction for the generation system.

---

### 2. A matching `QuestionTemplate` is selected

`QuestionTemplateSelectionService` selects an active template based on:

- subject
- question type
- difficulty
- generation pattern

This is important because the same question type and difficulty may have different generation patterns.

For example:

```text
MULTIPLICATION + HARD + BINARY_OPERATION
MULTIPLICATION + HARD + SMALL_MULTIPLICATION_CHAIN
```

Both are multiplication questions, but they require different generation rules.

---

### 3. The selected template becomes the source of truth for generation

`QuestionGenerationService` does not blindly trust all values from the incoming `QuestionPlan`.

After selecting a template, it rebuilds a new template-backed `QuestionPlan` using template values such as:

- question type
- difficulty
- min value
- max value
- time limit
- choices count
- generation pattern

The incoming plan still keeps future gameplay context fields such as adaptive mode and assistance level.

This keeps template configuration in the database as the trusted source for question generation.

---

### 4. `MathQuestionGenerator` creates the actual math question

`MathQuestionGenerator` is responsible for building the actual math question text and correct answer.

It supports basic binary math questions:

- addition
- subtraction
- multiplication
- division

It also supports the first connected expression pattern:

- `ADD_THEN_MULTIPLY`

Example:

```text
3 + 4 × 5 = ?
```

The correct answer is calculated using order of operations:

```text
3 + (4 × 5) = 23
```

---

### 5. Validation was extracted into `MathQuestionPlanValidator`

The generator originally became too large because it handled generation, validation, and operand randomization together.

This PR separates validation into `MathQuestionPlanValidator`.

It validates:

- required fields
- min/max value range
- supported binary question types
- expression pattern compatibility with difficulty
- expression pattern compatibility with question type
- division ranges
- multiplier ranges

This keeps `MathQuestionGenerator` focused on generating questions instead of validating all plan rules itself.

---

### 6. Operand creation was extracted into `MathOperandGenerator`

Operand generation is now handled by `MathOperandGenerator`.

It generates numbers according to `MathOperandRole`:

- `ANY`
- `ADDEND`
- `MULTIPLIER`
- `DIVISION_FACTOR`

This is important because not every number in a complex expression should be generated the same way.

For example, in:

```text
a + b × c
```

`b` and `c` are multiplier operands and should be limited by multiplication rules so the question stays fair for children.

The class also includes defensive validation to avoid `NullPointerException` if another developer calls it directly with invalid input.

---

### 7. Pattern rules were centralized in `MathPatternRules`

This PR introduces centralized rule handling for math generation patterns.

`MathPatternRules` defines what is allowed for each pattern, including:

- allowed difficulties
- allowed question types
- max multiplication operator count
- max division operator count
- max multiplication factor
- max correct answer value
- whether repeated multiplication is allowed
- whether repeated division is allowed
- whether the pattern uses order of operations
- whether the pattern uses parentheses

This prevents hardcoded logic from spreading across the generator.

---

### 8. `MathPatternRule` was introduced as an internal rule model

`MathPatternRule` represents the configuration for one generation pattern.

It is package-private and uses Lombok, matching the current project style.

This avoids using inner classes or Java records and keeps the code more readable and consistent with the rest of the project.

---

### 9. `MathExpressionPattern` now owns expression-specific math behavior

Expression-specific logic is now represented in `MathExpressionPattern`.

Each expression pattern can define:

- related `QuestionType`
- operators
- operand roles
- text layout
- correct answer calculation
- preferred distractor candidates

This means `MathQuestionGenerator` does not need to know every formula itself.

Example for `ADD_THEN_MULTIPLY`:

```text
a + b × c
```

Correct answer:

```text
a + (b × c)
```

Preferred distractor:

```text
(a + b) × c
```

The preferred distractor represents a common student mistake: solving left-to-right instead of using order of operations.

---

### 10. `AnswerChoiceGenerator` creates reliable multiple-choice answers

`AnswerChoiceGenerator` creates the final answer choices.

It ensures:

- exactly one correct answer
- unique choices
- preferred distractors are used when available
- random distractors are reasonable and close to the correct answer
- fallback distractors are generated when needed
- display order is shuffled

This gives the system realistic multiple-choice answers instead of random, obviously wrong numbers.

---

## Internal DTO protection

This PR protects internal generated question DTOs from accidental frontend exposure.

author: frankh
body:
## Problem

Logs drop rules with a "Rate limit" action weren't holding ingestion to the configured rate (e.g. a 10 MB/s rule let far more than 10 MB/s through).

Root cause is in the backend token bucket, not the UI. The logs sampling limiter sends one aggregated-cost call per batch and admits records up to the returned `tokensBefore`. But it runs on the **V2** token-bucket Lua, which on overdraft *preserves* the full bucket balance instead of draining it. So under sustained overload the bucket refills back up to the burst pool and re-admits a full pool on every batch — effective throughput becomes roughly `poolMax × batches/sec` instead of the configured `refillRate/sec`. It works at low volume (where a batch fits in the bucket) and fails exactly when the limit should bite.

The volume-preview chart is correct — bars above the reference line are expected for a preview of historical (pre-drop) volume.

## Changes

- Switch the logs sampling rate limiter to the **V3** token-bucket Lua, which floor-drains the available tokens on overdraft — exactly matching the aggregated-cost partial-admission pattern the caller uses. The bucket can no longer sit at the full burst pool and re-admit it every batch.
- V3 is opt-in via a new `scriptVersion` flag on `KeyedRateLimiterService` (default stays V2). The shared limiter's existing V2 contract — including the deliberate repeated-same-id "wedge fix" that `rateLimitGrouped` and other callers rely on — is left untouched.

Scoped to the reported drop-rule path. The team-level logs limiter (`logs-rate-limiter.service.ts`) and the metrics limiter (`metrics-rate-limiter.service.ts`) use the same aggregated-cost partial-admission pattern and carry the same latent bug; they're intentionally left on V2 here and can be flipped in a follow-up.

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent (PostHog Code); listing only automated tests I actually ran.

- Added two real-Redis regression tests in `keyed-rate-limiter.service.test.ts`:
  - `floor-drains the available tokens on overdraft instead of preserving the balance` — asserts the stored pool is drained to empty after an over-budget call.
  - `caps sustained-overload admission at refillRate per batch (drop-rule regression)` — reproduces the original bug: repeated over-budget batches stay pinned at ~`refillRate` per batch. Under the old V2 path the per-batch budget climbs toward `poolMax`, so this test fails pre-fix — the regression no existing test caught.
- Updated the stubbed pipeline mocks in `logs-sampling.service.test.ts` to the V3 command name (they feed a fixed return, so they still exercise the admission walk).
- Ran `keyed-rate-limiter.service.test.ts`, `logs-sampling.service.test.ts`, and `logs-rate-limiter.service.test.ts` — 89 passed. `eslint` clean on the changed files; `tsc` clean (remaining tsc errors are pre-existing, unrelated `@posthog/hogvm`/`@posthog/cyclotron` native-dep resolution failures in `src/cdp/*`).

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Investigated a reported "rate limit not limiting" bug starting from a screenshot of the drop-rule UI. Traced end to end: confirmed the volume-preview chart math (contiguous zero-filled buckets, correct per-second→per-bucket projection) was sound and ruled out the visualization, then found the real defect in the token-bucket Lua's overdraft branch.

Key decision: rather than flip the shared `rateLimitMany` to V3 wholesale (which would discard V2's intentional preserve-on-denial behavior and churn the generic suite), made V3 opt-in via config and switched only the logs sampling path. No repo skills were applicable to this Node.js ingestion change.

author: ebauza
body:
### Overview

This PR introduces a visibility control at appraisal level to support confidential appraisals.

A new field `visibility` allows defining whether an appraisal is:

- Visible to all (standard behavior)
- Visible to managers only

### Functional behavior

When an appraisal is set to "Visible to managers":

- The evaluated employee cannot access the appraisal (filtered by record rules)
- The appraisal is not visible in any view (kanban, list, form)
- No activities are created for the employee
- No automatic notifications are sent to the employee

Managers and HR officers keep full access and normal notification flow.

### Technical approach

- A new `visibility` selection field is introduced
- Existing access rule is extended to include visibility restrictions
- Notification logic (`action_confirm`, `action_done`) is adapted to skip employee notifications when required
- Activity creation is also filtered accordingly

This approach leverages standard mechanisms without altering `mail.thread`.

### Tests

- Existing tests are preserved
- New tests ensure:
  - Employee does not receive activities when visibility is restricted
  - Managers still receive activities
  - No regression in default behavior

### Documentation

Usage documentation has been updated to explain visibility behavior.

### Notes

- Backward compatible (default = visible to all)
- Existing flows are not impacted

This PR replaces the previous notification-based approach, focusing instead on access and visibility control.

author: cardene777
body:
# 概要

`@kiwa-test/orm` v0.7.0 をリリースします。
v1.2 で「future follow-up」 として残した Prisma + MySQL testcontainers 経路と、 Drizzle のみ対応だった file-based migration の Kysely 版を追加し、 受入 matrix を 9 → 11 組合せに拡張しました。
v1.3 milestone (#556) の maintenance sub-Issue です。

# 課題

v0.6 では 2 つの制約が残っていました。

- Prisma + MySQL は throw する分岐になっており、 Prisma を使う MySQL アプリの test 経路が無かった
- Kysely の `migrations: { folder }` は throw する分岐になっており、 ファイル単位で migration を分割管理したい Kysely 利用者は SQL 文字列を 1 つにまとめて渡すしかなかった

# 詳細

v0.6 の adapter dispatcher は以下のように Prisma + MySQL と Kysely + folder migration を throw で塞いでいました。

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[setupOrmEnv opts] --> B{orm}
    B -->|prisma| C{dialect}
    C -->|sqlite mock| D[setupMockPrismaSqlite]
    C -->|postgres live| E[setupLivePrismaPostgres]
    C -->|mysql live| X1[throw v0.6 future follow-up]
    B -->|kysely| F{migrations}
    F -->|folder| X2[throw v0.5 Drizzle-only]
    F -->|string array| G[apply SQL]
```

v1.3 milestone の主軸は framework 深堀り (`@kiwa-test/nuxt` 等) ですが、 v1.2 ORM milestone (#527) の残件は maintenance sub として本 milestone で消化する判断にしました。

# 解決方法

3 経路の変更で穴を塞ぎました。

- `setupLivePrismaMysql()` を追加し、 `@testcontainers/mysql` で MySQL コンテナを起動 → `prisma db push --schema=<schemaPath>` で schema 反映 → 呼出側の `PrismaClient` を返す
- `applyKyselyFolderMigrations()` helper を追加し、 `kysely.Migrator` + `FileMigrationProvider` 経由で folder migration を適用する経路に差し替え
- mock sqlite / live postgres / live mysql 全 Kysely adapter で `isFolderMigration` 分岐を「throw」 から「helper 呼出」 に変更
- `expectQuery` / `expectRowCount` の live MySQL 経路に Prisma 分岐を追加し、 `$queryRawUnsafe` で raw SQL を発行できるよう統一

# 仕組み

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[setupOrmEnv opts] --> B{orm}
    B -->|prisma| C{dialect}
    C -->|sqlite mock| D[setupMockPrismaSqlite]
    C -->|postgres live| E[setupLivePrismaPostgres]
    C -->|mysql live| F[setupLivePrismaMysql 新規]
    B -->|kysely| G{migrations}
    G -->|folder| H[applyKyselyFolderMigrations helper 新規]
    G -->|string array| I[apply SQL]
    H --> J[kysely.Migrator + FileMigrationProvider]
```

変更したファイルと内容。

| ファイル | 何を変えたか |
|---|---|
| `packages/orm/src/setup-orm-env.ts` | `setupLivePrismaMysql()` + `applyKyselyFolderMigrations()` 追加、 Kysely 3 adapter の folder 経路を throw から helper 呼出に差し替え |
| `packages/orm/src/types.ts` | `LivePrismaMysqlOptions` / `OrmTestEnvLivePrismaMysql` 追加、 `SetupOrmEnvOptions` matrix と `OrmTestEnv` union を拡張 |
| `packages/orm/src/expectations.ts` | live MySQL 経路に Prisma 分岐 (`$queryRawUnsafe`) を追加 |
| `packages/orm/src/index.ts` | 新 type を re-export |
| `packages/orm/package.json` | version 0.6.0 → 0.7.0 |
| `packages/orm/README.md` | Roadmap 行から「Prisma + MySQL testcontainers (future follow-up)」 を削除、 matrix 9 → 11 組合せ、 Limitations を v0.4 → v0.7 に更新 |
| `examples/orm-prisma-mysql-poc/` | 新規 PoC (8 tests T-PM-001〜T-PM-008、 testcontainers MySQL + prisma db push) |
| `examples/orm-kysely-migration-poc/` | 新規 PoC (4 tests T-KM-001〜T-KM-004、 `.mjs` migration file + Kysely Migrator) |
| `packages/orm/tests/kysely-migrator.test.ts` | 新規 unit test (4 tests T-ORM-KM-001〜T-ORM-KM-004、 mock sqlite + tmpdir migration) |

# テストと確認

- [x] `@kiwa-test/orm` 全 28 tests passed (24 既存 + 4 new kysely-migrator)
- [x] `examples/orm-prisma-mysql-poc` 8 tests passed (testcontainers MySQL + Prisma)
- [x] `examples/orm-kysely-migration-poc` 4 tests passed (Kysely Migrator file-based)
- [x] 既存 PoC (`orm-prisma-postgres-poc` / `orm-drizzle-file-migration-poc` / `orm-kysely-sqlite-poc`) 回帰なし
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm build` 全 pass

レビューで見てほしいところ。

- `applyKyselyFolderMigrations` の `FileMigrationProvider` 動的 import + 型 cast (kysely 動的 import の型解像対策)
- `setupLivePrismaMysql` の `testcontainers/mysql` `getConnectionUri()` がそのまま Prisma の `mysql` provider URL として通る前提 (testcontainers 標準動作、 `containerImage` で override 可能)
- `expectations.ts` の live MySQL Prisma 分岐 (既存 Postgres Prisma 分岐と同形)

# 関連

- 親 milestone #556 (v1.3 framework 深堀り)
- v1.2 ORM milestone 完遂 #527 / Linear CAR-291
- v0.6 release commit `e7c3621` (Prisma + Postgres testcontainers)

Closes #563

author: zx10r06
body:
## Description
Fixes a bug in `scripts/inject-ga.js` where the `%EXPO_PUBLIC_GA_ID%` token was left unsubstituted in the production `dist/index.html` when Expo SDK 52 copies `web/index.html` verbatim.

## Related Issue
Related to #75

## Root Cause
The original idempotency check was:
```js
if (html.includes('googletagmanager.com')) { skip }
```
Since `web/index.html` already contains the GA script tag with the `%EXPO_PUBLIC_GA_ID%` token, Expo's verbatim copy of that file to `dist/index.html` triggers the check — causing `inject-ga.js` to skip substitution entirely. Result: production HTML ships with the literal token `%EXPO_PUBLIC_GA_ID%` instead of `G-X09N3J8X17`.

## Changes Made
- [x] `scripts/inject-ga.js` — restructured `main()` into 3 explicit priority cases

## Fix Logic
```
Case 1: %EXPO_PUBLIC_GA_ID% token present  → replace all occurrences with real GA ID ✅
Case 2: Real GA ID already present (no token) → skip (idempotent, already correct) ✅  
Case 3: No GA tag at all → inject fresh snippet before </head> ✅
```

## Testing
All 4 cases verified:
- ✅ Token substitution (Expo verbatim copy — the bug scenario)
- ✅ Already injected correctly — skip
- ✅ Fresh injection (Expo generates dist HTML from scratch)
- ✅ Custom `EXPO_PUBLIC_GA_ID` env var honoured

## Checklist
- [x] Bug fix is surgical — only `main()` restructured, `readGaIdFromEnv()` and `buildGaSnippet()` unchanged
- [x] All 3 original use cases still work
- [x] No console.logs or debug code
- [x] Branch up to date with main

author: shehabyasser-scale
body:
Stacks on **#4** (`harbor-2-sidecar`). Addresses the trust-boundary findings from the review of that PR. 2 of 4 fix PRs. ### What this fixes | # | Sev | Finding | Fix | |---|---|---|---| | S1 | 🔴 | `tier_for_split` fails **open** (unlisted split → `viewable` → per-sample labels written to the agent volume) | Fail **closed**: unlisted → `no_access`, with a warning | | S2 | 🔴 | **Mode A scorer provenance (the headline).** `task_project=None` loads the `@task.evaluation()` scorer from the agent's committed repo; `evaluate_admin` then scores the hidden split with it, so a committed scorer returning `1.0` wins | `build_components` refuses a Mode A config without `task_project`, so the hidden-split scorer is always sidecar-baked, never the agent's commit | | S3 | 🔴 | `auto_best` ranks candidates purely by the agent-influenced recorded score, so a candidate can inflate its own selection score | Recorded score only shortlists; the winner is decided by re-running `evaluate_admin` (trusted scorer) on the selection split for the top-K and ranking by admin score. Fails closed | | S4 | 🟠 | The budget ledger is rebuilt from config on every start, so a sidecar restart resets spent budget to full | Reload `remaining_*` from the persisted ledger when present (fail-safe to configured budgets) | | S5 | 🟠 | No adversarial/OS-level tests for the integrity claims | Added: `no_access`→400, a cheating-agent repo proving `finalize` doesn't run the agent's scorer, token `0o600`/unreadable | ### Greptile findings on PR #4, also fixed here (replies posted on #4) - **stale result dirs** (`server.py`): `_route_results` recreates the dir so it reflects exactly the current metered run. - **`reward_mode` typed** (`serve.py`): now `Literal["submit","auto_best"]`, rejected at parse time. - **`auto_best` dataset scoping** (`verifier.py`): candidates filtered by `selection_dataset_id` so a foreign dataset's same-named split can't select the winner. ### Architecture question This PR keeps `tier_for_split` as the sidecar's write-routing resolver and flips it fail-closed; the engine-side real-time access gate lands in the core PR. See the design note (answering "should split access be a dataset property with a real-time check?") for the full reasoning. Short answer: yes, and the core PR implements the minimal version. ### Tests 20 harbor unit tests pass (protocol, verifier, app). The 3 real-eval serve tests pass end-to-end (built via `uv` against a real task project): the honest path, the cheating-agent scorer-provenance proof (reward stays `0.0`, not the agent's `1.0`), and the ledger-reload-across-restart test. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This PR tightens Harbor sidecar evaluation and reward handling. The main changes are: - Unlisted splits now fail closed to `no_access`. - Mode A startup now requires a trusted `task_project`. - Budget ledgers are reloaded from persisted state across restarts. - `auto_best` now admin re-scores a shortlist before choosing a winner. - Result directories are recreated to avoid stale per-sample files. - Tests cover scorer provenance, no-access handling, token permissions, ledger reload, and verifier selection.

Confidence Score: 2/5

 Not merge-safe until the auto-selection and budget reload paths are corrected. The changes address several trust-boundary issues, but runtime checks reproduced cases where candidate selection can still be controlled by recorded scores, scorer failures can abort finalization prematurely, and persisted budget state can override the current baked configuration. `vero/src/vero/harbor/verifier.py` and `vero/src/vero/harbor/serve.py` need attention.

T-Rex Logs

 **What T-Rex did** - Ran a focused pytest harness against the Verifier auto\_best path with five validation candidates and a recorded-score shortlist that excluded the trusted best commit. - The run showed evaluate\_admin was called only for bad\_1, bad\_2, and bad\_3, with the final scoring run on bad\_3 and the true\_best (0.99) not evaluated because its mean\_score ranked below the shortlist. - The test failed asserting the selected winner should match the full admin best, demonstrating auto\_best picked bad\_3 instead of true\_best. - Ran a focused ledger-restart repro that wrote a persisted ledger.json with dataset-a/test budgets (100 samples, 10 runs, max 50) and then restarted ledger loading with reduced budgets (10 samples, 1 run, max 5). - The loaded ledger still contained the persisted old values, allowed check(dataset-a, test, 6) despite the current max\_samples\_per\_run being 5, and, when restarted with an empty budget\_cfgs list, the removed dataset-a/test split remained evaluable from the persisted ledger. - Ran a Harbor Verifier auto\_best harness with two candidates ordered by recorded score; monkeypatched evaluate\_admin to raise for first\_raises and return 0.95 for later\_success, and finalize raised RuntimeError after evaluating only first\_raises, so later\_success was never considered. - Before: a fail-open tier showed viewable split\_accesses; After: the code path moved to a fail-closed tier with no\_access, and a repro script constructs the failing path for the tier switch. - Before: mode A provenance showed harbor=None, task\_project=None, initialized components, token written, and exit code 0; After: head raised ValueError about missing task\_project and the fail-closed guard activated, with exit code 0; Supplemental: a fail-closed pytest run appeared successful, though the trusted-scorer test did not run due to a FileNotFoundError during fixture setup. - Before: reward\_mode='bogus' with no selection\_dataset\_id and a chosen foreign\_ds2\_commit; After: the head rejected the bogus reward mode with ValidationError, exposed selection\_dataset\_id, narrowed ranking to ds1, and selected intended\_ds1\_commit. Ran code and verified through T-Rex

author: aaronbamblett
body:

author: ssedano
body:
### Summary
FIS network faults target traffic between an ECS task and a network destination. Customers identify the destination by IP, CIDR, or DNS name; for DNS names FIS resolves to IPs at fault start and hands the resulting set to the ECS Agent, which installs tc rules against it and never revisits the resolution. The set may go stale on long-running faults: resolvers may return only a subset of IPs per lookup, and DNS records rotate over time, so traffic to later-resolved IPs is unimpaired.

### Implementation details
Add `POST /fault/v1/{network-latency|network-packet-loss}/add-sources`. The handler installs additional `tc` filters against a running fault without touching the `qdisc`, returns 404 if no fault of the matching type is running, and caps combined `Sources`+`SourcesToFilter` at 16 IPs per call to fit the 5s `requestTimeoutSeconds` budget.

Touched files: request/response types in `ecs-agent/tmds/handlers/fault/v1/types/types.go`, handlers in `ecs-agent/tmds/handlers/fault/v1/handlers/handlers.go` (and its `agent/vendor/...` mirror), and route registration in `agent/handlers/task_server_setup.go`.

### Testing
Unit tests in `handlers_test.go` and `types_test.go` cover validation, the 16-IP cap, missing/wrong/stopped fault states, and routing.

18 sudo-tagged integration tests issue real `tc` commands on EC2 Linux (`go test -tags sudo -run TestAddSources ./tmds/handlers/fault/v1/handlers/`): happy path for latency and packet loss with `Sources`/`SourcesToFilter`/CIDR; 404 on no fault, wrong type, after stop; 400 on empty/over-cap/overlap/invalid IP/malformed/missing body; 200 at the 16-IP cap; duplicate IPs idempotent; concurrent add+stop and add+add serialized; `qdisc` params unchanged; stop after add cleans everything. All pass.

Manual tests on EC2 against TMDS from a task container, all passing: latency and packet-loss happy paths with mid-fault `add-sources` (verified via `ping`); IPv6 source installs v6 match keys; duplicate IP re-add returns 200 without `qdisc` corruption; add before start, wrong fault type, and add after stop return 404 with the expected error; empty body, `Sources=[]`, and invalid IP return 400 with the expected error.

New tests cover the changes: yes

### Description for the changelog
Feature - Add FIS-driven DNS refresh add-sources endpoint for network-latency and network-packet-loss faults

### Additional Information
**Does this PR include breaking model changes? If so, Have you added transformation functions?**
No. New endpoints and types only; existing types and routes are unchanged.

**Does this PR include the addition of new environment variables in the README?**
No.

By submitting this pull request, I confirm that my contribution is made under the terms of the Apache 2.0 license.

author: digiserg
body:
## Summary

- Cache `isKVv2` preflight results per mount path — eliminates repeated `GET /v1/sys/internal/ui/mounts/<path>` calls for the same mount
- Cache `GetStringMap` results per secret path — eliminates repeated reads when multiple keys are pulled from the same path
- Reorder `provider` struct fields for optimal memory alignment (240→232 bytes)

## Motivation

Each secret reference in a `vals`-processed YAML file previously cost **two** Vault API calls:

1. `GET /v1/sys/internal/ui/mounts/<path>` — KV version preflight
2. `ReadWithData` — secret read

For N secrets this meant 2N token uses, which breaks Vault tokens created with a low `-use-limit` (e.g. `-use-limit=1` fails immediately).

With both caches, token use-limit needed = **unique_mounts + unique_secret_paths** (typically P+1 for a single mount with P distinct paths).

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` passes
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `golangci-lint run` clean (0 issues)
- Integration tests skipped — require a live Vault instance

Rebuilds the character builder to follow the handbook's **Chapter 1 — five steps**: **Class · Background · Ability Scores · Armor · Details** (was a 6-step flow with a free-text background). Consumes the Backgrounds/Feats data added in #111.

## Flow
1. **Class** — class + subclass + class skill choices ("your background grants two more").
2. **Background** — pick one of the **14 structured backgrounds**; panel shows lore + grants (skills, tool, ability boosts, equipment). Grants the specified **Origin feat**, or shows an **Origin-feat picker** when the background leaves it open.
3. **Ability Scores** — point-buy (27) + the background ability bonus, now **constrained to the background's three abilities** (legacy cards keep the any-ability behaviour).
4. **Armor** — unchanged.
5. **Details** — name, level, review (lists background · feat · skills), notes, save.

## Data model
- `HunterCard` gains `backgroundId` + `feat`.
- Saved `skillProficiencies` = class choices ∪ background skills (deduped).
- Feat surfaces on the hunter card and the printable sheet.
- Re-editing strips the background's granted skills from the class-skill count so shared skills aren't double-counted.
- `gen_from_master.py` re-exports `ORIGIN_FEATS`.

## Verification
- `bun run check` (tsc + eslint + knip) green.
- Walked the flow in preview (screenshots): class-skill picker, all 14 backgrounds, **granted-feat (Cultist)** vs **feat-picker (Noble)**, and the ability bonus correctly limited to the chosen background's abilities (STR/INT/CHA for Noble).

author: pmontp19
body:
## Summary

Complete visual redesign of the site adopting a terminal/brutalist aesthetic inspired by `pierre.computer`. The design treats the entire page as a monospace text document with minimal chrome, using OKLch color tokens, a single amber accent, and separator tildes (`~~~`) instead of borders.

## Key Changes

- **Color System**: Migrated from HSL to OKLch color space with `light-dark()` for automatic theme switching. Reduced palette to essential tokens: `--bg`, `--fg`, `--muted`, `--accent` (amber), `--line`, and `--surface`.

- **Typography**: Unified all text to monospace (`ui-monospace`, SF Mono, Menlo, etc.) at 12px/20px line-height. Removed custom font faces (Geist Pixel, Geist Mono). Geist Sans retained only for `.prose` (blog articles).

- **Layout & Components**:
  - Removed sticky header (`Header.astro` deleted)
  - Simplified footer with minimal navigation
  - Replaced card-based design with plain text layout
  - Added `.doc` and `.prose` utility classes for semantic styling
  - Introduced `.mdlink` for markdown-style links with muted brackets
  - Added `.cursor` animation (blinking block) and `.tilde` separator

- **Pages Updated**:
  - `index.astro`: Streamlined to show latest post and 4 recent experiences inline
  - `blog/index.astro`: Terminal-style list with dashes and dates
  - `blog/[slug].astro`: Simplified article layout with prose styling
  - `experiencia.astro`: Converted to terminal format with inline metadata
  - `contact.astro`: Minimal contact display

- **Theme Toggle**: Refactored to use `data-theme` attribute (`light`/`dark`/`system`) instead of `.dark` class, with `prefers-color-scheme` as default.

- **Documentation**: Added `docs/design.md` as the source of truth for the redesign spec, including color tokens, typography rules, layout principles, and divergences (e.g., interactive avatar retained).

## Notable Details

- Removed all box shadows, rounded corners (`--radius: 0`), and decorative borders
- Separator `~~~` replaces `<hr>` elements
- Labels use ALL CAPS with `letter-spacing: 0.04em`
- Avatar size reduced from 12rem to 8.5rem
- Reading time and metadata displayed inline with muted styling
- Transitions reduced from 0.3s to 0.25s for theme changes

author: juul-mobile-bot
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [uniffi](https://mozilla.github.io/uniffi-rs) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs)) | build-dependencies | minor | `0.31.0` → `0.32.0` |
| [uniffi](https://mozilla.github.io/uniffi-rs) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs)) | dependencies | minor | `0.31.0` → `0.32.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>mozilla/uniffi-rs (uniffi)</summary>

### [`v0.32.0`](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v0320-backend-crates-v0320---2026-06-30)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/compare/v0.31.2...v0.32.0)

##### ⚠️ Breaking Changes ⚠️

- Kotlin and Python now fail to generate bindings when there are async primary constructors.
  Previously these languages skipped the constructor in this case or generated a constructor that always threw.
  You can get similar behavior by adding the primary constructor to the uniffi.toml excludes list in uniffi.toml (e.g. \`excludes = \["MyObject.new"])
- Ruby: Force named parameters for enum constructors ([#​2880](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/issues/2880))
- The `--config` flag now expects a [global config file](https://mozilla.github.io/uniffi-rs/next/bindings.html#global-configuration)
  rather than a flat `uniffi.toml`-style override. Old-style files will produce a warning and be ignored.
  See [#​2866](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/issues/2866)
- `[ByRef] bytes` UDL arguments now map to `&[u8]` on the Rust side instead of `&Vec<u8>`. UDL-defined functions whose Rust implementations take `&Vec<u8>` must change to `&[u8]`. Proc-macro signatures (`fn foo(x: &[u8])`) are unchanged. On the Kotlin side, call sites must now pass a *direct* `java.nio.ByteBuffer` rather than `ByteArray`; migrate with `ByteBuffer.allocateDirect(arr.size).put(arr).flip()`. Swift (`Data`) and Python (`bytes`) call sites are unchanged. ([#​2878](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2878))
- Reworked the experimental pipeline bindgen code.  Any external binding generators using this will
  need to be reworked as well.  See [#​2787](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2787) for
  examples of how this can be done.

##### What's Fixed

- Fixed bug that sometimes prevented renaming items inside a submodule [#​2792](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2792)
- Exempted `UniFfiTag` from `clippy::exhaustive_structs` since downstream projects may depend on it [#​2809](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2809)
- Fixed compile errors when exporting ambiguous method names [#​2937](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2937)
- Ruby: Code for all kinds of enums and custom types is now correctly generated [#​2880](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/issues/2880) and [#​2891](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/issues/2891)

##### ⚠️ Breaking Changes for external bindings authors ⚠️

- There's a new `GlobalConfig` struct for managing config. It replaces `BindgenPathsLayer::get_config()` method which has been removed. See [#​2866](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/issues/2866).
- `[ByRef] bytes` arguments now travel across the FFI as a `ForeignBytes` (pointer + length) value rather than a `RustBuffer`. External bindings need to accept the foreign-language byte buffer at the call site and lower it to `ForeignBytes` for the duration of the call (no copy). ([#​2878](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2878))

##### What's New?

- Global config file support via `--config`. See [the docs](https://mozilla.github.io/uniffi-rs/next/bindings.html#global-configuration).

- Traits can now be exported with `#[uniffi::export(foreign)]` for foreign-only implementations, or `#[uniffi::export(rust, foreign)]` for both Rust and foreign implementations. The `with_foreign` flag is deprecated in favor of `rust, foreign`.

- Recursive enums are now supported. UniFFI automatically detects when enum and record types participate in cycles — self-referential, mutually recursive, or cycling through a record — and generates appropriate bindings: `indirect` in Swift, forward references in Python ([#​2834](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2834)).

- `Box<T>` now automatically implements FFI traits when `T` implements them, allowing direct use in enum variants and function parameters without NewType wrappers ([#​2808](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2808))

- Record fields can now be renamed with the proc-macro `name = "new_field_name"` attribute ([#​2794](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2794))

- Items can be excluded from the generated bindings using `uniffi.toml`.

- Added `mutable_records` configuration option to allow specific records to remain mutable even when `generate_immutable_records` is enabled (Kotlin and Swift).

- Kotlin objects now have an `uniffiIsDestroyed` property that returns `true` if the Rust reference no longer exists ([#​2825](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2825))

- Updated `askama` version to `0.15.6`

- Custom Types can have docstrings in some languages ([#​2853](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2853))

- Ruby: Expose standard Rust traits for generated ruby code ([#​2883](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/issues/2883))

- Ruby: Add support for sync foreign traits ([#​2916](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2916))

- Ruby: Add async support ([#​2923](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2923))

- Added zero-copy transfer of `&[u8]` / `[ByRef] bytes` arguments from foreign code to Rust. Kotlin (`java.nio.ByteBuffer`, must be direct), Swift (`Data`), and Python (`bytes`-like, buffer protocol) pass byte buffers as pointer + length (`ForeignBytes`) rather than copying through `RustBuffer`. Not yet supported on Ruby, and not yet supported in async functions on any language ([#​2878](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2878)).

- `#[uniffi::export(async_runtime = "tokio")]` can now be applied to trait exports, wrapping each method's FFI scaffolding future in `async_compat::Compat` the same way it does for inherent impls and free functions ([#​2899](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2899)).

- Added support for using `HashSet` with proc-macros

- Allow literal number suffix with `derive(uniffi::Enum)`([#​2926](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/pull/2926))

[All changes in v0.32.0](https://redirect.github.com/mozilla/uniffi-rs/compare/v0.31.2...v0.32.0).

author: juliensimon
body:
## Problem

Starting a session whose project uses the Apple Container backend failed with a cryptic runtime error when the container daemon wasn't running:

```
Error: interrupted: "XPC connection error: Connection invalid"
Ensure container system service has been started with `container system start`.
```

`SandboxChecker` *already* detects this state (`.containerSystemStopped`) and has the right user-facing fix string — but the check only ran in the **config-time backend pickers** (`SettingsView`, `WorktreeSheet`, `AddProjectSheet`, `EditProjectSheet`). The **auto-start launch path** in `MainWindow` sent the `claude` command unconditionally, so a daemon that stopped *after* the project was configured (e.g. after a reboot) leaked the raw error into the terminal with no guidance.

## Change

- Run `SandboxChecker.check(backend:)` on the launch path before sending the command. It spawns blocking subprocesses, so it runs off the main actor via `Task.detached` (matching the pattern the config pickers already use).
- When the backend isn't ready, echo the existing actionable warning (e.g. *"container runtime is not running. Start it with: `container system start`"*) instead of firing the command.
- Extract the decision into `SandboxBackendUI.launchCommand(for:command:)`, reusing `SandboxBackend.shellSingleQuoted` for echo-safety.

This reuses machinery that already existed; it just routes the check to the one place that was missing it. Applies to all sandboxed backends, not just Apple Container.

## Tests

New `SandboxBackendUI launch preflight` suite (TDD — written red first):
- ready backend launches the command unchanged
- stopped daemon surfaces `container system start`, never the command
- no non-available status ever leaks the launch command

Full suite: **567 tests passing**. Release archive via `scripts/bundle.sh` succeeds.

It also hardens the parity validator so unresolved rows fail closed when they are self-referential, lack tracking rationale, lose the USF-167 source gate, lose the USF-193 environment-promotion standard dependency, or imply closure/readiness from partial evidence.

author: markadams31
body:
Cleanup of deprecations surfaced by analysing the green `deploy-dev` run (#28443341788). Three independent, low-risk fixes bundled into one PR — the workflow changes force the full CI suite anyway, so one PR is one CI run.

## Changes

1. **`deploy.yml` — `--docker-custom-image-name` → `--container-image-name`.** The deploy step logged `Option '--docker-custom-image-name' has been deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Use '--container-image-name' instead.` Same behaviour, current flag.

2. **`ci.yml` — Playwright artifact upload.** Every e2e run logged `No files were found with the provided path: frontend/playwright-report/`. The `list` reporter never produces `playwright-report/`; traces/screenshots from a failed retry (`trace: 'on-first-retry'`) land in `test-results/`. Point the upload there and set `if-no-files-found: ignore` — a green run is silent, a failing run still captures traces.

3. **integration `conftest.py` — structured testcontainers wait.** Replaced the deprecated `wait_for_logs(container, "<string>")` with `.waiting_for(LogMessageWaitStrategy("SQL Server is now ready for client connections").with_startup_timeout(180))` (testcontainers 4.x).

## Validation (local)

- `pytest -m "not integration"` → **298 passed**
- `pytest -m integration` against a real SQL Server container → **78 passed in 38s**; the testcontainers deprecation warning is gone.
- Both workflows parse as valid YAML.

## Deliberately out of scope

- **Node-20 action bumps** (the pervasive `Node.js 20 is deprecated` warnings) — that's the Dependabot *actions* group PR, handled separately.
- **Starlette `TestClient` → `httpx2`** — a dependency change with more surface area; its own PR.

author: h0mele55
body:
Adopts the inflect-compliance "bulk delete via the table selection action-row" feature onto agri-saas, including the **pending-invitations** table (which previously had no delete affordance).

**Tables wired (13):** Pending invitations, Members, Risks, Assets, Controls, Evidence, Policies, Vendors, Findings, Tasks, Locations, Roles, API keys.

Select rows → a danger Delete/Revoke/Remove button in the action-row → confirm → soft-delete, tenant-scoped, permission-gated, audited.

**How:** one shared `useBulkDelete<T>` hook (the only new primitive) + per-entity `bulkDelete<Entity>` usecase mirroring the single-delete + a `bulk/delete` route + 3-line client wiring.

**Notable:** Members has batch-aware last-OWNER/ADMIN protection (can't orphan the tenant); Controls delete is admin-gated alongside its edit-gated status verbs; Revoke verb for credentials. **Excluded with cause:** Inventory (table lists stock lots, no delete semantics) and Frameworks (install/uninstall catalog).

**Verification:** typecheck, lint, affected guards, and rendered tests for every touched client are green. See docs/implementation-notes/2026-06-30-bulk-delete-tables.md.

author: 616fun
body:
Makes the decumulation draw order configurable instead of hardcoded `taxable → pre-tax → Roth`.

## What
- **`simulate.py`** — `withdrawal_order(cfg)` resolves the bucket order from `cfg["withdrawal_order"]` (a list of `"taxable"`/`"pretax"`/`"roth"`), defaulting to `taxable → pretax → roth`. Any omitted bucket is appended so the plan can always reach every dollar. `_pull` now draws across the pools in that order, preserving the capital-gains/basis amortization on the taxable slice.
- **`config_loader.py`** — validates `withdrawal_order` when present.
- **`config.example.json`** — documents the option (pre-tax-first to shrink later RMDs / estate; Roth-last to preserve the tax-free pool).

## Why it matters
Draw order is one of the highest-leverage decumulation levers — it changes lifetime tax, RMD size, ACA/IRMAA exposure, and what's left to heirs. This exposes it as a first-class, testable knob.

## Verification
- **Default order reproduces prior behavior exactly** → all Phase 1 snapshot tests unchanged.
- New tests: order resolution + missing-bucket fill, the first-drawn bucket per strategy (taxable-first vs Roth-first vs pre-tax-first), and validation rejection. **121 tests pass.**

辞書配置は YAML 例どおり**トップレベル**（`voicevox` と同階層）としました（実装方針の確認結果に基づく）。

- `config.Config` に `Pronunciation map[string]string` フィールドと `EffectivePronunciation()`（nil を空 map に正規化）を追加
- `direct` に `WithPronunciation` オプションと `applyPronunciation` ヘルパーを追加し、`buildScript()` で「元テキスト → 辞書置換 → LLM 変換マップ適用」の順で処理

辞書置換は LLM 変換マップの**前段**で適用され、その行を LLM がかな化した場合は LLM の結果が優先されます（辞書は LLM が変換しなかった行に効きます）。LLM は変換が必要な行のみ `line_conversions` に返すため、辞書はそれ以外の行に作用します。

## The 9 tests

| # | Test | Tied to |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `checkworkspace_started_ack_then_completion_notification` | 0.2.5 async wire contract |
| 2 | `checkworkspace_publishdiagnostics_fan_out` | Per-file publish envelopes |
| 3 | `coveragestats_stale_after_edit` | coverageStats remains well-formed post-edit |

| 8 | `window_showmessage_no_folder_init` ★ | 0.2.6 #workspace-less-toast |
| 9 | `window_showmessage_check_before_index_ready` | **SKIPPED — TODO** |

## Skip with TODO

Same shape as PR 1's `request_before_index_returns_safe_partial` — timing-sensitive, requires triggering `checkWorkspace` BEFORE the initial workspace scan completes. Small fixtures scan in <50ms; the window's too narrow. Both unskip when we add a bulk-fixture workspace (a slow-to-scan corpus).

## Conftest gain

`_make_test_client` factory now tracks `dimfort/workspaceCheckCompleted` (counter + last payload). `$/progress` and `window/showMessage` are NOT re-registered here because pytest-lsp already tracks them via the default client features (`progress_reports` + `messages` attributes); tests use those.

## Two pytest-lsp quirks documented inline

- **Progress reports are keyed by token**, registered via `WORK_DONE_PROGRESS_CREATE`. Calling `.clear()` on the dict drops the token registrations and subsequent progress events fail token lookup — iterate without clearing instead.
- **Progress params are unwrapped** — the `Begin/Report/End` record is stored directly on `progress_reports[token]`, not under a `.value` attribute.

author: odadroca
body:
Sprint 4, amendment **A11**. Expose the existing, idempotent `db/seed-demo.php` through a Compose **`demo` profile** so the Docker try-it can show a populated app in one command.

**What:**
- A one-shot **`seed`** service in `docker-compose.yml` (`profiles: ["demo"]`) — reuses the app image, `command: php db/seed-demo.php`, shares the `comecome-data` volume, `restart: "no"`. `docker compose --profile demo up` → app + seed (seeds the volume, then serves). Plain `docker compose up` **never** starts it → clean empty install for real self-hosters.
- It runs as **`user: www-data`** so the DB it creates is writable by the app (see below).
- README + `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` "try it with demo data" block: login as guardian **Guardião / 0000**, or children **Boy (demo) / 1111** · **Girl (demo) / 2222**; re-seed via `docker compose --profile demo run --rm seed php db/seed-demo.php --reset` (foreshadows A25).

**Runtime bug caught + fixed in the real run:** without `user: www-data`, the seed service ran as **root** and created a root-owned `/data/data.db`; the www-data Apache workers then hit `attempt to write a readonly database` → **500 on every request**. Pinning the seed to www-data fixes it (the app creates the DB as www-data on a plain run, which is why A10 was fine).

**Verified locally (`docker compose --profile demo up`):** seed exits 0; DB www-data-owned; container **healthy**; HTTPS login **200**; demo children + ~90 days of data present (927 food rows). **Plain `docker compose up`** on a fresh volume → no seed service, **0 child users** (clean). `down -v` clean.

No app code or schema change — `db/seed-demo.php` is unchanged.

author: vedhavyas
body:
This fixes the spawn auto-kick footgun: a `workers__spawn` with an inline charter didn't actually start the worker - the charter landed in its system prompt but the worker sat idle until it got a separate `workers__tell`, so a "begin now" line in the charter never ran on its own. With the team on on-demand ad-hoc workers now, that bit every spawn (a silently-idle worker reads as progress when there's none).

I added an optional `kick` first-message to `workers__spawn(label, charter?, kick?)`. When provided, the kick is delivered as the worker's first user turn the moment it connects, reusing the same kick-on-connect mechanism the file-driven roles use (`kick.md`): it's stashed on the worker's `WorkerEntry` at spawn and enqueued in `maybe_kick_worker_on_connected`, landing as a plain first turn through the rate-limited dispatcher. The inline kick wins over `kick.md` when both are present.

No kick behaves exactly as today (the worker idles until told) - no regression. The tool description now strongly steers leads to provide `kick`. `CreateRole` and the file-driven `initial_kick` behavior are unchanged. It's an in-process MCP tool, so no wire-conformance scenario.

author: modelmirror
body:
## Why

Workflow changes carry outsized weight — triggers, permissions, token handling, OIDC — plus a house style the linters can't see: **logic in tested Python, bash only plumbs** (the convention we just applied to `run-cleanup`). zizmor/actionlint catch syntax + a slice of security, but not fail-closed authorization, the handoff-token gotcha, expression injection, or "this PR body is being built with `jq` and a heredoc."

## What

- **`.claude/agents/workflow-reviewer.md`** — a read-only review subagent (tools: Read/Grep/Glob/Bash) that diffs the change, reads the canonical rubric (`docs/pipeline.md` *Authoring or changing a workflow*, `docs/security.md`, AGENTS.md) and the closest existing workflow, runs zizmor + actionlint at the pinned versions, and reports a **verdict (blocker / recommended / clean) + `file:line` findings**. It reviews and reports; it does not edit.
- **Convention in AGENTS.md** — before pushing any `.github/workflows` / `.github/actions` change, run the subagent and resolve blockers; self-review against its checklist if it can't be invoked. Pointer added from the workflow-authoring section of `docs/pipeline.md`.

The reviewer's checklist encodes exactly the issues from recent workflow work: full-SHA pins, least-privilege `permissions`, authorize-before-credentials, App-token-vs-GITHUB_TOKEN, no `${{ github.event.* }}` free text in `run:`, and the logic-in-Python smells (jq/heredoc PR bodies, perm checks in bash) — pointing at `collect-plan` / the `cleanup` command as the model.

Docs/config only — no code or workflow change (so it doesn't trip its own convention). The subagent is available to interactive Claude Code and the `run-dev` CI agent alike.

¡Hola Nico! 👋 Soy Hector, de Trixocom. Esta es la segunda mitad de la feature; la primera (columna + helpers en `paloACL`) va en **IssabelFoundation/framework#33**.

### Qué hace
Para usuarios **sin** privilegio `reportany`, el módulo `monitoring` ahora filtra las grabaciones por la lista `acl_user.monitorexten` (vía `paloACL::getUserMonitorExtensions()`), usando `IN(...)` sobre `src` / `dst` / canal. Si el usuario no tiene lista cargada, cae a su extensión propia (comportamiento clásico). El plugin `extension` de `userlist` agrega el campo **"Extensiones a monitorear"** para editarla desde la UI.

Así, un supervisor puede ver las grabaciones de un grupo de internos (su equipo) sin ver las de toda la central y sin necesidad de `reportany`.

### Compatibilidad
Total hacia atrás: una sola extensión produce exactamente el mismo resultado que el filtro `=` anterior. Lo verificamos sobre datos reales de un cliente en producción:
- `viejo (= 592)` == `nuevo IN(592)` (mismos conteos)
- `IN(592,518)` == unión de 592 y 518 (mismos conteos)

### Depende de
**IssabelFoundation/framework#33** (agrega la columna `acl_user.monitorexten` y los helpers en `paloACL`).

El bump de release (5→6) lo podés descartar si manejás los releases por tu lado.

¡Gracias y un abrazo!
— Hector / Trixocom

author: jongodb
body:
## What

**Item 6 — pgBackRest backup repo → MinIO Operator Tenant S3 over TLS.** Adds an S3 repo (`repo2`) to the `PostgresCluster`, **alongside** the existing local-volume `repo1` (backup-continuity-safe — retire repo1 only after a verified S3 restore). Off-node backups are the real durability win. Values-gated on `postgres.backups.s3.enabled` (default off).

## Change
- **`charts/cosmos/templates/postgrescluster.yaml`** — `repo2` (s3: bucket/endpoint/region + schedules) + `spec.backups.pgbackrest.configuration` (projects the SOPS secret's `s3.conf`+`ca.crt` into `/etc/pgbackrest/conf.d`) + `global` (`repo2-storage-ca-file`, `repo2-storage-verify-tls=y`, `repo2-s3-uri-style=path`). `repo1` unchanged.
- **`charts/cosmos/values.yaml`** — `postgres.backups.s3` block (bucket `cosmos-pgbackrest`, endpoint `minio.minio.svc`, region, `secretName`, weekly-full/daily-incr schedules).
- **`charts/cosmos/templates/uds-package.yaml`** — a `cosmos→minio` egress allow.
- **`deploy/secrets/cosmos-pgbackrest-s3.enc.yaml`** — new SOPS-encrypted Secret: `s3.conf` (the repo2 S3 key/secret, a dedicated MinIO svcacct) + `ca.crt` (the Tenant CA = cluster CA).

## ⚠️ Gotcha #15 (documented in the runbook)
The `cosmos→minio` egress **must be portless**. The MinIO Tenant Service is `443→targetPort 9000`, so a `port: 443` netpol drops the packet **post-DNAT** — a silent connect timeout that looks like TLS/DNS. UDS Core's own Loki/Velero storage egress is likewise portless. (Caught via `openssl s_client` from the repo-host: exit 124 with port 443; CONNECTED + verify=0 after removing it.)

## Verification (lab)
- PGO created the repo2 stanza and ran a **full backup** → **1892 objects** in the `cosmos-pgbackrest` bucket over verified TLS; `repo1` preserved.
- TLS chain: the cluster-CA-signed Tenant cert verifies against the projected `ca.crt` (`openssl … verify return code: 0`).
- SOPS secret round-trips (`sops -d` → `s3.conf` has the repo2 keys, `ca.crt` is a PEM).
- `helm template --set postgres.backups.s3.enabled=true` renders repo2 + the egress; disabled by default renders neither.

> Depends conceptually on item 5 (the MinIO Operator Tenant providing the S3 endpoint). Touches `uds-package.yaml` (also touched by #95 in a different region — composes cleanly).

author: jclauzel
body:
## What

Render zxART star ratings on gallery cells in **Retro/pygame mode**, matching what the Classic mode already shows. Affects the **zxArt**, **Unite!/AllInOne**, and **Favorites** tabs (any zxART-sourced content).

## Why

In Retro/pygame mode the `GalleryScene` already split the star rating out of each aggregated title (via `_split_title_rating`) but **discarded it** — `title, _r = ...` — so the gallery cells drew only the clean title. As a result, a title with a zxART rating showed its stars in Classic mode but not in Retro mode. (The pygame *Table* view did show a Rating column; the *gallery* cells did not.)

## How

All changes are in `zxnu_pygame.py`, `GalleryScene`:

- Added `C_STAR = (255, 204, 68)` — gold, mirroring Classic's `#ffcc44`.
- `set_entries()` now caches each entry's `(title, rating)` split once (mirroring `TableScene`) and sets a `_show_ratings` flag when at least one entry on the page has a rating.
- `_cell_size()` reserves one extra strip line (+15px) **only** when the page has ratings.
- `render()` draws the rating string (e.g. `★★★☆☆  (4.2)`) in gold just below the title, elided to the cell width.

Panes without ratings (GetIt, ZXDB, itch.io) keep their compact cells — the extra line and gold text only appear for rated (zxART) content, so non-rated panes are unaffected.

## Testing

Offscreen render test of `GalleryScene`:

- **With ratings:** `_show_ratings=True`, cell height grows +15px, gold star pixels rendered directly under the title.
- **Without ratings:** `_show_ratings=False`, compact cell height unchanged, zero gold pixels.
- `(title, rating)` split cached correctly per entry.
- `py_compile` clean.

## Notes for reviewer

- The star glyphs (`★`/`☆`, U+2605/2606) render through the existing `_draw_text` → `_draw_text_mixed` glyph-fallback path, the same path the Table view already uses for its Rating column.
- `_show_ratings` is recomputed per page in `set_entries`, so the reserved line appears/disappears as you page between rated and unrated content.

author: hyperfinitism
body:
This pull request fixes FAPI callback output buffer lifetime handling.

The auth and sign callbacks allocate CFFI buffers and pass their pointers back to FAPI. Those buffers need to remain alive after the Python callback returns, because FAPI consumes the returned pointers later in the call path.

This PR stores callback output cdata on the callback metadata object so that the buffers remain referenced for the required lifetime.

### Tests

Tested with Python 3.14.6 free-threaded (`3.14t`):

```bash
python3.14t -m pytest -q \
  test/test_fapi.py::TestFapiECC::test_policy_signed \
  test/test_fapi.py::TestFapiRSA::test_policy_signed \
  test/test_fapi.py::TestFapiRSA::test_policy_action \
  test/test_fapi.py::TestFapiRSA::test_sign \
  test/test_fapi.py::TestFapiRSA::test_get_tpm_blobs \
  test/test_fapi.py::TestFapiRSA::test_encrypt_decrypt
```

Before this fix, these FAPI PolicySigned tests would occasionally fail with a `TPM_RC_SIGNATURE` error:

```console
FAILED test/test_fapi.py::TestFapiRSA::test_policy_signed
tpm:parameter(5):the signature is not valid
```

After this fix, the same test set passes:

```console
6 passed
```

body:
## Summary

Small, independent correctness fixes in the `out_stackdriver` payload parsers, found while auditing the plugin:

- **`try_assign_subfield_int`** — `atoll(obj.via.str.ptr)` was called on a msgpack string that is **not NUL-terminated**, so `atoll` reads past the value into adjacent memory. Copy into a bounded stack buffer and NUL-terminate before parsing.
- **`try_assign_subfield_str`** — `flb_sds_copy(*subfield, ...)` was invoked even when `*subfield` is `NULL`; create the sds via `flb_sds_create_len` in that case.
- **`pack_sds_safe`** — new helper that packs a possibly-`NULL` `flb_sds_t` as an empty string instead of dereferencing it; applied in the operation / sourceLocation / httpRequest packers, which could previously pack `NULL` fields.
- **`init_http_request`** — initialize the sub-fields to `NULL` (with matching `NULL` guards) instead of allocating an empty sds per record.

These are independent of each other and of any larger refactor.

- [x] Unit tests: `ctest -R flb-rt-out_stackdriver` — all `out_stackdriver` runtime tests pass.

author: zhulinsen
body:
## What changed

- Added DSL-level lookahead/repainting bias validation and `strategy validate --bias-check`.
- Added a reusable run-level `DataQualityReport` for data source health plus event/news provider vs proxy coverage.
- Wired the data quality gate into `RunPipeline`, `alphaevo run` CLI output, tiered research context, and `EvolutionPipeline`.
- Paused strategy mutation when event/news data is proxy-dominant or provider coverage is too low.
- Reviewed related GitHub projects and documented takeaways in `docs/competitive_project_review.md`.
- Added `alphaevo.evaluator.maturity`, a report-level research maturity checklist inspired by Qlib, FinRL, TradeMaster, vectorbt, freqtrade, backtrader, OpenBB, and AI hedge fund style analyst workflows.
- Rendered the maturity checklist in Markdown reports so each run shows sample evidence, baseline protocol, robustness, data quality, complexity, and optimization readiness.

## Why

The evolution loop should diagnose data-chain reliability and research maturity before mutating strategy rules. Mature quant projects consistently make baselines, validation protocols, data provenance, and promotion gates visible. This PR brings those checks into AlphaEvo without adding heavy dependencies.

## User/developer impact

- `run` results now carry explicit data-quality findings and surface them in the CLI.
- `evolve` records data-quality findings in the research log and stops mutation when evidence is not reliable enough.
- Markdown reports now include a research maturity checklist, making weak protocol runs harder to mistake for promotable results.
- The competitive review doc captures the external references and follow-up ideas for future optimization work.

## GitHub projects reviewed

- https://github.com/microsoft/qlib
- https://github.com/AI4Finance-Foundation/FinRL
- https://github.com/TradeMaster-NTU/TradeMaster
- https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt
- https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade
- https://github.com/mementum/backtrader
- https://github.com/virattt/ai-hedge-fund
- https://github.com/OpenBB-finance/OpenBB

## Validation

- `python3 -m ruff check src/ tests/ scripts/`
- `python3 -m ruff format --check src/`
- `python3 -m mypy src/alphaevo/evaluator/maturity.py src/alphaevo/evaluator/reporter.py --ignore-missing-imports`
- `python3 -m pytest tests/unit/test_research_maturity.py tests/unit/test_reporter.py` (44 passed)
- `python3 -m pytest tests/unit` (979 passed)
- `python3 -m pytest tests/integration` (20 passed)

## Risks

- Data-quality blocking thresholds are intentionally conservative: provider coverage below 30% or proxy-only coverage above 50% blocks strategy mutation for event/news-dependent strategies.
- Maturity checks are deterministic heuristics, not a guarantee of real-world performance.
- Report output is longer because each Markdown report now includes the maturity checklist.
