author: mrbill700
body:
## What

Adds an on-machine Whisper backend so `/watch` can transcribe caption-less videos without a Groq/OpenAI API key — the audio never leaves the machine. Captions are still tried first; this only changes the *fallback*. Opt in with `WATCH_WHISPER_LOCAL=1` — when set and a faster-whisper interpreter is resolvable, `local` becomes the default fallback backend.

## How

- **New `scripts/whisper_local.py`** — a small bridge that transcribes one audio file with [faster-whisper](https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper) and prints the **same JSON shape** the API backends produce (`{segments: [{start, end, text}], words: [{word, start, end}]}`). Because the shape is identical, frame/transcript alignment and the 0-10s hook microscope work unchanged. Defaults: `large-v3` / `float16` / beam 1 / VAD on; CUDA when available, CPU/int8 fallback.
- **`scripts/whisper.py`** — adds a `local` backend: `_local_python()` resolves the interpreter (explicit `$WATCH_WHISPER_LOCAL_PYTHON`, else the current interpreter if it can import `faster_whisper`), `load_api_key()` returns `("local", "local")` when local mode is on, and `transcribe_video()` / `transcribe_audio()` route to the bridge.
- **`scripts/watch.py`** — `--whisper local` choice.
- **`scripts/setup.py`** — `--check` / `--json` report `ready` with `whisper_backend: local` when local mode is configured, so no API key is requested.
- **Docs** — README capabilities table + a "Local Whisper" section, SKILL.md Transcription section, CHANGELOG 0.3.0.

## Why

faster-whisper (CTranslate2) gives large-v3 quality locally on a consumer GPU. For users who already run a local Whisper setup, or who'd rather not manage an API key / send audio to a third party, this makes `/watch` fully self-hosted for transcription while leaving the existing API backends untouched.

## Notes / tradeoffs

- The interpreter that runs faster-whisper can differ from the skill's own Python (GPU venvs commonly do), hence `$WATCH_WHISPER_LOCAL_PYTHON`. If `faster_whisper` is importable in the skill's own interpreter, that's used automatically.
- The model loads per invocation, so local transcription adds a few seconds of startup vs. an API call.
- No new dependencies on the default (API) path — `faster_whisper` is only imported by the bridge, under the user's chosen interpreter.
- Additive and backwards-compatible; the Groq/OpenAI backends are unchanged.

Tested on Windows + RTX GPU: forced `--whisper local` on a caption-less local file produced both the main transcript and word-level hook timestamps; `setup.py --check` returns 0 with `backend: local`.

author: wfederico97
body:
@
Implements **PNMC-98** — detect critical clinical thresholds and publish a patient risk event.

## What it does
On evaluation persistence, computes risk-threshold breaches (RSBI > 105, PaFi < 150, Cstat < 30; boundary values are safe), sets `alert_triggered`, and—only when breached—publishes a `PatientRiskEvent` (`patientId`, `shiftId`, `bedLabel`, `breachedMetrics[]`).

## Design notes
- `PatientRiskEvent` is an **internal domain event** published via Spring `ApplicationEventPublisher` (in-process), so PNMC-99s `@TransactionalEventListener` receives it identically whether or not Kafka is enabled. `EventPublisherPort`/Kafka is reserved for cross-service integration events.
- `bedLabel` is resolved across contexts via `PatientBedLabelPort` (clinical-owned) implemented by a patient-context adapter (single projection query) — no cross-context entity coupling.
- No Flyway migration: `alert_triggered` already exists in `V1`.

## Tests
- `RiskThresholdEvaluatorTest` (6) — thresholds, boundaries, multiple breaches.
- `PatientBedLabelAdapterTest` (2).
- `EvaluationPersistenceServiceTest` (+5) — publish on breach, no-publish when safe, multi-breach single event, null bedLabel, `alert_triggered` flag.
- Full suite green except a pre-existing, unrelated failure on `develop` (`AuthorizationCoverageTest` / `UserAdminController` missing `@PreAuthorize`, from PNMC-135).

## Scope
Produces and publishes the event only. The async webhook dispatch (PNMC-99), audit log (PNMC-100), and n8n/Telegram workflow (PNMC-101) are separate stories.

author: sushant-mishra-dtu
body:
## What & why

Wires up the **real ASR transcript source** (PHASES item C) and does a focused **environment cleanup**. Until now `on_user_transcript` — the entry point that turns a finalized user utterance into an intent/tool-call — was only fed by a debug driver. This adds the live transcript path and removes the manual `opus.dll` staging fragility.

> Note: this branch was cut from a local `main` that was two commits ahead of `origin/main`, so the PR also carries two prior unpushed commits (`4504b9b` Opus encode/decode across the WS boundary, `2f36821` lookup_rule match tightening). The session's own work is the top commit, `feat: integrate streaming ASR transcript source + env cleanup`.

## ASR integration

- **`ASREngineClient`** (real WebSocket + mock fallback) at `ASR_WS_URL` (default `ws://localhost:8090/api/asr_streaming`), mirroring the existing `DuplexEngineClient`/`TTSEngineClient` pattern. Aggregates Kyutai/Unmute STT-style `Word` messages closed by an end-of-utterance marker (`Marker`/`EndTurn`/`Pause`), or takes a final `Transcript`/`Final` outright -> yields **one finalized transcript per utterance**.
- It is a **transcription-only** consumer of the user's mic audio (fanned out in `on_client_message` alongside the duplex engine) — **not** a second turn-taking audio session, so the "one persistent bidirectional audio session" invariant holds. It is deliberately **not** the duplex inner-monologue (`0x02`), which is the *model's* speech, not the user's.
- New **`_asr_recv_loop`** feeds finalized utterances to `on_user_transcript`. The old `_debug_driver` ("DELETE LATER") is replaced by a clearly-labeled **`_mock_user_loop`** (MOCK_MODE only) that pushes transcripts through the *same* mock ASR path, so mock and real share an identical downstream flow.

**No concurrency-critical code was touched** — `StateMachine`, `AudioMux`, the transition whitelist, the async lock, and drain/interrupt logic are all unchanged (AGENTS.md compliant). All changes are additive.

## Env cleanup

- **`setup.sh`**: installs `pyogg` (ships the native `opus.dll`) and **auto-stages it into `.venv/Scripts/`**, then verifies `opuslib.Decoder` actually loads — removing the previous manual staging. Also anchors to the repo-root venv regardless of cwd, and adds `pytest`/`pytest-asyncio`.

author: etchmuzik
body:
## Summary

Follow-up fixes from an adversarial multi-dimension code review of the driver/hotel-handoff release work (merged in #13). The review scanned 29 changed source files across customer/driver apps, Supabase edge functions, and SQL migrations, then **adversarially verified each finding before fixing** — 8 candidates → **6 confirmed, 2 refuted** as false positives. Each fix was independently re-verified for correctness and regression before commit.

These are the 4 confirmed fixes, isolated onto a clean branch off `main`.

## Fixes

| Severity | Fix |
|----------|-----|
| 🔴 **Critical** | **Paymob payment forgery.** The webhook selected the order row via *unsigned* fields (`special_reference`/`merchant_order_id`/`extras.order_id`) while the HMAC covered only the signed set — so a replayed valid `{signed, hmac}` pair could be redirected to a victim's order UUID and flip it to `paid` with no real payment. Now asserts the signed `amount_cents == total_egp * 100` before the `pending→paid` transition. |
| 🟡 Warning | **expo-push fail-open.** Ran `--no-verify-jwt` and processed requests **unauthenticated** when `PUSH_INTERNAL_SECRET` was unset. Now fails closed (503). |
| 🟡 Warning | **place_order phantom success** (migration 036). The 031 `unique_violation` handler assumed every conflict was the idempotency-key race, so a `short_code` collision returned an all-NULL "success" with no order created. New migration makes the handler key-aware (re-raises non-idempotency conflicts). |
| 🟡 Warning | **OTP resend dead + errors hidden.** The "Resend now" button only restarted the countdown (never re-sent the SMS); verification errors were set in state but never rendered. Both wired up. |

## Refuted (documented, not fixed)

- *Non-constant-time HMAC comparison* — not exploitable under TLS + serverless jitter (defense-in-depth at most).
- *Double `driver_ping` race* — proven impossible via expo-location's event model (callback can't fire before `active` is assigned).

## Test plan

- [x] Customer app: `vitest` 16/16, `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] Shared package: `vitest` 20/20
- [x] Migration 036: verified byte-identical to deployed 031 except the two intended re-raise guards
- [ ] `supabase db push` migration 036 to a branch/staging before prod (full local chain load needs PostGIS)

## ⚠️ Deploy prerequisite

`expo-push` now **fails closed**: confirm `PUSH_INTERNAL_SECRET` is set in every environment **and** every internal caller (RPCs/webhooks via `net.http_post`, plus the paymob-webhook merchant push) sends the matching `x-internal-secret` header — otherwise push notifications will 503/401. Migrations 034/035 set up the secret pipeline, so prod likely has it; verify before merge/deploy.

## Note on the critical fix

The order selector still uses unsigned webhook fields (binding the lookup to Paymob's signed `order.id` isn't possible at webhook time — no Paymob ref is stored pre-payment). The amount assertion is the strongest available control: a replayed payment can now only target an order of the *exact same total*, which is economically pointless for an attacker. `total_egp` is `int not null`, so the strict comparison can't reject a legitimate payment.

author: joshkotrous
body:
PersistentShell builds its child env from a curated allowlist plus the agent's extraEnv and deliberately does not inherit arbitrary process.env, so platform secrets never leak into the agent's shell. That also meant workspace-configured agent env vars (transported into the sandbox as the PENSAR_AGENT_ENV_VARS JSON blob by the platform dispatch layer) never reached execute_command.

Add readSandboxAgentEnv() to parse that blob (fail-soft) and merge it into the shell env at lowest precedence, so the curated essentials (PATH/HOME/…) and any explicit per-agent extraEnv still win. This makes the configured env vars available to every agent's commands without per-agent wiring.

### What does this PR do?

Please provide a description of the issue (if there is one), the changes you made to fix it, and why they work. It is expected that you understand why your changes work and if you do not understand why at least say as much so a maintainer knows how much to value the PR.

### How did you verify your code works?

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes which secrets and config reach the agent shell; behavior is intentional but workspace-provided values (including tokens) become available to every command in that shell.
> 
> **Overview**
> **PersistentShell** now re-injects workspace agent configuration into the child shell by parsing the platform’s `PENSAR_AGENT_ENV_VARS` JSON blob via new **`readSandboxAgentEnv()`**, which only keeps string key/value pairs and **fails soft** (empty object) when the variable is missing or invalid.
> 
> Those vars are spread into the spawned shell env at **lowest precedence**—below the curated `PATH`/`HOME`/… allowlist and below per-agent `extraEnv`—so workspace settings reach `execute_command` without inheriting arbitrary `process.env` or overriding shell essentials.
> 
> Tests cover JSON parsing edge cases, end-to-end visibility in the shell, override behavior, and that unrelated host env vars still do not leak.
>

author: mturnbo
body:
## What

Adds `src/js/data/planets.js` — the static data file that all orbital mechanics modules will import from.

## Contents

- `PLANETS` array: Keplerian orbital elements for Mercury through Pluto
  - `a` (semi-major axis, AU), `e` (eccentricity), `i` (inclination), `L` (mean longitude), `lp` (longitude of perihelion), `lan` (longitude of ascending node)
  - Each element paired with a `*Rate` field giving change per Julian century from J2000.0
- `SUN` constant: origin marker for rendering
- Visual properties per body: `color`, `radiusPx`

## Source

JPL "Keplerian Elements for Approximate Positions of the Major Planets" (Standish 1992/2001, Table 1). Accuracy ~1–2° within a few centuries of J2000 — sufficient for visualization.

## Notes

This is pure data — no logic, no imports. The Kepler solver (PR 3) and epoch utilities (PR 4) will consume it.

author: 1337ninja1337
body:
## What

Caches the in-flight `initSentry()` boot under a module-scoped `pending` promise so a second `initSentry()` call (e.g. on auth-state change) that races the first one awaits the same promise instead of kicking off a second native-bridge handshake. Fixes a real race: two concurrent callers both passed the `initialised` guard (it only flips in the `finally` after the loader awaits), double-loading the SDK and calling `mod.init()` twice.

## How

- `lib/sentry.ts`: added `let pending: Promise<void> | null`. The init body was extracted into an internal `runInit(options)`; the public `initSentry()` keeps the `if (initialised) return` fast-path, then `if (pending) return pending` so a racing caller awaits real completion (not a premature no-op). `pending` is cleared in a `finally` after the await, and reset in `shutdownSentry()` and `__resetSentryForTests()`.

author: frenck
body:
# Proposed Changes

`OrderAwareStruct.unpack_from(buffer, offset)` reordered the whole buffer with `_swap_word_order(buffer)` and then called `struct`'s `unpack_from` at `offset`. The reordering always operates on the region starting at byte 0 (the value lengths it walks sum to `self.size` starting from index 0), so for any nonzero `offset` combined with a non-standard word or byte order it reordered the wrong bytes and returned a wrong value.

For example, with `OrderAwareStruct(">I", word_order="little", byte_order="big")` and the packed value placed at offset 2, `unpack_from(buffer, 2)` returned `0x00000a0b` instead of `0x0a0b0c0d`.

The fix slices the struct-sized region at the offset first, reorders just that region, and unpacks it. As a side benefit it no longer transforms more of the buffer than necessary. `unpack_from` at offset 0, and all offsets under the standard big/big order, are unchanged.

The library itself only uses `unpack` (offset 0) internally, so this is a latent bug on the public `unpack_from` method rather than a regression in the high level client. New tests cover every word/byte order combination at several offsets.

## Related Issues

None.

body:
## What changed
Wires the pregame guided-audio flow into `activity_events`: emits `pregame_start` (on both the full-setup and saved-session entries) and `pregame_complete` (when the audio session finishes) with allow-listed personalization `meta`.

## Why
The pregame guided audio is the product's premium differentiator and currently produces **zero** signal — start rate, completion rate, and clip-vs-timer behaviour are invisible. This is the #1 gap called out in the owner-dashboard work (`docs/admin-metrics-dashboard.md` §5) and surfaced by the activity_events foundation (#296).

## Linear issue
No issue — KC direct request (follow-on from #295/#296). Recommend filing `FV-` "pregame event wiring".

## Stacked on #296
**Base = `feat/activity-events-instrumentation` (#296)**, which provides `recordActivityEvent` / `event-core`. This PR's diff is only the pregame delta. GitHub retargets the base to `main` automatically when #296 merges; if #296 squash-merges, I'll `git rebase --onto main` this branch.

## Acceptance criteria checked
- [x] `pregame_start` fires on `beginFull` (src=full) and `beginFromSaved` (src=saved; also covers "Play saved offline", which delegates)
- [x] `pregame_complete` fires on reaching the card (audio finished), with meta: position, adversity, anchor, prayer_style, audio_completed, network_mode (online/offline)
- [x] Client → `"use server"` action resolves the athlete server-side (no spoofing), restricts to client-allowed events, delegates to the validating server-only writer
- [x] Fire-and-forget — never blocks the flow, never throws, never navigates
- [x] Existing PregameFlow RTL specs still green (action mocked, same pattern as useClipPlayer)

## Screenshots / Loom / preview URL
N/A — no UI change; events are written server-side. (Pregame is athlete-facing but the flow's visible behaviour is unchanged.)

## Risk
Low–medium — touches the hot `PregameFlow.tsx`, but only adds three fire-and-forget calls + one import; the play/setup/saved paths are otherwise byte-for-byte unchanged. The writer no-ops if the `activity_events` table isn't in prod yet (depends on #296's migration), so there is no ordering hazard. Rollback: remove the calls.

## How to test
From `apps/web/`: `npx tsc --noEmit` (0) · `npx vitest run components/pregame/__tests__/pregame-rerun-flow.test.tsx components/pregame/__tests__/pregame-prepare-ahead.test.tsx` (pass) · `npx next lint` (clean) · `npm run build` (green). Manual (after #296's migration is applied): run a pregame session → one `pregame_start` row; finish the audio → one `pregame_complete` row with the meta dimensions.

## Intentionally not done
- `practice_*`, `postgame_open`, `push_click` wiring — follow-ups. (postgame needs KC's OK — its "no order, no tracking" stance was deliberate.)
- Per-clip audio completion meta (clips_played/errored) from `useClipPlayer` — deferred to avoid touching the hottest file in this PR.
- Dashboard consumption of these events — separate follow-up after #296 is in prod.

Author: lead. Pending on this PR: qa-reviewer + frontend-engineer (athlete-UX, hot-file) + kids-privacy-officer (privacy path).

body:
## Summary

First PR of **P08** (the dice-check primitive that P05 unblocked). Introduces the data-driven **`dice-check`** PendingResolution kind and migrates **muster-roll** onto it — the cleanest kind, **zero new verbs**.

**⚠️ Review-gated:** this rewrites the muster card test (`tw-067`) to the new kind/action shape, so per project policy it's opened for your review and **not self-merged** (unlike the P05/P06 PRs, which touched no tests). It's PR-A of a planned stack (PR-B glamour+cvcc · PR-C call-of-home · PR-D body-check).

## What changed

- New `dice-check` kind: `{label, roller?, modifiers (constant|unused-gi), threshold, comparison (gt|gte), onPass?/onFail? (TriggeredActions), continuation (dequeue-only|chain-entry{match,drainSameSource}), requireTargetPresent?, targetCharacterId?/targetInstanceId?}`.
- `applyDiceCheckResolution`: rolls 2d6 (shared `rollForResolution`), sums modifiers dynamically, compares, runs the branch via a small resolution-context dispatcher `applyDiceCheckBranch` (delegates to `applyMove`; more verbs as later kinds land). Chain re-entry is generic scaffold.
- Muster: `modifiers=[unused-gi]`, `threshold 11`, `gte`, `onFail = move` (faction in-play → owner's discard), `continuation chain-entry/target-faction`. Removed `applyMusterRollResolution` / `musterRollActions` / the `muster-roll` kind+action; `resolve-dice-check` action replaces `muster-roll`.

## Review corrections folded in

- Target validated **before** rolling only when `requireTargetPresent` (muster always rolls, no-ops on an already-gone faction via a move fizzle — matches the original).
- Roll/threshold/continuation semantics preserved exactly.

## Verification

- `npm run build` ✅ · `npm run lint` ✅ · `npm run lint:md` ✅
- `npm test` — rules **791 passed** ✅
- `npm run test:nightly` — card suite **4729 passed / 0 failed** (incl. the rewritten tw-067) ✅

## Plan (scoped + adversarially reviewed)

5 of 10 roll kinds collapse (muster, glamour, cvcc-ally-discard, call-of-home, body-check); the other 5 stay bespoke (gold-ring table, seized-by-terror relocation, stay-her-appetite/flattery/faction-influence interaction windows). PR-B/C/D follow once you've validated this approach.

author: jonathanmcsweet
body:
Move the per-box authorized_keys and sudo policy out of host-side
`$ENGINE exec` calls and into the box entrypoint, which reads them from
non-secret run-env values (ISOPOD_AUTHORIZED_KEY, ISOPOD_SUDO) and unsets
them before starting sshd.

This removes the only bootstrap step that required exec, so a box reaches
a working SSH state under any OCI runtime (runc, gVisor, Kata, krun) and
closes the window where sshd was up before the key was installed.

author: alexander-morin
body:
## Description

Updating the workflow to generate `file_metadata/`, which provides a manifest of files for a data release.

**Behavior notes**
- spatial branching logic: removed spatial-specific functions, but there is still a spatial intermediate written, which is now combined with existing artifacts rather than treated as its own terminal `spatial_files.csv`
- Single raw intermediate file (instead of raw or fastq), but source prefix in table still defines raw or fastq
- Assumes one single fastq/ or raw/ (confirmed this is currently always the case)

## Summary of changes

Grouped by what changed, not strictly chronological — some later commits refine work done earlier in the same group.

### 1. MD5 hashing: gsutil → gcloud

- [e468f06](https://github.com/ASAP-CRN/crn-utils/pull/47/commits/e468f0632564755f0a5d84915c7a430822d16e44): Add gcloud-based `gcloud_hash()` to replace gsutil-based `get_md5_hashes()`, defined temporarily in `bucket_util.py` (this will be folded into wf-common `gcloud_ops.py` in a future PR). Remove `checksums.py` as it is no longer used.

### 2. Spatial cleanup

- [3af4920](https://github.com/ASAP-CRN/crn-utils/pull/47/commits/3af492050a9efc4170f395a85e9c01f278180110): removes spatial-specific functions like `gen_spatial_bucket_summary()` and their references. It **does not** remove these references in legacy calls like `get_release_metadata_human()`, as these are expected to be fully deprecated in a future PR.

### 3. Generic raw-bucket inventory + caching

The core of this PR: one generic helper walks the raw bucket's prefixes (artifacts, spatial, fastq/raw) and caches the result as an intermediate CSV, replacing several near-duplicate bucket-walking functions.

- [075a86b](https://github.com/ASAP-CRN/crn-utils/pull/47/commits/075a86bca191e353dc3d3c456f0bff1587a0f41c): makes `gen_bucket_summary()` more generic and uses intermediate .csv for caching (.json are no longer saved); adds `summarize_bucket_prefix()`
- [43c28a1](https://github.com/ASAP-CRN/crn-utils/pull/47/commits/43c28a189358385204d9f2ee183023d9fd87f803): Updates calls to fetch the artifacts and raw file (renamed from `get_fastq_df()`) tables. Placed `artifacts/` query in "raw" search only
- [71966e6](https://github.com/ASAP-CRN/crn-utils/pull/47/commits/71966e6e2e2f476c240ff83a568936618de972b4): renames `gen_bucket_summary()` -> `gen_raw_bucket_summary()` as dev bucket summary deemed distinct enough for two discrete calls.
- [c15eaea](https://github.com/ASAP-CRN/crn-utils/pull/47/commits/c15eaea4e173429f0a519a0e4c668d557be71d77): addresses the overly verbose logging by `gcloud_ls()` and adds logging to `gen_raw_bucket_summary()`

Only files specified in `DATA.file_name` are joined anyways

### 4. DATA table gcp_uri / file_MD5 population

Wires the raw-bucket inventory into `DATA.csv`, and — after finding real examples where this mattered — refines the MD5 reconciliation policy from "always take bucket" to "bucket wins, contributor value is the fallback when no bucket MD5 exists" (composite uploads have no bucket MD5).

- [8e3f26b](https://github.com/ASAP-CRN/crn-utils/pull/47/commits/8e3f26be3f1420ac661a6eb7527d689ec88aeda6): `update_data_table_with_gcp_uri()` -> `update_data_table_with_bucket_metadata()` call now joins file_MD5 as well as gcp_uri; rm `add_bucket_md5()`

Raw bucket always wins if non-NA, but contributor MD5 is taken if the bucket MD5 is NA. This is because for composite uploads no bucket MD5 exists, and I found examples where there was a contributor MD5 (they filled it out locally) but no bucket MD5 (they used composite upload)

### 5. Dev-bucket inventory + curated_files.csv

Ports the dev-bucket listing and `curated_files.csv` generation logic in from `asap-crn-cloud-dataset-metadata`'s `make_release.py`, reusing the same generic inventory helper from group 3, then fixes a duplication bug
found once it was exercised against real multi-manifest datasets.

## Summary

Cleans up the Toka-DOS boot header (the FreeDOS kernel signon) and moves the FreeDOS licensing off the boot screen and onto the C: drive.

**Before:**
```
Loading FreeDOS 123Toka-DOS 3.0  (C) 1997 JTM Soluciones - tongue firmly in chee
k.
(C) 2026 Toka-DOS project. Built on FreeDOS - see NOTICE / GUI About for licensing.
...

All Rights Reserved. This is free software and comes with ABSOLUTELY NO
WARRANTY; you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the
GNU General Public License as published by the Free Software Foundation;
either version 2, or (at your option) any later version.
```

**After:**
```
Loading FreeDOS 123
Toka-DOS 3.0 (C) 1997 General Simulation Works - tongue firmly in cheek.
See C:\LICENSE.TXT for more.
Toka-DOS 3.0 kernel - GIT (build 2043 OEM:0xfd) [compiled ...]
Kernel compatibility 7.10 - WATCOMC - FAT32 support
```

It's assembled at build time by `scripts/license_txt.py` from the single-source `NOTICE` + kernel `COPYING` (no duplicated blob).

Rebuilt KERNEL.SYS (70162 B) via Open Watcom and both committed images (`tokados-hdd.img` gains LICENSE.TXT; `tokados.img` tracks the new kernel so floppy/HDD stay consistent). `kernel/main.c` and `VENDOR.md` carry the modification notes.

author: michael-eng-ai
body:
## Frente 2 (segurança) — hardening dos endpoints publish

### Vulnerabilidade
`app/api/x/publish` e `app/api/linkedin/publish` juntavam o `slug` da requisição direto num caminho de arquivo (`content/x/<slug>.json`), validando o slug apenas como string não-vazia. Um chamador **autenticado** (com o publish secret) podia passar `slug="../../algo"` para ler **qualquer `.json` do disco** e postar o conteúdo. O `catch` ainda devolvia `error.message` cru, vazando caminhos internos e detalhes do driver.

### Correção
- Slug restrito a `^[a-z0-9-]+$` (max 200) — a forma kebab-case que o `slugify` produz —, impossibilitando escapar do diretório de conteúdo.
- Detalhe da falha logado no servidor; resposta genérica ao chamador (`400` para validação, `500` para erro interno).

Aplica-se aos dois endpoints. `pnpm check` (typecheck) passa.

Parte da revisão aprovada (frente 2, achados #1 alta e #2).

author: claudiodavi
body:
## What this does

Adds `--provider` / `--model` flags to `maple init` / `maple update` so a project can
pin its model provider **project-locally**, without depending on a contributor's global
Claude Code config.

The headline win is **OpenCode**. Upstream ships an `opencode.json` with no provider
block and agent files with no `model:` frontmatter — so OpenCode has nothing pointing it
at a provider and every agent falls back to OpenCode's default. This change makes
OpenCode actually usable with a chosen provider in one command:

```bash
maple init --provider openai          # writes opencode.json provider block + per-agent model:
maple init --provider github-copilot
maple init --provider amazon-bedrock
maple init --provider anthropic
```

Each run:

- Patches `opencode.json` with the provider block (merge, not overwrite).
- Stamps per-tier `model:` frontmatter on every agent (deep → orchestrator/architect,
  fast → impl agents, small → docs/rubber-duck/humanizer/spec-kit).
- Persists the choice to `.maple/provider.json` so `maple update` replays it.
- For Claude-native providers (anthropic, bedrock) also writes Claude Code env to
  `scripts/maple/provider.env`.

`maple req` (the Gherkin generator) layers the persisted provider env + `--model` onto
its inline harness call, so requirements run on the same provider the squad uses — on the
deep tier.

## Verification

- Build dance + `go test ./...` → 72 passing in a clean detached worktree.
- Functional smoke: `init --provider bedrock` produces correct per-tier models, valid
  `provider.env`, and `.maple/provider.json`; `--model` override pins all tiers.
- Bedrock slugs verified live against a real account (opus-4-8 / sonnet-4-6 / haiku-4-5).

## Summary

Fixes the My Workstation page: it showed **"Unassigned"** instead of the workstation name, the **timer read 00:00:00**, and it didn't clearly show that an operator runs **multiple** workstations.

The page already supports one tab per workstation — the problem was the data the backend returned.

## Changes

**Backend (`/jobs` list)** — now returns:
- `workstation_code` **and** `workstation_name` (joins `workstation_types`) — previously only `unit_code`, which the frontend didn't read, so everything fell back to "Unassigned".
- `shift_number`, `operation_name`/`step_number`.
- the open step log's `started_at` + `net_work_seconds` (via a LATERAL join) so the live timer has something to count from.

**Frontend (`MyWorkstation.jsx`)** — groups and labels by workstation, showing the friendly **name** (with the unit code as a sub-label) on the station tabs, the station header, and the queue; the active-job header shows the workstation name + shift number. Multiple workstations render as multiple tabs (already supported — now populated).

**Demo seed** — assigns the shift's jobs to the primary operator across **four distinct named workstations** (Band Saw, Bunch Grinder, Rough Mill, Finish Mill) and opens an un-closed step log on the in-progress job so its **timer actually runs** (~12 min).

## Validation
Against Postgres: logged in as `operator`, `GET /jobs` returns 8 jobs across 4 named workstations (no "Unassigned"), `shift_number=2`, and the active job has a real `started_at`. `vite build` passes.

body:
Part of #1016 — the manifest-parity follow-up flagged in PR #1037. Extends the reference-lock bound to the two remaining injection surfaces so reference locks are never injected verbatim *anywhere*.

## What

- **Context-rebuilder block** (`_format_block`): a `reference`-tier lock now renders as its bounded topic with a `tier="reference"` attribute instead of full content; its `retrieve()` call passes `manifest_reference_locks=True` so the budget matches.
- **Search-tool hook** (`Grep`/`Glob`/`Bash` injection, `_format_results`): a reference lock renders as an `[L0-ref] <id>: <topic>` line; same `manifest_reference_locks=True`.

Full text stays available on demand via `aelf locked` / `aelf search`.

## Safety

Same guarantee as PR #1037: `frozen` cost == full content and the flag is inert for frozen locks, so this is **byte-identical until a lock is demoted to `reference`** — the rebuilder/search outputs, and all benchmarks, are unchanged for every existing store.

## Tests

`tests/test_lock_manifest_injection.py`: rebuild block renders reference lock as `tier="reference"` topic (not full content); search-tool renders `[L0-ref]` with topic; frozen locks keep their `[L0]` / verbatim form.

author: hugalafutro
body:
Two non-blocking robustness follow-ups Greptile noted on #334 (it still rated that PR 5/5; neither affects correctness on the current provider set).

## 1. Orphaned log row on native read error
`handleNativeNonStreaming` wrote a 502 and returned when `io.ReadAll` on the upstream 200 body failed, but never finalized the request log row — leaving it stuck in the in-flight state forever (an observability gap for a routing/metering gateway). It now sets `state=failed` + `KindProviderError` + status/duration and calls `updateRequestLog`, mirroring the OK path. No client-visible change.

## 2. `Content string` 502s on array content
`BuildMessageResponse` decoded the OpenAI message `content` as a Go `string`, so a provider returning a structured-content array (or `null`) would fail `json.Unmarshal` and 502 the whole response. `content` is now `json.RawMessage` decoded via `decodeRespContent`, which accepts a string, an array of `{type,text}` parts (concatenated), or null (→ `""`). Not known to occur on the translated path today, but tolerating diverse providers is the gateway's job.

## Tests
- `TestHandleNativeNonStreaming_ReadErrorFinalizesLog` (erroring body → state=failed, KindProviderError, 502).
- `TestBuildMessageResponse_ArrayContent` + `_NullContent`.

`go vet`, full `go test` (proxy + anthropic), and `golangci-lint` clean. No version bump (per repo policy).

body:
This pull request refactors the project-related code to follow a clean, layered architecture by separating the domain, application, infrastructure, and presentation layers. It introduces new interfaces and implementations for the repository and service layers, restructures package organization, and updates imports and test files accordingly. The changes improve maintainability and testability by enforcing clear boundaries between layers.

**Layered Architecture Refactoring**

* Introduced a domain-driven structure for projects, including `Project` in `project.domain.model`, a domain-level `ProjectRepository` interface, and moved DTOs and mappers to `project.application` packages. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1fea771d15e12c8eaa165b01699efd2429f3d9deafe91d0971534f4a696080ecL1-R1) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7739e01e63a0f2019cbcfd7a9541eb04485115b5774b833588e52f246dff67afR1-R14) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c7b68cbff6e5755601f1b64f7d31c9a827aec7f3beed04113790ca513ef6a1f0L1-R1) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-fa1837cda3092912336cde3d138a97ce8f85781f62daa99b6e77181d2f539046L1-L15)
* Created an application service interface (`ProjectService`) and its implementation (`ProjectServiceImpl`) in the application layer, moving business logic out of the old service implementation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-000eb61e898e481c1f096f7c9652ff3ff79dcf8a4963664b2f3dc563d0670776R1-R13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1c5532238051ae56efaa22c642a0b017f36314c8686c610fbc00c024e5282107R1-R86)

**Infrastructure Layer Implementation**

* Added `ProjectRepositoryImpl` in the infrastructure layer to bridge between the domain repository interface and Spring Data JPA, and created `SpringDataProjectRepository` as the JPA repository. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2782b85da1e42db06aa913ee7661a4926c63380ab2ff69bd812b36779c05c093R1-R40) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a4df97a76d9bad83f79f6435ff5d0b76b4646c587792529205add7d83623a634R1-R7)

**Presentation Layer and Test Updates**

* Moved the `ProjectController` and its test to the `project.presentation` package, updating imports and wiring to use the new service structure. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0f82323744e818d566aafd45578975f486689cb7c2bc5c986b27779bdfba6631L1-R6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a44377d246c1ad24cb80064e07fb9b38c4f474eaeae76b3b345a19bc1e6e0120L1-R6)
* Updated all project-related tests and usages to reference the new package structure and repository/service interfaces. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d819c4fd4d49f8e6b79581b79041192257fc7e3b66acea5d13903f2c954b4568L1-L8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-867d6185d11a2cec8b18fc60ec6cfee4b7a5586b66cb6b022cb7e36b00abef23L1-R1) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3ff4832233236ff82e491c577b91ad9149b24135443cb7f417f70db97c3ef961L1-R3) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-3ff4832233236ff82e491c577b91ad9149b24135443cb7f417f70db97c3ef961L27-R27) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-bd762d7f51ebe45dffd1077cf4b13f9ee4c8a8ed09bb7161be56527891d34ef0L3-R7) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-bd762d7f51ebe45dffd1077cf4b13f9ee4c8a8ed09bb7161be56527891d34ef0L33-R34)

**Cleanup of Old Structure**

* Removed the old service, repository, and entity files related to projects, eliminating redundancy and ensuring the new architecture is enforced. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1896ed0fd1af22028015fe4f7756989ef6e0321f81675e99f473f1017e3bfe81L1-L8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-31349e8e2dd67caff0e8a587562bbe84ba4612cfe78c2ee5ee9b1fb82821851cL1-L13) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-dd5976e80d43e2c883d6b4ef73297083a3376f9f10549bffe245c41838178a79L1-L121)

**Other Refactoring**

* Updated all references and imports in the codebase to use the new package and class locations, including in `TaskServiceImpl` and related test files. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b6bdb27379d9af4cd6b6991362b04a7aa49b582ebf8985448f36c1ce1d17f7c8R5) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-70cdcd88d6ed09b3cd59074692c8fe9f2267bc85e1262461964c71d515350cb5L4-R10)

This refactor sets a solid foundation for further extension and maintenance of the project domain.

## What

Adds `docs/workplan/vxture-platform-integration-requirements.md` - the coordination artifact handed to the **vxture platform team** spelling out exactly what the platform must provide for arda to "connect" end to end (entitlement + commands), beyond the OIDC handshake already in place.

### Contents
- **OIDC (channel A)**: client `arda` / `arda-beta` registration to confirm; token must carry opaque `active_org` / `active_workspace`; `arda:subscription` claim deprecation path.
- **Read-only entitlement endpoint (channel B, platform must add)**: arda pulls `state/tier/features/quota` by `(workspaceId, product=arda)`; arda keeps no mirror table (short-TTL cache only).
- **Service-to-service command / invalidate channel (channel C, platform must add)**: `invalidate / seed / wipe` with signature + idempotency key + soft-delete + audit.
- **Enum lock** to the ADR vocabulary (`tier = free|starter|pro|business|enterprise`, `state = trial|subscribed|expired|none`), noting the code's current `ArdaState` `free` vs ADR `none`.
- A **platform confirmation checklist** (10 items) and **end-to-end acceptance criteria**.

Derived from `docs/ADR-entitlement-and-workspace.md` and the identity / entitlement design docs. Docs-only - the release `detect` job skips deploy for docs-only changes.

author: ggiesen
body:
### What does this PR do?
On dnf5 systems (Fedora 41+, AlmaLinux 10), `pkg.list_holds` always returned an empty list even when packages were held. `_list_holds_dnf5` parsed `/etc/dnf/versionlock.toml` via `salt.serializers.tomlmod`, which depends on the third-party `toml` library. `toml` is a CI-only dependency and is **not** bundled in the onedir packages, and the onedir ships Python 3.10 (no stdlib `tomllib`), so the parse failed silently and `list_holds` returned `[]`. With `hold: True`, `pkg.installed` then re-held packages on every run. (`pkg.hold`/`pkg.unhold` work fine -- they shell out -- only reading holds was broken.)

This parses the file with the standard-library `tomllib` instead, falling back to the `toml` serializer on older interpreters where it is installed.

### What issues does this PR fix or reference?
Fixes #69607. Remaining gap from the partial dnf5 versionlock fix in 3006.26 (#69181).

Depends on #69526: `tomllib` is standard library only on Python 3.11+, which the onedir gains in 3006.27. On the 3006.26 onedir (Python 3.10) neither `tomllib` nor `toml` is present, so the fix takes full effect once the Python 3.11 bump lands; the `toml` fallback covers any non-onedir 3.10 environment that has the library installed.

### Previous Behavior
`salt-call pkg.list_holds` on dnf5 logged `Failed to parse dnf5 versionlock file ...: name 'toml' is not defined` and returned `[]`, even with packages held.

### New Behavior
`pkg.list_holds` reads the holds from `/etc/dnf/versionlock.toml` using `tomllib`, returning e.g. `tree-0:2.2.1-4.fc44.*`.

### Platform test matrix
- Bug reproduced on Fedora 44 (dnf5) with the official onedir salt 3006.26 (Python 3.10): `pkg.hold tree` writes `/etc/dnf/versionlock.toml`, but `pkg.list_holds` logs `name 'toml' is not defined` and returns `[]`. The same mechanism applies to every dnf5 platform (Fedora 41+, AlmaLinux 10).
- Fix validated by unit tests exercising the `tomllib` path (run under Python 3.11+), including a regression test (`test_list_holds_dnf5_parses_without_toml_library`) that fails against the previous `tomlmod`-based implementation. The released 3.10 onedir cannot exercise `tomllib`, so the fix lands in shipped packages with the Python 3.11 bump (3006.27, #69526).

A second commit adds unit tests for previously-untested `yumpkg` functions (`version_cmp`, `group_diff`, `list_repos`) to raise coverage of the touched module.

- [x] Tests written/updated

body:
## Summary
- Adds a confirm-gated "Delete" button on each row in the Timesheets card on the Pay page, visible only to `parent_admin`/`parent_co_admin`, so an accidental or incorrectly-dated generated timesheet can be undone.
- Deleting a timesheet also removes its linked payment record (deleted first to satisfy the FK constraint), and logs an audit event.
- Fixes two RLS bugs uncovered while implementing this: `timesheets_delete_manager` previously required `status = 'draft'`, but generated timesheets are always inserted as `'approved'`, so the delete could never actually succeed under the old policy. `payment_records_delete_admin` was also admin-only, inconsistent with every other manager-level action on the Pay page (generate, mark paid). Both policies now allow `parent_admin` or `parent_co_admin`, gated on the record not being `paid`/`locked`.
- Adds `supabase/migrations/0004_allow_timesheet_delete.sql` for databases that already applied `0002_rls.sql`, since the live database needs this policy update manually applied (it can't pick up edits to an already-run migration file automatically).

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [ ] Manually verify in the deployed app: generate a timesheet, delete it, confirm both the timesheet and its payment record disappear and a nanny cannot see the Delete button.

author: manus-use
body:
Adds `score_reachability` — a new Strands tool and CLI subcommand that measures **how reachable** a CVE's vulnerable code path is in a typical deployment.

## Why

`score_exploit_complexity` (already merged) answers *"how hard to weaponise?"*. `score_reachability` answers *"can an attacker actually trigger the vulnerable path in a typical deployment?"* — a complementary and distinct triage signal.

## New tool: `score_reachability`

Six weighted signals combine into a 0–20 score:

| Dimension | Weight | Source |
|-----------|--------|--------|
| Attack Vector | 25% | NVD CVSS v3/v2 |
| Privileges Required | 15% | NVD CVSS |
| User Interaction | 10% | NVD CVSS |
| CWE Reachability Tier | 20% | NVD CWE → HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW |
| PoC Availability | 20% | Trickest CVE index |
| EPSS Score | 10% | FIRST.org EPSS |

Levels: **CRITICAL** ≥15 | **HIGH** ≥10 | **MEDIUM** ≥6 | **LOW** <6

CWE tier classification covers ~60 common CWE IDs (injection/memory-corruption → HIGH; auth-bypass/SSRF/path-traversal → MEDIUM; side-channel/physical → LOW).

All three external sources degrade independently — PoC and EPSS use neutral fallbacks on failure; NVD failure returns an error dict.

## New CLI: `manus-agent reachability`

```
manus-agent reachability CVE-2024-3094
manus-agent reachability CVE-2024-3094 --output json
manus-agent reachability CVE-2024-3094 --save report.txt
```

JSON `--output` routes progress to stderr (pipe-clean stdout).

## VI agent

`score_reachability` added to the tool list + Step 6d in system-prompt workflow.

## Tests

64 new tests (all HTTP mocked, zero real calls). Total suite: **966 passed** (was 902), 0 failures.

author: jakechampion
body:
## What

Lifts the limitation noted in #4095: a consume-by-match enum local built with a **qualified** variant constructor (`Bag.Items(..)`, not the bare `Items(..)`) is now reclaimed too. Previously the `fresh_rcpayload_enum_init` / `fresh_scalar_enum_init` classifiers only matched a bare-ident callee, so a qualified construction's callee — an `ExprFieldAccess` (obj=Enum, field=Variant) — fell through and the enum box + payload leaked, while the identical unqualified form reclaimed.

## How

Both classifiers now resolve the variant by its field name (`variant_enum_owner(structs, fa.field)`), covering the payload-carrying ctor (`ExprCall` → `ExprFieldAccess` callee) and the bare qualified unit variant. Pure frontend analysis — uniform across all three backends, no codegen change.

## Soundness

The qualified construction path **shares** the unqualified lowering, so a bare-ident array payload is array-alias-inc'd at construction exactly as the unqualified form is — the match-site rc-dec is balanced (no double-free). A fresh-literal struct payload rides the same fresh-literal gate from #4095.

## Verification

Verified locally (swap enabled for the self-host driver builds):
- `TestSelfHostEnumQualifiedCtorReclaimIRX86_64` — qualified ctor + **fresh-literal** payload: 40M consume-by-match churn stays bounded (exit 0) where it previously leaked → SIGKILL. Qualified ctor + **bare-ident** payload: 20M churn stays bounded **and** value-correct (17) — proving the construction alias-inc balances the reclaim (no double-free).
- Byte-identical **fixpoint** + **bootstrap** pass — the self-host source uses only unqualified ctors, so these confirm the unqualified path didn't regress. The win is for user programs in qualified style, which native-Go already reclaims (parity, verified directly).

`wgsl-parse` took 25s to compile. The parser was running 7 times and generating 7x as much code. In a subsequent PR, I'll reduce compile times further by including the generated parser code in the source instead of invoking lalrpop in build.rs. This should reduce compile times a lot more.

author: kimayabedarkar
body:
# Add support for unsigned bit-fields in structs

## What this adds

Support for **unsigned** (and `_Bool`) bit-fields in C structs, e.g.

```c
struct flags {
    unsigned int a : 3;      // value in [0, 8)
    unsigned int nibble : 4; // value in [0, 16)
    _Bool  ready : 1;        // 0 or 1
    int    normal;           // ordinary field, unchanged
};
```

Before this change PAL silently mistranslated these: the `: N` width was
dropped and each bit-field became a full-width, separately-addressable field.
That is wrong — C bit-fields are **not addressable** (`&s.a` is illegal) and
**share storage units**, so they do not fit PAL's per-field `ref T` + `pts_to`
model.

## Encoding: refined machine cell + mask-on-write

Each unsigned bit-field is modeled as an ordinary scalar record slot whose
backing cell is the declared underlying machine type **refined to the width**:

```
unsigned int a : N   ==>   (v:UInt32.t{UInt32.v v < pow2 N})
```

(`UInt8/16/64.t` for the other underlying widths.)

- **Reads** are conversion-free: the stored value already has the bit-field's
  logical unsigned type and is used directly (via subtyping) in returns, specs,
  and arithmetic.
- **Writes** mask the RHS to the width — `s->a = e` stores
  `Pulse.Lib.C.BitField.mask_uW N e` — so the stored value satisfies the cell's
  `< pow2 N` refinement. This is exactly C unsigned modular truncation
  (`e % 2^N`), and the masked value's postcondition (`mask == e % pow2 N`) makes
  the truncation provable in user specs (`_ensures(s->a == v % 8)`).
- Defaults are `0` (in range for every `N >= 1`).

Physical bit packing / storage sharing is intentionally **not** modeled: each
bit-field is an independent value. This is sound because a bit-field's backing
cell is never C-address-exposed (`&s->a` is illegal C and never appears in valid
input).

## Why this design over `FStar.UInt.uint_t n`

The natural alternative is to store each bit-field as the parametric,
exactly-`n`-bit integer `FStar.UInt.uint_t n` (= `x:int{0 <= x < pow2 n}`).
We chose the **refined machine cell** instead, for three reasons:

1. **It is the faithful model of C.** A C bit-field genuinely *is* an
   `unsigned int` (or `unsigned char`, ...) whose value happens to be
   range-limited. `(v:UInt32.t{UInt32.v v < pow2 N})` says exactly that.
   `uint_t n` is a mathematical `nat`, a value type C has no notion of.

2. **Reads are conversion-free.** Because the cell already *is* a `UInt32.t`, a
   read is directly usable wherever the field's `unsigned int` value is expected
   — returns, specifications, and integer-promoted arithmetic — with no cast.
   With `uint_t n` every read site would need a `uint_to_t` conversion back to a
   machine type, adding proof obligations and noise to generated code.

3. **Consistency with how PAL already handles unsigned overflow.** PAL lowers
   unsigned `+`/`-`/`*` to width-selected, total library helpers
   (`add_wrap`/`sub_wrap`/`mul_wrap`) that keep values as machine ints and encode
   modular ("wrapping") semantics in their postconditions. The mask-on-write
   design mirrors this one-to-one: a width-selected total helper (`mask_uW`) that
   keeps the value a machine int and states its modular result (`v % pow2 N`) in
   the postcondition. `uint_t n` would introduce a value representation that
   nothing else in PAL uses.

> Note: an earlier justification appealed to *C extraction* ergonomics. That
> reasoning was dropped — PAL is a one-way C→Pulse transpiler with no
> KaRaMeL/C-extraction path, so extraction is not a factor in this decision.

### Why a refinement is still needed

There is no machine type for arbitrary widths (1, 3, 7, 31, ...); the smallest
is `UInt8`. A bare `UInt32.t` only bounds the value `< pow2 32`. The refinement
is what narrows a machine word down to the actual `N` bits, so it carries the
real invariant regardless of which storage width backs the field.

### Why the mask uses `rem`, not `logand`

`mask_uW` truncates by modular arithmetic (`UW.rem v (pow2 n)`) rather than a
bitwise `logand` + `logand_mask` lemma. This is both simpler and more
consistent: the `< pow2 n` bound falls out of "mod by a positive" and the exact
value `v % pow2 n` is the `rem` postcondition, with no bitwise reasoning — and it
uses the same modular primitives as the `add_wrap`/`sub_wrap`/`mul_wrap`
overflow helpers.

## Scope and rejections

- **Unsigned and `_Bool`** bit-fields are supported.
- **Signed** bit-fields are rejected with a diagnostic: their reads need
  sign-extension and their out-of-range writes are implementation-defined
  (C11 6.3.1.3p3), so they are not portable to bake into a verification model.
- **Union** bit-fields are rejected (would need the value encoding layered onto
  the union variant model).
- **Anonymous / zero-width** bit-fields (`int : 3;`, `int : 0;`) are padding and
  are skipped entirely — no record slot, no accessors.

## What it gives us

- Correct translation of a common C idiom that was previously mistranslated.
- Reads for free (subtyping, no conversions).
- Writes that truncate with C unsigned modular semantics, provable in user-facing
  specifications (`_ensures(s->nibble == v % 16)`).
- An encoding that stays uniform across widths and consistent with PAL's existing
  unsigned-overflow handling, keeping the generated Pulse idiomatic.

## Commits

1. `ir:` model unsigned bit-fields as refined machine cells (IR variant, passes,
   emit field/representation helpers).
2. `frontend:` parse unsigned bit-fields; reject signed/union; skip padding.
3. `pulse:` add `Pulse.Lib.C.BitField` truncation helpers (`mask_u8/16/32/64`).
4. `emit:` mask unsigned bit-field writes (C truncation on store).
5. `test+docs:` `bitfields` test + internals documentation.

author: varun1308
body:
## The bug

On prod (`ASYNC_ASSEMBLY=1`), asking for an **unseeded destination** (e.g. Bali) produced contradictory chat messages ending with a **false promise**:

> "Putting your Bali recommendations together now — they'll appear right below in a moment! 🌿"

…but no cards ever appeared, and the progress spinner never resolved.

### Root cause

The `assemble_recommendations` tool **always** created a background job and returned `assembly_started` — **without checking eligibility first**. So the agent narrated the `assembly_started` "coming in a moment" line (system-prompt branch), then the worker ran `runAssembly`, found no candidates, and marked the job `no_eligible_hotels`. The optimistic narration was emitted *before* the job could know the destination was empty, and never retracted.

The old **synchronous** path didn't have this: it ran `runAssembly` (eligibility check included) *before* the model narrated, so the agent said the right thing the first time.

## The fix

Run the cheap, **model-free** eligibility check **before** dispatching the async job.

- **`run-assembly.ts`** — extract `resolveEligibility()`: the model-free decision (`queryCandidates` → preview → runtime-seed). Returns `{assemble: candidates}` when there's real work for the model, else the **terminal** result (preview cards / `preview_seeding` / `no_eligible_hotels`). `runAssembly` now delegates to it → the async pre-check and the worker share one source of truth and can't diverge.
- **`agent.ts`** — `dispatchAssemblyJob` runs `resolveEligibility` first. A terminal result is returned (hydrated) synchronously so the agent narrates the **true** outcome ("no options for that destination yet") instead of a false "coming in a moment". A job is created **only** when there are candidates. Added `isAssemblyStarted` type guard.
- **tests** — +3 `resolveEligibility` unit tests covering the exact Bali case (candidates → assemble; unseeded → terminal `no_eligible_hotels`; preview hotels → terminal preview cards).

## Behavior after

- **Unseeded destination (Bali):** agent says warmly it has no options yet and offers to widen/switch — **no false promise, no orphaned spinner.**
- **Seeded destination (Phuket):** unchanged — job dispatched, cards stream in via polling.

## What

Bumps the `logos-protocol` flake input to `976bc7a` ([logos-protocol#10](https://github.com/logos-co/logos-protocol/pull/10)), which stops `ModuleProxy::callRemoteMethod` from logging cross-module call **arguments** in plaintext (they routinely carry secrets — mnemonics, passwords, tokens). It now logs only `args.size()`, matching every other transport call site.

## Why this is a clean bump

`d5d58e7` (the currently-pinned protocol rev) is the **exact parent** of `976bc7a`, so this pulls in exactly one commit — the logging fix — and nothing else. Only `flake.lock` changes.

Part of a re-pin chain: protocol → {cpp-sdk, module-client} → rust-sdk → module-builder.

author: nipitphand-maker
body:
## Problem

`merge_history()` iterated `set(existing) | set(draws)`, so the `history`
object's key order depended on Python string hash randomization. Every
scrape run could emit `data/hanoi.json` with the categories in a different
order — producing large, noisy diffs (e.g. `vn_hanoi` ↔ `vn_hanoi_vip`
swapping) even when no result actually changed.

## Fix

Iterate `sorted(set(existing) | set(draws))` so output key order is stable
and alphabetical. One-line change; the two protected feature sets
(soft-block defenses + history accumulation) and the dedup/newest-first
merge logic are untouched.

## Verification

Ran `merge_history` under `PYTHONHASHSEED` 0/1/42/1000 — all produce the
same order `['vn_hanoi', 'vn_hanoi_special', 'vn_hanoi_vip']`, matching the
order already committed in `data/hanoi.json`, so existing data won't churn.

author: adelaidasofia
body:
Adds the **Footprint SLA gate** — the budget ratchet that stops the hook fleet's cold-start fan-out from silently re-growing (`SLOW-INSTALL-FROM-LAZY-PLUMBING`). Keystone of the "100% value, near-zero felt footprint" epic (MYC-2348), built first so the cheap fixes land already enforced.

## What it gates (deterministic, hard)
- Per-event / per-tool substrate cold-start **fan-out** vs `footprint-budgets.json`. Per-message events exclude `once: true` (they fire once per session, not per turn); `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` are matcher-gated, so fan-out is computed per tool. `[ -f ~/.claude/hooks/… ]`-guarded maintainer hooks no-op on a fresh install and are excluded.
- **Default-on daemon count** — the default install (`bootstrap.sh`) wires 0.

## Reported (advisory, never gated)
Per-hook cold-start time + per-event felt = `MAX(hook)`, and per-message injected bytes. Hooks for one event run concurrently (felt = `MAX`, not `SUM`) and CI timing is flaky on shared runners, so `--gate` keys only on deterministic axes — a wall-clock gate would teach bypass.

## Shape
`footprint-sla-check.py` ships `--gate` / `--measure` / `--selftest` / `--update-budgets`, fails loud (exit 2) on a missing or unparseable `hooks.json` / budgets file, and carries a built-in negative control (`--selftest`: a 30-hook fan-out trips the gate, a default-on daemon trips it, a within-budget fleet passes, a missing budgets file fails loud). Wired into `ci.sh` via `test_footprint_sla.sh`. Rationale in `0004-footprint-sla-gate.md`; discoverable from `HOOK_FLEET_RESOURCE_GOVERNANCE.md`.

Budgets are `measured + headroom`, so the gate ships green and bites on growth (`_baseline_measured` recorded). The measurement cross-validates the epic's Stage 0 audit exactly: `SessionStart` 14, `UserPromptSubmit` steady 6, `Write` 7, daemons 0.

Sibling-by-design with `audit-sessionstart-boundedness.py` — that governs each hook's *work shape*; this governs the *fleet's footprint*. Local `ci.sh` ran green: py_compile (274 files) + 51 integration tests + shellcheck.

Basic idea is to scan RF phase, fit spectrometer BPM to Acos(PDES+psi), then adjust an offset to correct the error psi.

body:
Adversarial multi-agent audit of the chat/offers/assignment code confirmed five real bugs left open by the D1 "no interactive transaction" design; this fixes them all, with the fixes themselves re-audited.

### Fixes
- **BUG-A (HIGH)** `acceptOffer` writes now run in one atomic `db.batch` (wired D1 `batch()` / libSQL `batch('write')` into the sqlite-proxy driver). No more orphan/duplicate conversations or half-closed siblings. Atomicity proven by a direct rollback test.
- **BUG-B (HIGH)** admin-assign and offer-accept both atomically claim the request (`SET assigned WHERE status IN ('new','offered') RETURNING`); admin-assign closes sibling offers. Two pros can no longer be bound to one request.
- **BUG-C (HIGH)** new DO `/disconnect` endpoint severs live sockets on close/suspend (keeps transcript); new professional D1 kill-switch at connect (closed conv / suspended account).
- **BUG-D (CRITICAL, privacy)** anonymization only stamps `anonymizedAt` when every DO transcript purge succeeded; on failure it leaves the row for the retention cron to retry instead of abandoning live PII.
- **Capacity leak (MEDIUM)** `releaseAssignmentsForRequest` status-guards each close and decrements capacity only when it actually closed the row.

### Verification
biome ✓ · typecheck (0 new errors) · 88/88 vitest (+4 kill-switch tests) · build ✓ (37/37 pages) · batch-atomicity proof ✓ · adversarial re-audit of the diff (2 follow-up findings found and fixed).

author: copilot
body:
`docker.yml` was building the echo binary from Rust source at CI time and resolving the bins release tag at runtime from `BINS_VERSION.txt` — violating the rule that docker must only consume published, pinned artifacts. There was also no prepare step to update those pins before a release.

## docker-assets.yaml (new)
Minimal pinned facts for `toolshed-echo`:
```yaml
assets:
  toolshed-echo:
    release-tag: bins-v0.1.57
    version: 0.1.0
    # sha256 values are populated by the release prepare step.
    sha256:
      amd64: ""
      arm64: ""
```
`sha256` placeholders are replaced with bare hex digests by the prepare step on first docker release.

## docker.yml
- **Removed**: `Get bins version`, `Install Rust toolchain`, `Build echo binary`, `Strip echo binary`
- **Added**: `Get echo asset info` (reads pinned values from `docker-assets.yaml` via yq) + `Download and verify echo binary` (curl + `sha256sum -c` against pinned hash — no GPG/checksum file dance)
- OCI tarball/image tag naming switches from `v{bins-version}` → `v{echo-version}`
- `should-run` paths: drops `BINS_VERSION.txt` + `rust/echo/**`, adds `docker-assets.yaml`

## _release.yml — `# DOCKER ONLY` prepare block
Mirrors the existing `# BAZEL ONLY` block. When `type=docker`:
1. Resolve latest `bins-` release tag + fetch its SHAs
2. Read echo version from `rust/echo/Cargo.toml` via yq (no cargo install needed)
3. Read current `docker-assets.yaml` state
4. Use `bson` to emit + execute yq commands updating `release-tag`, `version`, and per-arch `sha256`; fails loudly if the echo asset isn't present in the bins release

## Manifest/publish pipeline
- `docker-manifests.yml`: toolshed-echo tag/artifact-pattern uses `{echo-version}` instead of `{bins-version}`
- `_publish_release.yml`: replaces `Get bins version` (reads `BINS_VERSION.txt`) with `Get echo version` (reads `docker-assets.yaml`); substitutes `{echo-version}` in manifest generation

## CI wiring
- `releasing.yml`: adds `docker` to the matrix type list; adds `docker/build/VERSION.txt` + `docker-assets.yaml` to `should-run` paths
- `publishing.yml`: adds `docker-assets.yaml` to `should-run` paths

author: claude
body:
Thanks for asking me to work on this. I will get started on it and keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress.

> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>tool-scout: weekly modern-CLI scan</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## tool-scout: weekly modern-CLI scan — 2026-06-23
> 
> Confirmed. The headline finding is real and even more clear-cut than a typical "adopt" — `sesh` isn't a new tool to introduce, it's a tool the repo already **ships config for and calls at runtime** but never **detects**. The gap is precisely two things:
> 
> - **No `HAVE_SESH` in `zsh/tools.zsh`** (grep shows zero matches there) — yet `sesh` already appears in the `core-doctor` tool-list tokens (`functions.zsh:118,183`), the wired-integration table (`functions.zsh:655`), the Ctrl-G binding (`bindings.zsh:41`), the shell picker (`fzf.zsh:144-156`), the tmux popup script (`tmux/scripts/tmux-sesh.sh`), a seeded `sesh/sesh.toml.example`, and `core.manifest`.
> - **No `sesh` row in `PORTING-MATRIX.md`** — so a fresh box has no install guidance and silently drops to the find+fzf fallback.
> 
> Here's the relayed proposal.
> 
> ---
> 
> # /tool-scout report — whole modern-CLI stack (2026-06-23)
> 
> **Bottom line:** the stack is mature and well-chosen. Almost every "modern alternative" out there is a sidegrade, not an upgrade. There is exactly **one clear win**, and it's an integration the repo already half-shipped.
> 
> ## 1. ADOPT — `sesh` detection (finish what's already wired) ✅ *verified directly*
> 
> **What:** smart tmux session manager (Go, zoxide-aware, git-repo-named sessions). Core already drives it from `fzf.zsh` (Ctrl-G) and the tmux `prefix+f` popup, with a graceful find+fzf fallback.
> 
> **The gap:** every layer references `sesh` *except* detection and packaging docs. So `core-doctor` probes it via raw `command -v` with no install line, and a bare box quietly degrades with no signal as to why.
> 
> **Adoption cost — packaging is the one catch:** in AUR (2.26.2), Homebrew, nixpkgs, pkgsrc, conda — but **not** Arch-official, Alpine, Fedora, openSUSE, Gentoo, or Debian. So most of the fleet uses `go install github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/v2@latest` (note the **v2** module path) or `mise use -g`. That's the same script/cargo/mise fallback the matrix already documents for starship/yazi/atuin, and `go` is already a pinned mise runtime — the build path exists everywhere.
> 
> **The change is small:** add `_have sesh && HAVE_SESH=1` to `tools.zsh`, add a `sesh` row + go-install footnote to `PORTING-MATRIX.md`. No load-order impact, **no `core.manifest` change** (the `.example` is already listed). Optionally a `sesh)` arm in `_core_wired` — though since sesh has no persistent shell hook, presence ≈ wired, so the existing tool-list token may be enough.
> 
> **Recommendation: adopt** — pure upside; it makes detection/doctor/matrix tell the truth about a dependency the code already has.
> 
> ## 2. WATCH — `television` (tv)
> Rust fuzzy finder (nucleo + ratatui, channel-based). Genuinely good and active, but **not an fzf replacement for this stack's usage**: fzf is load-bearing through `FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS` theming, three custom zle widgets, every `fif`/`fbr`/`fcd` helper, and `fzf-tab` (which has no tv equivalent). Packaging is thin (Arch extra; cargo/mise elsewhere). *Revisit only if you ever want a Telescope-style launcher alongside fzf.*
> 
> ## 3. WATCH — `jujutsu` (jj)
> Git-compatible Rust VCS, strong trajectory (~27k stars, used at Google). But **v0.42, still pre-1.0** with upstream warning of on-disk format breaks before 1.0 — disqualifying for a vendored Core that pins everything for reproducibility. It also replaces nothing Core ships. *Revisit at 1.0.*
> 
> ## Direct-upgrade scan — incumbents all hold
> - **delta vs difftastic** — complementary, not competitive: difftastic can't emit applyable patches and scales poorly on big diffs; delta stays the right git pager. **Skip.**
> - **eza** — moved to `eza-community` org, maintained; lsd is slower with no extra feature. **Stay.**
> - **atuin** — v18.13 (Mar 2026) is a feature release, not a method shift; normal freshness-bump cadence. **Stay.**
> - **mise vs proto/aqua** — mise still the default polyglot manager; your `lockfile=true` + native-shims is current best practice. **Stay.**
> - **carapace, fzf, bat, fd, ripgrep, zoxide, btop, duf, dust, procs, yazi, hyperfine, ouch, lazygit, jq/yq, sd, gum, tealdeer** — all current category leaders, no 2025–2026 displacer found. **Stay.**
> 
> ---
> 
> **My take:** the only thing worth doing this round is landing `sesh` detection properly — it's a doc/code-truth fix more than a "new tool," low-risk, and the `doc-audit` routine would eventually flag the same drift. The other two are watch-list items, and the rest of the stack is honestly "stay put."
> 
> Want me to implement the `sesh` detection + porting-matrix row (with a `CHANGELOG.md` entry and `make audit` before a PR)? I'll only touch files if you say go.
>

author: matjmiles
body:
## Why

The toolkit ships the pedagogical knowledge files *and* the per-step audit tools, and the README has a marketing-level "Architecting a course" section — but there was no concrete, ordered **walkthrough** an agent could follow to run a course design end to end. So an agent acting on a prompt like *"architect a redesign — start with the CLOs and work outward"* had all the pieces but no orchestration, and tended to free-style the pedagogy instead of grounding each step in the right knowledge file + tool.

This surfaced while dry-running that exact workflow on a real course as a documentation/usability test (companion to #121, which added the AGENTS.md routing pointer).

## What this adds

**`docs/course_design_workflow.md`** — the shared backbone **CLOs → assessments → modules → rubrics → workload**, with the knowledge file and tool named at each step, written as two flows:

- **Flow A — Redesign:** starts from a `course_audit.py --full` baseline, then a scope decision (refine / re-derive / rebuild), then the backbone.
- **Flow B — From scratch:** starts from course purpose + level, derives CLOs fresh, then the same backbone.

A "where the two flows differ" table makes the divergence explicit — both converge on the identical backbone from the assessment step onward. Includes the safety gates (local-files-source-of-truth, sandbox-first, confirm-before-write, re-audit-after) pulled from AGENTS.md, and a tool index.

Plus a one-line pointer to the guide from the README's "Architecting a course" section.

## Verification

- All **8 tool links** referenced in the guide verified to resolve to real files under `lib/tools/` (no broken links — the repo's recent stale-link cleanup in mind).
- Pre-commit hooks (ruff / actionlint / shellcheck) passed; no Python touched.
- Captured from an actual run of the redesign workflow, not written abstractly.

## Scope / risk

Docs-only: one new file + a one-line README pointer. 154 insertions, 0 deletions. No code paths touched. Independent of #120 and #121 (no overlapping lines).

author: deepak-kesavan
body:
## What

Allow a **platform API key (bearer token)** to call the `rotate` endpoint, so credentials can be rotated **via the API** for automation. Session org-admins keep rotate (unchanged).

## Why

UN-3586 (RLDatix on-prem blocker) asks for "rotate credentials **through the API**" for operational automation. **Confirmed empirically on staging (`globe.unstract.com`, main):**

```
GET  …/api/deployment/                     → 200   (valid key, bearer auth + reads work)
POST …/platform-api/keys/<id>/rotate/      → 403   "Only organization admins can manage platform API keys."
```

Rotation via a **logged-in admin session** already works (the UI's rotate button), but rotation with a **platform API key** was blocked — the `rotate` endpoint's `IsOrganizationAdmin` gate rejects service accounts, and a platform API key authenticates *as* a service account. So the token/automation path did not exist. This PR opens it.

## How

- New `CanRotatePlatformApiKey` permission on the `rotate` action:
  - **Session callers** → must be org admins (unchanged behavior).
  - **Platform API key callers** → must present a **`full_access`** key (the admin-equivalent tier, which already permits DELETE). `read`/`read_write` keys cannot rotate.
- **Why `full_access` (not any bearer key):** `rotate` returns the new key value, so letting a lower-tier `read_write` key rotate a `full_access` key would let it read that key's new secret and escalate `read_write → full_access`. Requiring `full_access` closes that path — a `full_access` caller rotating any key gains no privilege (it's already the top tier), matching what a session admin can do.
- **Org scoping unchanged and still enforced**: the auth middleware validates the URL `org_id` against the key's immutable org (403 on mismatch), and the viewset queryset is org-scoped — a key can only rotate keys **in its own organization**. Cross-org is impossible.
- `rotate` already returns the new key once via `PlatformApiKeyDetailSerializer` — no serializer change.

Note: an earlier revision restricted key callers to *self-only* rotation; that wasn't a ticket requirement and was dropped in favor of the `full_access`-tier gate above (a `full_access` key may rotate any key in its org, matching a session admin) — which also closes a privilege-escalation path flagged in review.

## Can this PR break any existing features? If yes, please list possible items. If no, please explain why. (PS: Admins do not merge the PR without this section filled)

No.
- Session-admin rotation is **unchanged** — the permission was only widened, additively, to also admit platform-API-key callers to an existing endpoint.
- **Cross-org isolation is unchanged** (auth middleware + org-scoped querysets; independently verified).
- No model, serializer, or migration change.

## Database Migrations

None.

## Env Config

None.

## Notes on Testing

- **Staging (`globe.unstract.com`, main) baseline:** bearer `rotate` → **403** (blocked); same key reads deployments → 200. Confirms the gap.
- **Dev (`deepak-unstract-dev`, `snapshot.1782909801`):** verified live against the new pod — a **`full_access`** key rotating a **different** key via bearer → **200** + new key; a **`read_write`** key attempting rotate → **403** (tested 3×, all denied — the privilege-escalation path is closed); session admin rotate → **200**. Cross-org remains blocked (auth middleware + org-scoped queryset).

## Related Issues or PRs

- Jira: https://zipstack.atlassian.net/browse/UN-3586
- Builds on UN-3405 (`full_access` tier).

## Checklist

I have read and understood the Contribution Guidelines.

author: sergioestebance
body:
## What

Replaces the silent multi-minute **"Processing"** a large dataset shows while it's prepared with a **live bar** — bytes percent, a running row count, a client-computed **ETA**, and a phase stepper (Uploading → Processing → Finalizing → Ready). Wired on the dataset **detail page** and in the **bulk upload drawer**.

## Why

A customer onboarding a multi-GB dataset waits minutes on a spinner with no feedback — it reads as hung. The upload itself is already robust (presigned S3, ADR-032); this makes the *preparation* legible.

## Design — see `dev/docs/adr/034-dataset-processing-progress.md`

Locked via an ADR (with a red-team pass folded in as v2). Load-bearing decisions:

- **Broadcast-only, never persisted.** The normalize job emits progress over the existing **export SSE spine** (`BroadcastService` → tRPC subscription) — **zero new schema, zero migration**. No per-flush DB writes on the heaviest path.
- **`getById` is the terminal authority.** The durable `Dataset.status` (ADR-032) reconciles the bar on subscription connect / `done` / SSE-gap, so the bar **can never hang** even if a progress event is dropped — and never overshoots (bytes measured input-side).
- **One subscription per project, client-filtered** by the watched `datasetId` set (detail = 1, drawer = N) — sidesteps the per-tenant 50-listener ceiling.
- The `runInline` no-worker large-file hazard is explicitly **out of scope** here (a separate ADR-032 amendment) rather than buried in this UX change.

### Red-team-caught fixes (folded before this PR)
- Terminal `done`/`error` goes through the **plain** broadcast path (not the dropping rate limiter) and only **after** the durable commit (I-ORDER) — otherwise the bar could strand at 99%.
- Denominator is the **input** HEAD size, not the output `sizeBytes` column (which doesn't exist mid-job) — otherwise the bar overshoots on an expanding CSV.
- `dataset_progress` registered in `ALL_EVENT_TYPES` or delivery is silently same-pod-only.

## Testing

- **Producer** (`dataset-normalize.job.progress`): terminal emitted strictly after the `ready` commit; input-side denominator; failure commits `failed` then emits terminal error.
- **View logic** (`datasetProgressView`): durable status overrides a stale tick (un-hangable); never exceeds 100%; ETA from byte-rate.
- **Broadcast wire** (`dataset-progress`): real `BroadcastService` round-trip, schema parse, both paths, tenant isolation.
- `pnpm typecheck` clean; existing normalize / chunk-writer / broadcast suites unbroken (70/70 across the touched suites).

## Not in this PR
- **Live browser pass** with a real multi-GB upload — needs a running dev stack + valid dev S3 creds; the SSE wire is proven deterministically by the integration test. Best run via `/prove-them-wrong` against this PR once the stack is up.
- Surfacing the failing line number on `failed` (deferred — generic message for v1).

## Spec
`specs/datasets/dataset-processing-progress.feature`


## Deployment Impact

None. No database migration, no new environment variables, no charts/services/infra changes.

- **Schema:** none — progress is broadcast-only and reuses the existing `Dataset` columns from ADR-032.
- **Runtime:** adds one Redis pub/sub event type (`dataset_progress`) on the existing `BroadcastService` channel set and one tRPC SSE subscription (`dataset.onDatasetProgress`). No new services or workers.
- **Self-hosted:** unaffected — progress is best-effort and degrades cleanly with or without Redis; the durable dataset status stays the source of truth.
- **Docs:** adds ADR-034 (which is why this check flagged the PR).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added live dataset-processing progress (determinate percent clamped to 100%, rows, ETA, and phase stepper), with indeterminate mode when totals are unknown.
  * Bulk upload drawer now shows independent per-dataset progress during uploading/processing.
  * Dataset pages now use a unified processing/status panel with retry support for failures.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Ensured terminal outcomes are authoritative (no stuck/incorrect completion), and progress reconciles safely after refresh or missed updates.
* **Tests**
  * Added unit/integration coverage for progress views, ETA, reconciliation, and multi-dataset isolation.
* **Documentation**
  * Added ADR-034 and an end-to-end feature spec.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: rbaumier
body:
Closes #6965

## Problem
`rust-unit-error-result` flagged `type ParseResult<T> = Result<T, ()>;` — a module-private parser-combinator type alias (nom/winnow style) where `Err(())` is the conventional "input did not match" rejection signal and the error detail is collected out-of-band by the top-level parser.

## Fix (structural, no allowlist)
New helper `is_private_type_alias_rhs` exempts a `Result<_, ()>` `generic_type` only when it is the declared RHS (`type` field) of an enclosing `type_item` that:
- is a free-standing module-scope alias (not an associated type in an `impl`/`trait` body), and
- carries no `visibility_modifier`.

Pure AST position + visibility — no name/value/project inspection. A named private alias is a deliberate, auditable author decision with no consumer to mislead.

## Still flags
- `pub` / `pub(crate)` / `pub(super)` aliases (any visibility modifier present)
- direct function-return `Result<_, ()>`
- `Result<_, ()>` nested deeper than the alias RHS (e.g. `Box<Result<T, ()>>`)
- associated `type Assoc = Result<_, ()>;` in an `impl`/`trait` body

## Tests
7 new cases (2 positive, 5 negative controls). All 54 `rules::rust_unit_error_result` tests pass.

author: cedricconday
body:
The "Tips for Writing Parquet Files" page documents `ROW_GROUP_SIZE` and notes that the reader uses row-group min/max metadata for predicate pushdown, but it does not mention the most effective way to take advantage of that pruning: **sorting the data on commonly-filtered columns before writing**.

Sorting makes each row group's min/max ranges tight and non-overlapping, so highly selective queries on those columns scan far fewer row groups. This comes up regularly (e.g. when compacting Parquet files by a key), so I added a short subsection with an example next to the existing row-group tips.

Targeted `docs/current`. Happy to also apply it to `docs/lts` if youd like.

The CN verifier now runs the round-based BSP batch drainer (it only drains a channel when a code_ctrl manifest is present). RemoteEvalClient still used the old per-task protocol (enqueue code_queue, poll result_queue, no manifest), so its eval task sat in code_queue forever and the npu_remote eval hung.

Each evaluate() now ships a count=1 batch: enqueue the task to code_queue, then a code_ctrl manifest (LAST), collect the verdict from result_queue, and drain the result_ctrl manifest so nothing orphans. Queue names are namespaced by host_id/server_id via relay_batch helpers (default bare = single host/server); make_eval_fn threads RELAY_HOST_ID/RELAY_SERVER_ID through.

Verified: 12 unit tests (fake BSP drainer + preserved infra/timeout/retry behavior) + 221 geak suite green; live round-trip against the CN drainer returned a verdict in 38s (correct=true on a torch decoy, host_id-isolated smoke).
