author: kpa-clawbot
body:
# Partial fix for #1749 — MQTT watchdog escalation + panic recovery + tick exposure

Red commit: 9912bbb3e9ecb5a3cd1e093cf40ce071aae22b84 (CI run: https://github.com/Kpa-clawbot/CoreScope/actions/runs?branch=fix%2Fissue-1749)

## Problem
Production CoreScope v3.9.1 (and a more recent prod recurrence on 2026-06-30 with the wcmesh source on `ssl://mqtt2.wcmesh.com:8883`) showed two distinct watchdog failure modes:

1. **Per-source paho machinery dies silently.** `IsConnectedFn` returns false; paho's `SetAutoReconnect(true)` never retries. The watchdog's `processLivenessTransition` deliberately stays silent on `LivenessDisconnected`, trusting paho to recover — so there is no escalation path when that trust is misplaced.
2. **Watchdog goroutine death.** Three sources went silent within ~60s of each other; no `WATCHDOG` log lines for 75 min. The most plausible single point of failure is a panic inside `emit` (e.g. a blocked log pipe) killing the loop with no defer/recover.

## Changes

**`cmd/ingestor/mqtt_watchdog.go`**
- Added `disconnectedReconnectMultiplier = 5` constant.
- Added `DisconnectedSinceUnix int64` (atomic) on `SourceLivenessState`. Stamped on the first tick the source is observed disconnected; cleared on any non-disconnected tick.
- `processLivenessTransition` now escalates: when `(now - DisconnectedSinceUnix) > multiplier × threshold`, emits a `WATCHDOG ESCALATION` WARN and calls `maybeForceReconnect` (subject to existing `forceReconnectThrottle`). Distinct from the existing `LivenessStalled` path so operators can grep escalation events independently.
- Added package-level `watchdogLastTickUnix atomic.Int64` + `WatchdogLastTickUnix()` getter. The loop stamps it BEFORE per-source processing — a wedged source-handler does not freeze the clock for an external observer.
- `runLivenessWatchdogLoop` wraps each per-source `processLivenessTransition` call in `func() { defer recover; ... }()` so a panic in `emit` (or in any per-source code path) is logged and skipped, not fatal. The loop continues to the next source and the next tick.

**`cmd/ingestor/stats_file.go`**
- Added `WatchdogLastTickUnix int64` field on `IngestorStatsSnapshot` (additive, `omitempty`); populated from `WatchdogLastTickUnix()` each stats tick.

**`cmd/server/mqtt_status.go`**
- `MqttStatusResponse` gains `WatchdogLastTickUnix int64` (additive, `omitempty`) sourced from the ingestor stats file; surfaced via `GET /api/mqtt/status`.

**`config.example.json`**
- No new config field added — the multiplier is a code constant (5×) per the issue's "N×threshold (e.g. 5×)" recommendation. The active per-source `threshold` is the 5-minute scan threshold hard-coded at the sole `runLivenessWatchdog` callsite (`cmd/ingestor/main.go:460`: `runLivenessWatchdog(60*time.Second, 5*time.Minute)`), so escalation fires at ~25 minutes (5 × 5min) of continuous disconnect — plus a deterministic per-source jitter of 0..30s (#1810 round-1, see Taleb #4) to avoid synchronized escalation across N sources sharing an upstream broker outage.

## Acceptance (#1749)
- [x] Persistent `LivenessDisconnected` > N×threshold → force-reconnect + WARN
- [x] Watchdog goroutine liveness clock exposed (`WatchdogLastTickUnix` in `/api/mqtt/status`)
- [x] Test: `IsConnectedFn` false for >5×threshold → assert `ForceReconnectFn` invoked at least once
- [x] Test: panic in `emit` → assert loop recovers and continues ticking

## Test plan
- 4 new tests in `cmd/ingestor/mqtt_watchdog_1749_test.go` (all RED on master, GREEN on this PR).
- Existing watchdog tests (`mqtt_watchdog_force_reconnect_test.go`, `mqtt_reconnect_test.go`, r1/r2/m1 suites) continue to pass — the escalation path is additive.

## Preflight
- TDD: red commit pushed and asserted to fail BEFORE green commit landed.
- PII grep: clean on diff and PR body.
- Worktree: `_wt-fix-1749` on branch `fix/issue-1749`.

author: ian-t-adams
body:
## What & why

Proactively upgrades the **vitest** dev dependency in `app/web` from `3.2.6` → **`4.1.9`** (latest 4.x). This is a follow-up to the just-merged Dependabot consolidation (#124). Dependabot has **not** opened a vitest-4 PR yet (it's on a weekly schedule), so we're getting ahead of it.

vitest is a **dev-only** test framework — no production/runtime code is affected.

## Scope (deliberately narrow)

Only the vitest bump is included here. The other pending majors are intentionally **left out**:
- **eslint 9 → 10**: BLOCKED — `eslint-config-next@16` peer-requires `eslint ^8 || ^9`.
- **@azure/monitor-query 2.0**: deliberately capped.

So vitest 4 was the only safe pending major.

## What vitest 4 required

Vitest 4 switched its default code transformer from **esbuild to oxc** (it now bundles **Vite 8**). Vite 8 removed esbuild's `jsx` option from `ESBuildOptions`, which made the existing config both:
- emit a runtime warning (`Both esbuild and oxc options were set. … esbuild options will be ignored`), and
- fail `next build`'s TypeScript check (`'jsx' does not exist in type 'ESBuildOptions'`).

Minimal, surgical fix in `vitest.config.ts` — migrated to the documented oxc equivalent:

```diff
- esbuild: { jsx: "automatic" },
+ oxc: { jsx: { runtime: "automatic" } },
```

(oxc's documented default for `JsxOptions.runtime` is already `"automatic"`, so this preserves the original intent — component test files don't need an explicit `import React`.) No test files or snapshots needed changes; the suite uses no snapshots and none of the removed/deprecated config keys (`workspace`, `environmentMatchGlobs`, `poolMatchGlobs`).

## Verification (full `app/web` CI gate, run in order)

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm ci` | ✓ 438 packages, 0 vulnerabilities; lockfile coherent (vitest + all `@vitest/*` deduped to 4.1.9) |
| `npm run lint` (`eslint .`) | ✓ **0 errors**, 19 warnings (all pre-existing react-hooks warnings; CI has no `--max-warnings`) |
| `npm test` (`vitest run`) | ✓ **113 passed** (8 files), warning gone |
| `npm run build` (`next build`) | ✓ compiled + TypeScript check + static generation all pass |

## Files changed

- `app/web/package.json` — vitest `3.2.6` → `4.1.9`
- `app/web/package-lock.json` — regenerated (vitest + `@vitest/*` internals → 4.1.9)
- `app/web/vitest.config.ts` — `esbuild`→`oxc` JSX option migration (see above)

author: emirongrr
body:
## Summary

- Loom's cross-L2 keystore promise requires at least one production L2 verifier; none currently exists.
- This decision record (`docs/decisions/0008-op-stack-l2-keystore-verifier.md`) establishes the design for the first one: **OP Stack (Base / Optimism)**.
- Follows the pattern and change-rules from `ARCHITECTURE.md` (decision record required before adding a new proof verifier).

## Approach decided

**OP Stack `L1Block` precompile + EIP-1186 storage proof** (Option A):

1. Read `L1Block(0x4200...0015).stateRoot()` as the trusted L1 state root — no bridge, oracle, or Loom-operated service.
2. Accept a caller-supplied `eth_getProof` output proving `LoomKeystore._configs[identityId]` on Ethereum L1.
3. Verify account trie → storage trie → decode `KeystoreConfig` fields on-chain.
4. Return false (not revert) on any mismatch, malformed proof, or stale version.

Options considered and rejected: `DisputeGameFactory` finalized output root (L2→L2 indirection, per-deployment ABI drift), generic cross-chain standard (no mature standard yet).

## What this record covers

- Storage slot derivation for `_configs[identityId]`
- Acceptance conditions (positive + negative vectors)
- Per-chain deployment model (one instance per OP Stack chain)
- Residual risks: sequencer liveness for root currency, trie library correctness, storage layout drift, L2 upgrade

## What comes next (separate PRs)

- `docs/security/threat-model.md` update
- `OPStackL2KeystoreVerifier.sol` implementation
- Storage layout pin test
- Testnet rehearsal + `keystore-proof-profile.md` evidence
- Independent audit before production deployment

## Test plan

- [ ] Decision record reviewed against `docs/design/keystore.md`, `docs/decisions/0003`, and `docs/operations/keystore-proof-profile.md` for consistency
- [ ] No behavior change in this PR — documentation only

author: sukramj
body:
Docs-only. Raises the `bridge.Registry` migration from a cosmetic wrap to the **architecturally-complete** design, in response to the requirement that this be done architecturally soundly and safeguarded — not the simple version.

## ADR 0047 (new)
Records the decision that the `bridge.Service`/`Registry` contract becomes the **mandated** wiring path for every north-bound surface:
- Each surface is a `bridge.Service` that **owns its lifecycle in its own package** (as `webhook.Outbound` already does) — **no thin shims in `cmd/`**; `cmd/openccu-loom` becomes a composition root.
- **Registration order = boot-dependency order**, made explicit and test-pinned (not implicit in `defer` LIFO).
- The **MQTT supervisor is encapsulated inside the MQTT service**: registry owns process lifecycle, the config-watcher owns runtime reconfiguration. The `Service` interface is **not** grown with hot-swap.
- **MCP is a REST sub-mount**, not a peer service (no dishonest no-op Service).
- Health aggregates through `Registry.Health()` into `/health`.
- A **registration-completeness guard** prevents any future surface from bypassing the contract — the structural lock.
- Alternatives (thin `cmd` shims; a `SupervisedService` capability; no-op MCP service; leave A4 half-adopted) considered and rejected/deferred with reasons.

## Plan rewrite
`docs/plans/bridge-registry-migration.md` rewritten to execute ADR 0047, with the **boot-dependency graph analysis up front** and the full safeguard suite: registration-completeness guard, ordering characterization (golden), rollback fault-injection, goroutine-leak guard per service, health aggregation, per-surface behavioural equivalence. Effort raised S–M → **M**.

## Roadmap
Item updated: architecturally-complete framing, ADR-linked, effort M, still sequenced directly after A4.

No code change; `TestMarkdownLinksValid` green.

author: tomjn
body:
## Summary

Adds a physically-correct 3D terrain preview to the **Content → Maps → map detail** page for installed maps, by extracting the map's heightmap through **unitsync** (`GetInfoMap "height"`) — pure static SMF parsing, no engine boot, no decompile. The existing `MapPreview3D` (three.js) component is reused: the colour minimap is draped over the heightmap displacement.

Investigation first ruled out the Lua `SyncedCtrl#Ground` APIs (they only run inside a live engine simulation; unitsync can't call them) in favour of unitsync's existing info-map API, which is the right tool and already how we read minimaps.

## What changed

- **unitsync worker** (`coilbox-unitsync-worker`): new `heightmap` mode. Binds `GetInfoMap` / `GetMapMinHeight` / `GetMapMaxHeight` (all optional, decade-stable symbols), reads the full-res 16-bit heightmap, downscales to a grayscale PNG `data:` URL, and returns it with world `minHeight`/`maxHeight`. Disk-cached like minimaps.
- **Plugin** (`tauri-plugin-coilbox-unitsync`): `unitsync_heightmap` command + ACL (build.rs `COMMANDS` + `permissions/default.toml`), mirroring `unitsync_minimap`.
- **Frontend**: `unitsyncHeightmap` binding + `useUnitsyncHeightmap` hook; `MapPreview3D` gains additive `heightSrc`/`textureSrc` props (so the content flow passes pre-resolved data URLs — the mapconv compile/decompile file-path flow is untouched); `MapDetailPage` renders the 3D preview beside the 2D minimap.
- **Layout**: minimap and 3D preview sit side-by-side as equal-height columns; the minimap is capped to the 3D preview's height and centered (preserving the map's true aspect via the source `aspect-ratio`), stacking vertically on narrow widths.

## Notes

- World displacement uses elmos (`(heightmap.width-1)*8`) to match `minHeight`/`maxHeight` units, so relief is physically correct (water plane sits at sea level, no vertical exaggeration). This was the one bug caught in review — grid units would have exaggerated relief ~8x.
- three.js `TextureLoader` decodes the 16-bit PNG to 8-bit, so displacement is ~256 height bands (same as the existing mapconv preview; correct mapping, just quantized).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test` (worker + plugin) — 10 pass, incl. PNG-encode + arg-builder units
- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] `bunx biome ci .`, `bun run typecheck`
- [x] Live `bun tauri dev`: 3D preview renders for installed maps; basin sits below the water plane at sea level; Water/Wireframe toggles work; mapconv compile/decompile previews still work (no regression); equal-height side-by-side layout verified on multiple maps. Zero console errors.

Screenshots of the map detail page (2D minimap + 3D preview, side-by-side) captured via the Tauri MCP — happy to attach.

author: manusa
body:
## Summary

Reference proof-of-concept for #5622, scoped to a single module (`kubernetes-model-batch`): snapshot sundrio's annotation-processor output (`*Builder.java` / `*Fluent.java`) into committed source and skip sundrio APT in the default build, so the Builders/Fluents compile as plain javac source. This removes the per-build APT round-trip that dominates model-module build time.

This is an independent take from #7979 and deliberately avoids the antrun copy-with-filter that PR uses. The key finding: with the reactor building dependencies first, sundrio's APT already emits **only the module's own Builders** (no shallow "shadow" copies of referenced types like `PodTemplateSpecFluent`), so no filtering and no copy step are needed.

## Mechanism

A dedicated, committed source root `src/generated-builders/java` holds the Builders/Fluents, kept separate from the POJOs in `src/generated/java`:

- **Default build** (no `-Pgenerate`): `maven-compiler-plugin` names only the Lombok processors, so sundrio APT does not run and the committed Builders compile as plain source. Lombok still runs, keeping `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`.
- **`-Pgenerate`** (via `make generate-model`): the compiler's `generatedSourcesDirectory` points at `src/generated-builders/java`, and it names the Lombok + sundrio processors so they load from the **compile classpath** — sundrio then resolves referenced Builders from dependency jars rather than emitting shallow shadow copies.

`build-helper` adds `src/generated-builders/java` as a source root. Supporting config (license excludes, `sonar.exclusions`, `javadoc.sourcepath`, `.gitattributes`, and the `generate-model.yml` drift guard) is extended to the new directory.

## Why a separate directory (vs. writing into `src/generated/java`)

`maven-compiler-plugin` deletes its `generatedSourcesDirectory` before annotation processing. Pointing it at `src/generated/java` deletes the POJOs that are sundrio's input. A separate directory makes that wipe land on exactly the Builders — which is what you want on a regen — while the POJOs are untouched. The same wipe makes regeneration idempotent and removes orphaned Builders when a POJO is deleted (verified with a removal test).

## Evidence (local, `kubernetes-model-batch`)

- `-Pgenerate` regenerates 44 Builders/Fluents, **byte-identical** to the previous APT output, **zero** shadow files.
- Default build runs **zero** sundrio generation, produces a jar with a **byte-identical class list**, and the module test passes.
- `license:check` and `spotless:check` pass.

## Corrections vs. the issue's original plan

- The issue's `<proc>none</proc>` would disable Lombok too, silently dropping `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`. The default build runs Lombok-only instead.
- No copy/antrun and no Makefile stale-file cleanup are needed: the compiler's `generatedSourcesDirectory` wipe plus the openapi generator's own `deleteDirectory` of `src/generated/java` handle staleness.

## Scope and follow-ups (tracked on #5622)

This is a single-module POC. Lifting the wiring into the model parent pom for all model modules (atomically with committing their Builders), the modules with hand-written `@Buildable` sources, a parent-level `generate` profile, and the option to make the default-build processor selection less brittle (`annotationProcessorPaths` = lombok only) are follow-ups described on the issue.

## Commits

1. **config** — build wiring + license/sonar/javadoc/`.gitattributes`/CI-guard.
2. **generated** — the 44 committed Builder/Fluent files.

author: montana
body:
Hey Sourcegraph, 

This change adds `cmd/src/version_check_test.go`, covering both pieces of thenew logic with table-driven unit tests. The functions under test are pure and have no network or filesystem dependencies, so the suite runs fast and
deterministically.

### `isOutdated`

Verifies the version comparison that decides whether a warning should fire:

- **Major / minor / patch comparison** — confirms an older patch (`4.3.0` vs
  `4.3.1`), older minor (`4.3.0` vs `4.4.0`), and older major (`3.43.0` vs
  `4.0.0`) are each reported as outdated, while equal (`4.4.0` vs `4.4.0`) and
  newer (`4.5.0` vs `4.4.0`) versions are not.
- **`v`-prefixes** — checks that a leading `v` (`v4.3.0`) parses correctly and
  compares the same as its bare form, so the result doesn't depend on how the
  version string is formatted.
- **Prereleases** — ensures comparison is limited to the major/minor/patch
  components: a prerelease on the same base (`4.4.0-rc.1` vs `4.4.0`) is *not*
  flagged as outdated, while a prerelease on an older base (`4.3.0-rc.1` vs
  `4.4.0`) still is. This guards against spurious warnings for users running
  release candidates.
- **Unparseable input** — confirms the function returns `ok = false` (rather
  than guessing) when the current version can't be parsed (`dev`) or the
  recommended version is empty, so callers know to stay silent instead of
  warning on bad data.

### `shouldSkipVersionCheck`

Verifies the guard that decides when to run the check at all:

- **No-op subcommands** — confirms the check is skipped for `version`, `help`,
  an empty subcommand, and flag-only invocations like `-h` / `--help`, where a
  warning would be noise (and where `version` already reports this information
  itself).
- **Normal subcommands** — confirms the check *does* run for representative
  real commands (`search`, `batch`, `api`), so the feature isn't accidentally
  disabled.
- **`SRC_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK` opt-out** — confirms setting the environment
  variable suppresses the check, covering the documented escape hatch for CI
  and scripts.
- **Dev builds** — confirms the check is skipped when `version.BuildTag` is the
  default `dev` value, so local and development builds don't warn on every
  invocation.

Because `shouldSkipVersionCheck` reads the package-level `version.BuildTag`, the test temporarily overrides it to a real release value (`4.3.0`) and restores it via `t.Cleanup`, keeping the cases isolated from the build-time version.

author: morganc8559-code
body:
## What

Upgrades the **in-sandbox** generated MCP client (`tool_generator.py`) from naive JSON-POST to the full **streamable-HTTP** transport (MCP 2025-06-18), so the agent can talk to modern OAuth/HTTP MCP servers (e.g. Robinhood's Agentic Trading MCP) from inside the Daytona/Docker sandbox.

## Why

MCP tools execute **inside the sandbox** via the client emitted as an f-string by `src/ptc_agent/core/tool_generator.py` — not the host `mcp_registry.py`. The previous codegen only spoke plain JSON POST, which modern streamable-HTTP servers reject. This is the enabling change for HTTP-transport workspace MCP servers.

## Changes

- New verbatim `_STREAMABLE_HTTP_SOURCE` helper injected into the generated client:
  - `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`
  - Parses **SSE-or-JSON** responses
  - Captures + replays `Mcp-Session-Id` for session continuity
  - Sends `MCP-Protocol-Version` header; `protocolVersion` `2025-06-18`
- Rewrote `_initialize_sse_server`, `_call_mcp_tool_sse`, `_discover_sse` to use the helper
- Bumped `MCP_CLIENT_CODEGEN_VERSION` `2` → `3` so existing sandboxes re-sync the client

## Compatibility & risk

Backward-compatible with JSON-only servers (SSE-or-JSON parsing). No HTTP/SSE workspace MCP servers are enabled today, so blast radius is low.

## Testing

- Validated end-to-end against a live FastMCP streamable-HTTP server: `initialize` → session-id capture → `tools/list` → `tools/call`
- All 85 generator unit tests pass

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

- **New Features**
  - Added support for a new streaming HTTP transport, improving compatibility with remote MCP tools and server responses.
  - Updated protocol handling to use the latest supported version for better interoperability.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved reliability of tool discovery and tool calls over HTTP/SSE, including better handling when responses are missing.
  - Session information is now carried across requests more consistently, reducing connection and context issues.

author: alexanderlhicks
body:
## DIV-perf Phase 3 — rank algorithm candidates under the real mainnet workload

Stacked on #9547 (Phase 2 data). **Base: `perf/div-evm-workload-data`** — this PR
adds only the 3 Phase-3 commits on top.

Part of the DIV-opcode performance effort (motivated by @pirapira's gas-repricing
question: DIV is flat `LOW`=5 gas, but real zkVM proving cost ≈ dynamic
instruction count and varies ~3.4× with divisor size). Phase 1 built the cost
harness; Phase 2 gathered the real mainnet operand distribution; **Phase 3 ranks
the algorithm candidates under that distribution and picks the winner.**

### What this PR does

- **Extends `bench/DivBench.lean`** to rank DIV/MOD candidates under the **real
  workload**, not a guessed one. The headline metric is the **operand-sampled
  mean**: the true mean step count (running the *verified* `step` semantics) over
  a frequency-weighted sample of **800 real DIV + 400 MOD mainnet operands**
  (`scripts/sample-div-operands.py` → `bench/div-operands-sample.txt`, drawn from
  the Phase-2 trace). A representative per-class weighting is kept as a labeled
  cross-check. Adds `benchMod`, MOD candidates, and a 112-operand correctness sweep.
- **`docs/divmod-evm-redesign.md`** — measured before/after table, methodology,
  and the cheap-dispatch / n=2 roadmap.
- No change to the verified core (the only `EvmAsm/**` edit is a one-line stale
  comment fix in `FastN1Program.lean`).

### Measured result (all sampled operands correct)

| | deployed (v4) | v5 | **v6 (n=1 fast path)** | v6 vs deployed |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **DIV** (800 real ops) | 551.53 | 557.60 | **399.08** | **−27.6%** |
| **MOD** (400 real ops) | 609.48 | — | **406.52** | **−33.3%** |

`evm_div_v6` / `evm_mod_v6` (the n=1 single-limb fast path, #9303) are the **ranked
winners**: they collapse the dominant n=1 bucket (49% of DIV, 68% of MOD operands)
from ~685 to 365 steps, while the n≥2 fallback costs only ~6 extra steps. Correct
on all 1200 sampled ops + the 112-operand corner sweep. (`evm_div_v5` is a −1.08%
regression vs v4 — it exists only as v6's fallback core.)

**Recommendation:** verify `evm_div_v6`/`evm_mod_v6` next — they already exist, are
executable, and capture the biggest measured win. Then the cheap-dispatch
front-end (a<b/pow2/b0) and the n=2 double-word path (the most defensible
vintage-independent un-captured win, 18.2%).

### Adversarial review (already applied in commit 3)

A fresh two-agent adversarial review (independent harness-code audit +
methodology audit) plus an independent recompute were run on this work. The
arithmetic reproduced to the last digit, but the review found real defects, all
fixed here:

- **HIGH (code bug):** `f2` printed `0.00` for negative inputs (`Float.toUInt64`
  floors negatives to 0), masking that `evm_div_v5` is a −1.08% regression. Fixed.
- **HIGH (methodology):** the original "n-weighted EXACT" framing was false — step
  count varies *within* a divisor word-count (v5 n=2 spans ~528–634; v6 n=1
  ~347–369), so a single representative is biased toward the expensive end.
  Replaced the headline with the bias-free operand-sampled mean; the true win
  (−27.6%) is in fact slightly *larger* than the earlier −26.9% point estimate.
- **MED:** "helps MOD even more" was asserted, never measured. Now measured (−33.3%).
- **LOW:** doc mixed `div`/`divmod` series figures (reconciled); stale exit-PC
  comment (1888→1884); cosmetic column padding.

### Commits

1. `4e8216c0` — frequency-weighted DivBench harness + v6 measurement
2. `4a1423d3` — redesign findings doc + PLAN.md
3. `34b3e7d6` — adversarial-review fixes (operand-sampled mean + `f2` bug)

### Reproduce

```
lake build EvmAsm.Evm64.DivMod.FastN1Program EvmAsm.Evm64.DivMod.Program \
           EvmAsm.Rv64.Execution EvmAsm.Evm64.Basic
python3 scripts/sample-div-operands.py
lake env lean bench/DivBench.lean
```

author: imran-siddique
body:
## What changed

`_canonical_bytes` in `src/agentrust_trace/sign.py` previously used `json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=True)`, which is **not** RFC 8785 (JCS) conformant. The spec (`spec/trace-v0.1.md` §3.2.2) normatively mandates JCS as the signature pre-image. `_canonical_bytes` is now backed by the `rfc8785` library.

`sign_record` and `verify_record` already share `_canonical_bytes` (confirmed: it is the only producer of the signing pre-image, called once in each), so this single change applies the same canonicalization to **both** signing and verification.

### Why JCS, not json.dumps

`json.dumps(sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=True)` diverges from RFC 8785 in three load-bearing ways:

- **Non-ASCII strings:** json.dumps escapes them as `\uXXXX`; JCS emits raw UTF-8 (e.g. `ü` → `\xc3\xbc`, not `ü`).
- **Numbers:** json.dumps zero-pads exponents (`1e-07`); JCS uses the ECMAScript shortest round-trip form (`1e-7`), per RFC 8785 §3.2.2.3.
- **Key ordering:** json.dumps sorts by Unicode code point; JCS sorts by UTF-16 code unit (these differ for astral-plane code points).

Each divergence breaks cross-implementation verification and opens a signature-preserving mutation surface.

### Library vs hand-rolled

Used the **`rfc8785`** PyPI package (added to `dependencies` in `pyproject.toml`, pinned `>=0.1.2`) rather than hand-rolling JCS. Justification: a vetted library is the spec's own recommendation ("Implementations MUST use an RFC 8785-conformant library"), avoids re-implementing the subtle ECMAScript Number-to-String and UTF-16 ordering rules, and installs cleanly. I cross-checked it against the RFC 8785 Appendix B number vectors (`1e-7`, `1e+21`, `9.999999999999997e+22`, `5e-324`, etc.) and it matches.

## Tests (in `tests/test_sign.py`)

- `test_round_trip_with_non_ascii_payload` — sign then verify a record carrying non-ASCII data (`modèle français 🤖`); round-trip still passes.
- `test_canonical_bytes_known_answer_non_ascii` — literal expected-bytes assertion `{"id":"caf\xc3\xa9","msg":"h\xc3\xbcllo"}`, plus an explicit assertion that the json.dumps form (`é`/`ü`) differs. A regression to json.dumps fails this.
- `test_canonical_bytes_known_answer_numbers` — literal `{"n":1e-7}`, plus `assert json.dumps(1e-7) == "1e-07"` to show the form we moved away from.
- `test_canonical_bytes_matches_reference_library` — full record cross-checked against `rfc8785.dumps`.
- `test_jcs_distinguishes_unicode_key_order_from_json_dumps` — object with a `z` key and a `U+1F600` key; JCS (UTF-16 code unit) puts `z` first and the two schemes produce different bytes.
- `test_canonical_bytes_sorts_keys_no_whitespace` — basic JCS shape.

All 71 tests pass (including the #73 freshness / trusted-key tests). `ruff check src/ tests/ --select E,F,W --ignore E501` is clean.

## Scope

This PR is canonicalization only. Two related items remain separate **Wave 2** work:

- **Revocation enforcement** (the spec's "verifiers MUST consult current revocation status" requirement is not yet enforced in code).
- The **cnf-in-preimage scope decision** (whether `cnf` should be inside or outside the signed pre-image — currently `cnf` is signed and only `signature` is excluded).

author: stano-salvatore
body:
## What

Makes the Android home-screen **Quick Log widget** real. The provider, layouts and manifest fragment already existed in `android-widget/` but were never installed into the generated Android project, so the widget could never be added to the home screen. This wires it end-to-end.

## Changes

- **Build wiring (`.ci/customize-android.py`):** copies the widget provider + `widget_quick_log` layout, `quick_log_widget_info` xml and `widget_background` drawable into the generated Android project, and registers the `AppWidgetProvider` `<receiver>` in the manifest (idempotent, runs before `cap sync` like the existing permission injections).
- **Kotlin → Java:** the project compiles Java (`MainActivity.java`); a `.kt` in the app module wouldn't build, so the provider is translated to `QuickLogWidget.java` (emoji as `\u` escapes to be encoding-safe in CI). The orphaned `.kt` is removed.
- **Key plumbing:** adds `@capacitor/preferences@^8.0.0` so the app can write `widget_api_key` + `widget_app_url` into the `CapacitorStorage` SharedPreferences file the native widget reads. Ports the activator into `src/lib/widget-activator.ts` and adds an **"Activate Widget"** button to the Android Widget settings card.

## How it works

Settings → Android Widget → Generate Key → **Activate Widget** stores the key + app origin. The home-screen widget's water/coffee/beer/wine buttons then POST to `/api/widget/log` (`x-widget-key` header → existing, working endpoint) without opening the app. Daily totals are cached natively and reset at midnight; tapping the widget body opens the app.

## Notes

- Requires a **new APK install** to get the widget (native change). The `build` check produces the signed `emergenthealth-release` artifact.
- Service-worker cache hardening (so web fixes stop getting pinned stale in the APK WebView) is a separate follow-up.

author: bunsdev
body:
### Motivation
- The code previously auto-loaded any `.json` under `COVEN_HOME/adapters`, creating an implicit trust path that allowed planted manifests to register harnesses which could execute attacker-controlled commands.
- This change protects the adapter trust store by ensuring only known, bundled adapter recipes are implicitly trusted when their manifest files exactly match the packaged recipe and are regular (non-symlink) files.
- The install flow is hardened so existing untrusted or stale manifests are replaced rather than silently accepted as already installed.

### Description
- Replace the unconstrained `adapter_manifest_paths_in_dir` scan of `COVEN_HOME/adapters` with `trusted_adapter_manifest_paths`, which only yields manifests for known recipe names that pass exact content matching via `trusted_adapter_manifest_matches_recipe`.
- Add `trusted_adapter_manifest_matches_recipe` to check that a manifest is a non-symlink regular file and that its text matches the bundled recipe returned by `known_adapter_manifest` before treating it as installed.
- Update the installer (`run_adapter_install`) to treat a manifest as installed only if it matches the recipe, and to remove symlinked or stale manifests before writing the trusted manifest.
- Add tests and regressions: unit test to ensure a planted/modified `COVEN_HOME/adapters/hermes.json` is ignored, a unit test that a correct bundled Hermes manifest is loaded from `COVEN_HOME`, and a smoke test verifying `coven adapter install hermes` replaces an existing planted manifest.

### Testing
- Ran `cargo fmt` to apply formatting without errors.
- Ran `cargo test -p coven-cli adapter` which executed the adapter unit and smoke tests.
- All adapter-related tests passed (including the new regressions) with no failures.

author: tylerjroach
body:
## Summary

`ScheduledExecutorService#scheduleAtFixedRate` permanently cancels future executions if the runnable throws an uncaught `Throwable`. `fetchDefinitions()` only catches `Exception`, so an `Error` (`OutOfMemoryError`, `StackOverflowError`, `LinkageError`, etc.) escaping would silently kill flag-definitions polling for the JVM's lifetime — and the thread factory has no `UncaughtExceptionHandler` to even surface it.

Wrap the scheduled runnable in a defensive `try { fetchDefinitions(); } catch (Throwable t) { logger.log(SEVERE, ...) }`. `fetchDefinitions()` keeps its `Exception` handling unchanged; the wrapper exists purely to swallow + log JVM-level escapes so the schedule keeps firing.

## Context

Linear: [SDK-86](https://linear.app/mixpanel/issue/SDK-86). Practical scope is narrow (JVM-level errors only) but the defense is one-line.

## Test plan

- [x] Full test suite passes (173 tests, was 172, +1 new)
- [x] New `testPollingSurvivesThrowableFromFetch` arms an `Error` to escape the second `httpGet` call, then asserts the polling task continues to fire (`callCount >= 3` after 2.5s with a 1s interval). Before the fix the scheduler would have cancelled the task on the `Error` and `callCount` would have stopped at 2.

author: alistair3149
body:
Fixes https://github.com/ProfessionalWiki/NeoWiki/issues/784

When a View renders a Subject with relations, the
`subject/{id}?expand=relations` response already bundles every related Subject.
`RestSubjectRepository.getSubject` discarded all but the requested one, and
`StoreStateLoader` then re-fetched each relation target via
`getReferencedSubjects` — one redundant HTTP request (and graph-backed read) per
relation.

Add `RestSubjectRepository.getSubjectWithReferencedSubjects`, which deserializes
the whole bundle into a SubjectMap (sharing the fetch with `getSubject` via a
private helper). `StoreStateLoader.loadForSubject` now stores the requested
Subject and its referenced Subjects from that single response, dropping the
per-target fetches. This mirrors the existing page-subjects path
(`getPageSubjects` -> `loadPageSubjects`).

A Subject with N relations now costs 1 request instead of N+1. Verified against
the demo `ACME Inc` Subject: the endpoint returns the main Subject plus its 8
distinct referenced Subjects in one response, and StoreStateLoader issues a
single repository call with zero per-target re-fetches.

> Worked from the @alistair3149-directed task to confirm #784 was still live and
> fix it; the approach (surface the bundle, mirror the page-subjects path) was
> confirmed against the codebase.
> Context: the NeoWiki frontend (RestSubjectRepository, StoreStateLoader,
> StatementList) and the live demo REST response.
> <sub>Written by Claude Code, `Opus 4.8 (1M context)`</sub>

author: msywulak
body:
Closes #4129.

## What

Consolidates the three byte-identical in-process `Map`-of-timestamps sliding-window rate limiters on the **unauthenticated public surface** — `trial-abuse.ts` (per-IP + per-email), `contact.ts` (per-IP), `demo.ts` (per-email) — into **one async limiter behind a swappable `SlidingWindowStore` interface** (`packages/api/src/lib/sliding-window-rate-limit.ts`).

## Why (correctness, not just cleanliness)

The limiter guards the unauthenticated trial-signup / demo / contact surface. Each regional API service (US / EU / APAC) is an independent process holding its **own** in-process window, and each scales to N replicas under load — so the per-IP cap is effectively `R × (total replicas across all regions)`. Latent at one replica per region, it **activates on exactly the horizontal scale-up you'd do under launch load**. The seam makes the eventual fix (a process-external Redis store) a drop-in.

## How

- **New `lib/sliding-window-rate-limit.ts`** — async `SlidingWindowStore` interface + `InMemorySlidingWindowStore` adapter + `SlidingWindowLimiter`. Because every store method is async, a Redis adapter (sorted set per key) shares the window across replicas/regions **without touching any call site**. The multi-instance limitation is documented at the seam (and the atomicity note is precise: the in-memory adapter is effectively atomic per process via microtask draining; the read/record race appears only with a networked adapter).
- `RateLimitDecision` is a **discriminated union** — `retryAfterMs` present IFF blocked — so consumers read it after `!allowed` with no fallback or non-null assertion.
- `trial-abuse` / `contact` / `demo` refactored onto it; `check` / `reset` / `cleanup` are now async.
- Call sites awaited: contact / demo / starter-prompts routes (`Effect.gen` handlers via `yield* Effect.promise`, plain async handlers via `await`) and the MCP onboarding limiter; the three scheduler cleanup ticks switched `Effect.try` → `Effect.tryPromise`.

## Behavior preserved (in-memory adapter)

Same per-IP / per-email RPM, same anon-IP graceful degradation, same two-phase **record-in-neither-bucket-until-both-pass** semantics, same settings-backed limits (`ATLAS_*_RATE_LIMIT_RPM`) and `trialAbuseRejections` metrics. A store rejection (impossible in-memory; relevant for the Redis follow-up) fails **closed** — `runEffect` maps it to a 500 with `requestId`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] One `rate-limiter` module with a swappable store interface, consumed by all three call sites (no per-call-site `Map`)
- [x] Store interface is process-external-ready — a Redis adapter shares the window across replicas/regions without touching any call site
- [x] Behavior preserved under the in-memory adapter
- [x] Multi-instance limitation documented at the seam; a test covers the window logic against the store **interface** (parametrized over two distinct stores), not a concrete `Map`

## Tests

New `sliding-window-rate-limit.test.ts` runs every window-logic case over **two conforming stores** — the shipped in-memory adapter and a deliberately `Map`-free `Record`-backed one — proving the limiter speaks only the interface. The three existing unit suites migrated sync→async with no assertions dropped.

## Review

Internal review panel run on the diff (type-design, silent-failure, comment-accuracy, test-coverage) — converged CLEAN over 2 rounds. Notable: the discriminated union surfaced two previously-unguarded `.retryAfterMs` test reads, now narrowed.

## Notes

- The Redis adapter is a **not-yet-filed follow-up** (parent umbrella #3801; this PR lands the seam).
- Out of scope: the separate fixed-window `public-rate-limit.ts` / `source-rate-limit.ts` limiters (different algorithm/domain).

## Summary

Removes the duplicate `SaleSummaryListItem` interface and reuses the shared `SaleOrderSummary` type for sale summary report rows. This eliminates type duplication and ensures the frontend and gateway use a single mapper for all sale-summary row representations.

body:
Closes #412.

`DemoInputRecorder` only ever read `cams[0]` and held that single framing for the whole clip — built for a static initial position, not animation. The scripted-input format already accepts a `camera` **array** of `{tick,x,y,zoom}` keyframes; this PR makes the recorder actually use them.

## Change

- **`CameraKeyframes.sample(track, tick)`** — a pure helper that interpolates position and zoom **linearly by tick fraction** between the two surrounding keyframes, clamping to the first/last frame outside the track's range and guarding duplicate ticks. No node/engine state, so it's directly unit-testable (like `DistanceLegend`).
- **`DemoInputRecorder`** — keeps the full keyframe array and samples it each physics frame, so the camera pans and zooms along the track. **Single-keyframe demos are unchanged** (one keyframe = held framing, exactly as before).

## Demo

`demos/inputs/camera-zoom.json` (shipped as `demo.412.json`) has **no input steps** — just an animated framing that zooms in on the left flank, then pans right and zooms back out. Stills from the recorded clip, zoomed out vs zoomed in — note the bottom-right **distance legend rescaling 5 m → 2 m** as the zoom changes (the live-zoom motion #364 wanted but couldn't record before this):

author: gavingolden
body:
## Why

`flow epic run` already drives an epic with a deterministic, intentionally LLM-free reconciler, but the moment a child feature stalls (`gated` / `needs-human` / a CI failure surfaced as `needs-human` / `orphan`) or the DAG deadlocks (frontier empty, not all merged), the orchestrator only surfaces the raw state and exits `blocked`. The developer must then read each child pipeline by hand and sequence the recovery by eye — the exact babysitting `flow epic run` was meant to remove. This is the deferred half of the orchestrator's "Decision I": the LLM judgment layer that interprets a stall and decides the next move.

## What

- `flow epic run <slug>` spawns a new `/epic-run` sanctioned supervisor session that drives ticks via the existing deterministic reconciler and applies LLM judgment only on a halt or deadlock event (never on a green tick).
- On a halted child feature, the supervisor interprets the failure into a typed decision — retry, redirect, or escalate — with a one-line reason.
- Recoverable stalls are retried autonomously through `flow new --resume`, bounded by a per-feature retry budget in run-state; budget exhausted escalates.
- A frontier-empty-but-not-all-merged deadlock gets a probable-cause diagnosis (e.g. a stuck/`orphan` feature, a silently-cancelled dependency, manifest/run-state drift), not just the generic "frontier empty" line.
- Escalation fires `flow-notify`, records the interpreted reason in run-state, and halts only the affected subtree.
- A deterministic `flow-epic-judge-context` helper assembles the bounded evidence the LLM reasons over, fully unit-testable with stubbed `gh`/`git`.
- `flow epic run --once` / `--no-judgment` and `epic.judgment: false` keep the existing pure LLM-free loop unchanged.

## Key decisions

- The LLM layer sits alongside/above the reconciler: `reconcile()` stays pure and LLM-free; judgment consumes its `ReconcileResult` rather than replacing it — preserving the "intentionally LLM-free v1 reconciler" framing.
- `/epic-run` is a separate sanctioned supervisor session (the `/epic-create` precedent), so it does not touch `/flow-pipeline`'s nine Task-tool exemptions or two AskUserQuestion forms.
- Judgment runs in-process over a deterministically-bounded context (CI logs truncated to the failing-check tail) for v1 simplicity; a one-shot judgment sub-agent is recorded as the escalation if context bloat appears.
- Orchestrator hard invariants stand: never merge a feature PR, never override a `gated` verdict (`gated` ⇒ escalate-only), never `send-keys` into a feature window.
- Out of scope (v1): autonomous redirect (the `redirect` decision is actuated as escalate-with-a-suggested-redirect for the human to apply); unattended `launchd` ticking.

## User-facing changes

- `flow epic run <slug>` now opens a tmux window running the `/epic-run` supervisor (like `flow epic create`) and reasons about stalls/deadlocks instead of exiting `blocked` with a raw message.
- A stalled child feature is auto-retried (bounded) or escalated with an interpreted reason rather than always halting the epic for manual triage.
- A DAG deadlock now prints a probable-cause diagnosis and suggested resolution.
- New: `flow epic run --no-judgment` (and existing `--once`) keep the pure LLM-free loop; `epic.judgment: false` in `~/.flow/config.json` disables judgment; `epic.maxRetries` configures the per-feature retry budget.

author: auschoi96
body:
## What

Builds **lane 2** of the loop controller per `docs/LOOP_CONTROLLER.md` (Option A): the framework autonomously **detects → decides → proves → gates → proposes**, and a human approves the apply later (lane 3). **The controller never applies a change** — it sets no champion alias, runs no `CREATE`, and has no apply seam.

New `ail.loop` package:

- **`proposals.py`** — typed (pydantic v2, `extra='forbid'`) `ProposedAction`: agent/action_kind/risk_class/status; the **why** (`TriggerSignal` — which RLM rec / judge dimension / L0 waste pattern, with trace refs); the **what** (`ProposedChange` — metric-view SQL / skill+instruction diff / GEPA evolved-body ref / revert target, validated to match the action kind); the **proof** (`ProofSummary` — frozen-suite realized delta + promote/block counts + suite hash + correctness-held, sourced from the comparison aggregate built from `ComparisonResult`); the **gate status** (`GateStatus` — readiness tier + certifying-judge agreement + scored coverage). `risk_class` is informational, never an auto-apply switch.
- **`decision_rules.py`** — goal-parameterized **pure** rules: RLM recurring additive asset + objective unmet → `metric_view`; dominant redundant-read → `skill_update`; trusted judge dimension below the goal's own threshold → `gepa_prompt`; post-apply regression → `revert`. No magic thresholds — bars come from the compiled goal / `DecisionThresholds`.
- **`controller.py`** — `run_cycle(agent, goal, *, feedback_source, candidate_builder, prover, gate)` over **injectable seams** (proving via `compare_candidate`/`run_phase2_comparison`, gating via `compute_readiness`), so it is unit-testable with **no live MLflow/agent runs**. **Fail-closed**: a non-improving/crashed candidate (no PROMOTE / correctness regressed) or an ungated state (readiness not met / distrusted judge) yields **no proposal**. Refuses to run on an unconfirmed goal.
- **`publish_proposals.py`** — **agent-scoped atomic REPLACE** into the unified `agent_proposed_actions` UC table (keyed by `agent_name, proposal_id`) that lane 3 reads SELECT-only; reuses `ail.publish` helpers, never re-implements the swap.

## Reuse, not reimplementation

Consumes `ail.goals.compiler`, `ail.readiness`, `ail.compare`/`ail.optimize.phase2`, and `ail.registry` as-is. No goals/readiness/compare/assets/gepa logic is duplicated.

## Tests (`pytest -m 'not live'`)

- a proven + gated candidate → exactly one pending proposal with the right why/proof/gate payload;
- a non-improving candidate (no PROMOTE / correctness regressed) → zero proposals;
- an ungated state (readiness not met / distrusted certifying judge) → zero proposals;
- each decision rule maps its signal to the right action kind;
- `risk_class` is set but never triggers an auto-apply (the controller calls no apply/alias function — there is none);
- the publish writes agent-scoped rows.

## Gate results

- **ruff** `check` + `format --check` on `src tests`: clean.
- **mypy** `src`: `Success: no issues found in 78 source files`.
- **pytest** `-m 'not live'`: **795 passed, 1 skipped** (the 1 skip is the dspy-absence env case; the 1 deselected-and-otherwise-failing `test_run_returns_failed_result_when_sdk_missing` is a pre-existing CI-vs-local divergence — it asserts SDK-absence behavior but the local venv has `claude-agent-sdk` installed; unrelated to this change). The 40 new lane-2 tests are in the passing set.

New tests: `tests/test_loop_proposals.py`, `tests/test_decision_rules.py`, `tests/test_loop_controller.py`.

Scope: `src/ail/loop/*` + the publish step + tests + the `docs/LOOP_CONTROLLER.md` status update. **No app/TS changes** (lane 3 owns the UI). Not merging — lane 3 builds on this.

This pull request and its description were written by Isaac.

author: recursive-ai-dev
body:
## Summary
This PR implements complete backward (gradient) passes for the attention, FFN, and MoE layers, adds several numerical stability improvements, and refactors code for clarity and correctness.

## Key Changes

### Backward Pass Implementations
- **DifferentialAttention.backward()**: Full analytic backward through differential attention with RoPE support, including proper handling of GQA (Grouped Query Attention) expansion undoing
- **FFNBlock.backward()**: Backward through layer normalization and SwiGLU with proper gradient computation for scale/shift parameters
- **MoELayer.backward()**: Backward through mixture-of-experts with precomputed token→expert routing maps (O(n_tok * top_k) instead of O(n_experts * n_tok * top_k))
- **SwiGLU.backward()**: Updated to accept optional bias parameters for correctness
- **Attention.backward()**: Added `_softmax_backward()` helper for proper softmax gradient computation

### Numerical Stability & Correctness
- **LayerNorm backward**: Refactored for numerical stability using precomputed `std_inv` and `x_mu` to avoid redundant computations and improve clarity
- **RoPE.rotate_inverse()**: New method to undo RoPE rotations (orthogonal transformation inverse via transpose)
- **Empty ndarray handling**: Added check in `_format_value()` to handle empty arrays without calling `.min()/.max()`
- **Logger propagation**: Set `logger.propagate = False` to prevent double-logging in Jupyter environments
- **Null projector computation**: Use `np.linalg.solve()` instead of explicit matrix inversion for numerical stability

### Training Loop & Architecture
- **Complete backward chain**: Training step now properly chains backward through MoE → FFN → Attention, matching forward order
- **Deterministic seq_offset**: Use training step as seq_offset for reproducibility
- **ShardedLinear refactor**: Explicit accumulation in row strategy to avoid undocumented `__radd__` behavior with `sum()`

### Documentation & Clarity
- Added comprehensive docstrings to backward methods explaining mathematical derivations
- Clarified simplicial complex message passing with detailed explanation of node/edge signal computation
- Improved comments in LayerNorm backward explaining why certain terms vanish
- Better variable naming and intermediate computation documentation

### Bug Fixes & Maintenance
- Fixed `SimplicialComplexNN.W_down` → `W_edge` naming for clarity
- Removed unused `self.W_full` from `ShardedLinear`
- Added schema version checking in checkpoint loading with warnings
- Improved error handling in safetensors loading with explicit KeyError for missing config
- Fixed `.gitignore` to properly exclude `.venv/` and `artifacts/` directories

## Implementation Details
- Backward passes recompute forward activations (no activation caching) for memory efficiency
- Proper chain rule application through all transformations including RoPE and GQA
- Gradient accumulation respects routing weights in MoE backward
- LayerNorm backward uses simplified form exploiting that mean(x - mu) = 0 by definition

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The PORT binding logic in `server/_core/index.ts` has a critical bug that causes deployment failures:

```typescript
// BUGGY CODE (line 1026-1028)
const port =
  process.env.PORT || process.env.NODE_ENV === "production"
    ? preferredPort
    : await findAvailablePort(preferredPort);
```

**Issue**: Due to operator precedence, this evaluates as:
```
(process.env.PORT) || (process.env.NODE_ENV === "production" ? preferredPort : await findAvailablePort(...))
```

In production:
- If `process.env.PORT` is set (Railway always sets it), the condition is truthy
- The ternary is never evaluated
- The app always binds to `preferredPort` (parsed from `process.env.PORT`)
- ✅ This part works correctly

But the real issue is the logic intent: **the code should only use `findAvailablePort` when BOTH conditions are false**:
1. `process.env.PORT` is NOT set (genuine local dev)
2. `NODE_ENV` is NOT production

The current code uses `||` (OR) which is wrong. It should use `&&` (AND).

## Solution

Change line 1026 from:
```typescript
process.env.PORT || process.env.NODE_ENV === "production"
```

To:
```typescript
process.env.PORT && process.env.NODE_ENV === "production"
```

Now the logic is:
- If `PORT` is set AND we're in production → use `preferredPort` (Railway's assigned port)
- Otherwise → scan for available port (local dev fallback)

This ensures:
1. **Production (Railway)**: Always respects Railway's injected `$PORT` environment variable
2. **Local dev**: Scans for available port starting from 3000 if PORT is unset
3. **Healthcheck**: Railway's proxy can now reach the app on the correct port

## Impact

- Fixes all recent deployment failures caused by healthcheck timeouts
- Ensures the app binds to Railway's assigned port in production
- Preserves local development port-scanning behavior
- Zero impact on running deployments (only affects new deployments)

author: neilotoole
body:
Closes #965.

## What

Adds `DBSemver` — a deterministic, semver-comparable engine version — to sq's SQL drivers, so version-dependent decisions branch on the **runtime server version** instead of re-parsing the free-form `metadata.Source.DBVersion` string at each call site.

## How

- **`SQLDriver.DBSemver(ctx, db) (string, error)`** — a new interface method, implemented by all 8 SQL drivers. Each is a thin engine-specific version query plus a package-local pure `parseSemver(raw)` that normalizes to canonical `golang.org/x/mod/semver` form (`vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`).
- **`Grip.DBSemver(ctx) (string, error)`** — a delegating interface method. The 8 SQL grips delegate to their driver; the 4 non-SQL grips (csv/json/userdriver/xlsx) delegate to their backing SQLite grip, consistent with how they already surface `DBVersion`.
- Normalization is **per-package** by design (no shared helper): MariaDB makes MySQL's parsing engine-specific, and keeping each driver's logic local avoids a shared utility quietly accreting per-engine special cases. MySQL handles the MariaDB `5.5.5-` replication sentinel (`5.5.5-10.6.4-MariaDB` → `v10.6.4`).
- The leading-token regex caps multi-part versions at three parts (Oracle `23.26.1.0.0` → `v23.26.1`, SQL Server/ClickHouse 4-part → 3-part); `semver.Canonical` pads shorter forms (Postgres `16.1` → `v16.1.0`), so every driver returns a uniform 3-part value.
- **Consumer migration:** the MySQL JSON-type test now skips MySQL < 5.7 via `grip.DBSemver` + `semver.Compare` instead of an inline `fmt.Sscanf`.

`DBSemver` is a plain I/O accessor (no caching) and runtime-only (no serialized `metadata.Source` field).

## Per-driver version source

| Driver | Query | Example | Canonical |
|--------|-------|---------|-----------|
| mysql | `@@GLOBAL.version` | `8.0.36-0ubuntu0.22.04.1` / `5.5.5-10.6.4-MariaDB` | `v8.0.36` / `v10.6.4` |
| postgres | `current_setting('server_version')` | `16.1` | `v16.1.0` |
| sqlserver | `SERVERPROPERTY('ProductVersion')` | `16.0.4115.5` | `v16.0.4115` |
| oracle | `product_component_version.version_full` → `v$instance.version` | `23.26.1.0.0` | `v23.26.1` |
| clickhouse | `version()` | `25.3.2.39` | `v25.3.2` |
| sqlite3 | `sqlite_version()` | `3.45.1` | `v3.45.1` |
| duckdb | `version()` | `v1.5.2` | `v1.5.2` |
| rqlite | `sqlite_version()` | `3.45.1` | `v3.45.1` |

## Testing

- Per-driver `parseSemver` unit tables (pure, no container), incl. MySQL/MariaDB literals.
- Per-driver live `TestDBSemver` smoke tests — verified passing against running containers for **all 8 engines** (6 servers + sqlite3/duckdb embedded), exercising the live query+scan the unit tests can't.
- The migrated JSON-type test verified passing live on MySQL 8.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and pinned `golangci-lint` all clean.

## Out of scope (deferred)

- Exposing `DBSemver` on `metadata.Source` for debug/inspect/diff → **#992** (cheap follow-up; `getSourceMetadata` reuses the already-fetched raw version via the per-package `parseSemver`).
- Converting the MySQL `generation_expression`/`CHECK_CONSTRAINTS` error-driven fallbacks to version checks (left as-is).

author: pmrv
body:
## What

Adds an opt-in `monotone_slope: bool = False` to `SoftplusSurface2DInterpolator`. When set, every term's slope magnitude `|b_i(T)|` is constrained to be non-increasing in `T`. The default is unchanged (`b_i(T)` stays a free polynomial in `1/T`).

## Why

A convex well only ever sharpens as it cools, so the fitted sharpness should never reverse. The free slope (a degree-`b_order` polynomial in `1/T`) has no such guarantee — it can sharpen and then soften again across the range. `benchmarks/bench_monotone_slope.py` includes a `humped_b` surface where the free fit reproduces exactly that reversal.

## How

The slope is reparametrised through the same non-negative softplus link the amplitude already uses (`a_i = softplus(α_i)`):

```
b_i(T) = s_i * [ softplus(B_i0) + sum_{k>=1} softplus(B_ik) * w^k ],
w = max((1/T) - min_train(1/T), 0)
```

with the branch sign `s_i` fixed from the per-slice seed. Each `softplus(B_ik) >= 0` and `w^k` is non-decreasing in `1/T`, so `|b_i|` is non-increasing in `T` by construction at every temperature. The `max(., 0)` clamp anchors the training minimum at `w = 0` and holds `|b|` flat for `T` hotter than the training range, so an even-power term cannot turn it back up (or flip its sign) under extrapolation.

`s_i` is frozen from the seed and not refined by the coupled solve — reliable for the intended convex-V wells (the opposite-slope seed yields `[+, -]`); a near-degenerate seed slice could in principle lock in a wrong sign.

### Softplus, not sigmoid, for the positivity link

Both keep `|b|` positive, but softplus is `(0, ∞)` while sigmoid is `(0, s)`. Sigmoid imposes a ceiling that caps the slope (which grows unboundedly at the cold end) and saturates at both tails; in a side comparison it converged worse on sharp wells and never tripped the convergence test on the sharpest case, burning the full iteration budget. Softplus is unbounded above and keeps the coupled solve unconstrained, so the default `lm` fast path is retained.

## Cost

`benchmarks/bench_monotone_slope.py` fits the public class both ways on three surfaces (fit wall-time, worst-over-T normalised RMSE, and `max_T d|b|/dT` over `[50, 5000] K`):

- `in_family` (monotone truth): ~1.5x fit time, recovers to ~1e-7 (vs ~1e-10 free), guarantee holds exactly (`+0.0`).
- `sharp_v` (sharp monotone truth): monotone is *faster* (~0.45x) and more accurate — the constraint regularizes the stiff sharp-knee fit.
- `humped_b` (non-monotone truth): free follows the reversal; monotone refuses it (higher RMSE, as expected when the data genuinely reverses).

## Tests

`tests/unit/interpolate/test_softplus_surface.py`:
- in-family recovery under the constraint (`atol=1e-6`);
- `|b_i(T)|` non-increasing across heavy extrapolation on both sides of the training range, with a recovery + wide-`|b|`-span check so a degenerate/constant fit cannot pass;
- the constraint binding on a non-monotone truth (free reverses, monotone does not);
- convexity and non-negative amplitudes preserved on noisy data;
- composition with `shared_knee=True` (recovery + monotonicity);
- `n_softplus=3` sign stability (extra term stays monotone, recovery holds);
- Gibbs-Duhem `c = -dphi/dmu` consistency under monotone mode via `Surface2DInterpolatingPhase`;
- `monotone_slope` participates in dataclass equality.

Full `tests/unit/interpolate` + `tests/unit/test_phases.py` suite passes (184 tests); existing `SoftplusSurface2DInterpolator` behaviour with the default `monotone_slope=False` is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Why
When the floor-collapse timer gets low, the AI was still willing to spend time on opportunistic pickups and side detours, which could stall objective progress and miss stair unlock/clear windows.

## What changed
- Added a deterministic collapse-pressure model in `BehaviorTreeAI` that derives panic from `deadlineMs - elapsedMs`, stair unlock state, and stair discovery state.
- Added hard beeline behavior under low time (`<= 60s` and stairs undiscovered):
  - suppresses opportunistic loot/farm pulls,
  - suppresses quest-giver detours,
  - suppresses Track A COLLECT fallback so panic windows stay objective-first.
- Added dynamic opportunistic blending under rising panic:
  - collect/farm pull influence scales down as collapse pressure rises,
  - dodge influence is reduced but clamped to a non-zero panic floor to keep evasive behavior alive.
- Introduced panic tuning constants in `src/game/ai/bt-ai-tuning.ts`.

## Tests
- Added `tests/unit/ai-collapse-panic-profile.test.ts` for boundary and semantics coverage:
  - neutral/no-objective context,
  - 180s ramp start boundary,
  - 60s beeline boundary,
  - locked vs unlocked stairs pressure behavior,
  - discovered-stairs beeline-off behavior.
- Extended `tests/game/behavior-tree-ai.test.ts` to cover:
  - low-time suppression of on-path loot detours,
  - low-time suppression of Track A COLLECT fallback in objective-null windows.

## Review harness and prereqs
- Added validated 2-apple review ledger:
  - `docs/knowledge/review-ledgers/2026-06-30-quest-path-dodge-loot.review-ledger.json`
- Added session handoff and apple metrics artifacts required by project policy.

body:
## Summary

Implements the ReqIF half of the metamodel export-mapping design note as a one-way **publish** exporter. This is the next item after the metamodel views/completeness/YAML work (PR #39); the ReqIF/OSLC mapping note was the one explicitly deferred feature, and ReqIF is the implementable half today.

- **`dev/planning-forge/scripts/lib/reqif.mjs`** — `buildReqif(artifact, { now })` produces a well-formed ReqIF 1.0 document:
  - node → `SPEC-OBJECT`, node type → `SPEC-OBJECT-TYPE` (only used types emitted)
  - typed edge → `SPEC-RELATION` in canonical direction (no reverse links materialized)
  - `status` / `claim_kind` / `obligation` / `confidence` → pre-declared enumeration datatypes
  - external edge endpoints (`Goal`, `In Scope`, `risk:`, `manual check:`, `review check:`, `command:`) → `SPEC-OBJECT`s of a dedicated `external` type, in a separate `_so-x-` id namespace so they can't collide with node ids
- **`dev/planning-forge/scripts/export-metamodel-reqif.mjs`** — CLI matching the existing generator conventions: loads JSON/YAML via the shared loader, defends against non-array `nodes`/`edges`, writes to stdout or `--out`, exit 2 on usage/parse/write errors.

## Correctness / safety

- XML output **strips characters outside the XML 1.0 `Char` production and lone surrogates** while **preserving valid astral characters** (emoji, CJK extensions).
- Attribute-borne text encodes `\t` / `\n` / `\r` as `	` / `
` / `` so multi-line requirement text survives XML attribute-value normalization on read-back.
- Canonical edge direction preserved; reverse navigation stays a derived traversal, exactly as the metamodel requires.

## Validation

- `test-metamodel-reqif.mjs` — 78 assertions (structure, enum mapping, external endpoints, escaping, illegal/astral characters, whitespace preservation, referential integrity of `SPEC-OBJECT-REF`/`SPEC-OBJECT-TYPE-REF`/`ENUM-VALUE-REF`, CLI behavior)
- `lint-examples.mjs` (11 fixtures), `test-metamodel-validator.mjs`, `test-metamodel-views.mjs` — all pass
- Every metamodel fixture (specification/architecture/test-plan/bundle) exports **well-formed XML** (verified with `xmllint --noout`)
- Two adversarial review rounds; both findings (illegal-XML-char escaping, multi-line attribute fidelity) fixed, plus a self-introduced astral over-stripping regression caught and fixed before push.

## Scope

One-way ReqIF export only. ReqIF import/round-trip and the OSLC exporter remain design-note items (open questions retained in `metamodel-export-mapping.md`). JSON/YAML remains the source of truth.

author: hashbender
body:
## What

`looks_like_codex_intermediate_ack()` in `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` gates intent-ack continuation on an **English-only** future-ack regex (`\b(i'll|i will|let me|...)\b`) and an English-only `action_markers` substring list. When the acting model replies in Chinese ("我先載入 skill 確認用法…"), the regex never matches, the function returns `False` on its first guard, and the turn ends without executing a tool — the user has to manually type "please continue" every turn. This makes `intent_ack_continuation` a complete no-op for CJK users, most visible with MoA aggregators that tend to summarize the reference outputs and stop.

## Why

- The future-ack regex relies on Latin word-boundary phrases that simply don't exist in Chinese text — no amount of `\b` tuning fixes that, the fix needs CJK phrases.
- `action_markers` already matches via plain substring `in` containment (no regex), so CJK action verbs slot in directly with zero new matching logic.
- Scope is intentionally narrow: only the future-ack gate and `action_markers` are touched (the two markers the linked issue's repro actually exercises and the reporter validated locally). `workspace_markers` is untouched — it's only consulted on the `require_workspace=True` path, which this issue's repro doesn't reach, and guessing at unvalidated CJK workspace vocabulary isn't worth the risk in this PR.

## Change

- Added a parallel CJK substring check for future-ack phrases (我先, 我來/我来, 我會/我会, 讓我/让我, 我直接, 接下來我/接下来我) — only consulted when the English regex doesn't match, so the English path is untouched.
- Extended `action_markers` with CJK action verbs in both Traditional and Simplified script (載入/载入, 查, 執行/执行, 掃描/扫描, 檢查/检查, 分析, 讀取/读取).

## How to test

```bash
python -m pytest tests/agent/test_intent_ack_continuation.py -v
```

Repro before the fix (run on `main`, returns `False`):
```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from agent.agent_runtime_helpers import looks_like_codex_intermediate_ack

a = SimpleNamespace(_intent_ack_continuation=True, api_mode="chat_completions",
                    model="copilot/claude-opus-4.8", _strip_think_blocks=lambda c: c)
user_msg = "幫我看一下伺服器狀態並抓最新的錯誤紀錄"
ack = "我先載入 skill 確認用法，然後幫你檢查伺服器狀態。"
looks_like_codex_intermediate_ack(a, user_msg, ack, [{"role": "user", "content": user_msg}], require_workspace=False)
# main: False (bug) — this branch: True
```

- All 14 pre-existing tests in `tests/agent/test_intent_ack_continuation.py` pass unchanged (English path is byte-stable).
- 2 new tests added: Traditional + Simplified Chinese ack fires under the opted-in (`require_workspace=False`) path, and a real Chinese final answer (no future-ack phrase) still does **not** fire — confirming the CJK addition only widens the future-ack gate, not the other guardrails (no-prior-tool, length cap, action-verb requirement).
- `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` clean on the diff.

## Platforms tested

macOS (logic-only change, no OS-specific code paths — pure string/regex matching).

Fixes #55664

## What & why

Implements the **Dyslexia-friendly mode** from `ROADMAP.md` (§3.2), the last open item on the **Accessibility & Focus** shelf — taking it from `SOON` to shipped (4 / 4).

Per the roadmap spec: *Atkinson Hyperlegible (embedded as base64 for true offline), wider spacing, 1.8 line height — as a global app-wide toggle plus a reading surface.*

## Changes

- **Embedded Atkinson Hyperlegible** (latin: regular / bold / italic) as base64 `@font-face` rules — no network dependency, works from a `file://` copy. This also fixes the **Reading Ruler's "readable font"**, which referenced Atkinson but previously had no face to load (it silently fell back to Verdana/Tahoma).
- **App-wide toggle:** turning the mode on adds `.dys` to `<html>`, which swaps `--sans` / `--serif` to Atkinson everywhere and opens up line height (1.8) plus letter/word spacing via `--dys-lh` / `--dys-ls` / `--dys-ws`. Monospace (code, math, calculator readouts) is deliberately left untouched.
- **New `mountDyslexia` tool:** a master on/off switch, three live persisted sliders (line height, letter spacing, word spacing), a reset, and a reading-surface **preview** that renders all three faces and works even while the mode is off (try-before-you-commit).
- State persists in `localStorage` (`st:a11y:dyslexia`) and is **re-applied at boot** via `applyDyslexia()` in `boot()` — no flash of unstyled text.
- Flipped the tool card from `status:'soon'` to a live `mount`; updated `ROADMAP.md` and `STYLE_GUIDE.md`.

## Guardrails

No accounts, no servers, no tracking. The font is inlined, so the mode is fully offline. Nothing leaves the device.

## Testing

Headless Chromium (Playwright) against the built file:
- Tool mounts; toggling on adds `.dys` to `<html>`, sets body `font-family` to Atkinson, `line-height` 28.8px (16×1.8) and `letter-spacing` 0.288px (16×0.018).

author: eliasjustus
body:
## Summary

- Collapses the shell's 5 historically always-on SSE streams (intent, the two advisory classes, action-ledger, indexing-jobs) onto **one** multiplexed connection (`/api/shell-events/stream`), removing the browser's HTTP/1.1 ~6-per-host connection-pool exhaustion that starved the cheap `/api/status`/`/api/inference/status` polls under enrichment/ingest load (tempdoc 649).
- Backend: `MultiplexedSseWriter` fans in N `SseStreamChannel`s onto one client, reusing each channel's existing resume/snapshot logic verbatim — no new resume protocol (the `?since=` bundle is the existing per-channel `streamId:seq` tokens, comma-joined). `ShellEventsStreamController` assembles the 5 sources via new package-visible accessors on the existing controllers (extend, don't fork).
- Frontend: `MultiplexedStream` demuxes by the envelope's existing `streamId` to each consumer's unchanged reducer. All 5 consumers migrated, each keeping a documented fallback direct-connection path. The pre-existing duplicate action-ledger socket (`AiActivityDigest` + `ActionLedgerView` each opening their own connection) collapses for free.
- Adds `governance/live-channels.v1.json` + `check-live-channels.mjs` — a transport-agnostic (SSE *and* fetch-stream) connection-budget register/gate, plus a runtime peak-signal module, so the exhaustion class can't silently recur.
- Correction discovered during implementation (recorded in the tempdoc): indexing-jobs joins the multiplexer rather than going lazy as originally designed — its rows feed an always-mounted task tray, a genuine idle consumer the design pass missed.

## Post-merge-readiness hardening (4 rounds of critical review, each independently verified)

The initial build went through four subsequent critical-review passes (adversarial two-agent review each round, every finding independently re-verified against the actual code before being accepted) plus a round of design-alignment/UX investigation. Real, substantive fixes landed:

- **Late-subscriber race**: a consumer joining the shared connection after it was already open could permanently miss its initial data. Fixed with a debounced reconnect that only fires when a subscriber genuinely still needs it (avoids reconnecting after a subscriber that triggered it already unsubscribed).
- **Backend cleanup leak on partial failure**: a mid-setup exception could leave earlier channels' subscriptions dangling; the cleanup path itself is now guarded against its own failure (multiple simultaneous cleanup failures are individually preserved via `addSuppressed`, not lost).
- **`AdvisoryRailBadge` UX flicker**: it read a raw per-frame connection flag directly, so it visibly flickered "offline" on the now-routine reconnect above. Now reads the app's existing calm, debounced connection-phase signal (the same one every other liveness surface already uses) instead.
- **New diagnostics**: the connection-count/peak signal that was already being tracked internally is now surfaced in the System Health screen.
- Two candidate follow-on ideas (cross-tab connection sharing; migrating to an industry-standard resume-token format) were investigated and explicitly **retracted** — the first solves a problem the shipped desktop app can't actually hit (it already refuses a second window), the second would break reuse with still-live standalone endpoints for no real benefit. author: vaguelyserious
body:
TLDR;
- New wire framing and world-vercel websocket-based writer
- Speed up write-heavy stream workflows 4x
- Reduce e2e test runtime by 2 minutes just by that speedup alone
- NEED TO UPDATE THE VERSION CUTOFF BEFORE MERGING

---

Stream writes move from one short PUT per 10 ms flush batch to a **long-lived, acknowledged write channel** (WebSocket), with a new **framed-v2** wire format that stamps every frame with a per-writer marker (`writerId` + `seq`).

- **Core stays world-agnostic**: there is one write path — the buffered sink flushing through `writeMulti`. When frames carry framed-v2 markers, the flush passes `{ retransmitSafe: true }` (new optional `StreamWriteOptions` on `writeMulti`), granting the world permission to use a transport that resends unconfirmed chunks across reconnects, since readers can deduplicate the overlap. Worlds that ignore the option keep exactly their current behavior. Aborting a writable tears down the world's transport state via the new optional `streams.abort`.
- **world-vercel owns the transport choice**: retransmit-safe batches ride a long-lived WebSocket channel (one writer per stream) — each chunk is one binary message, persisted and published by the backend **on arrival** and acked back `{index, chunkIndex}` in order; `close()` drains all pending acks, completes a **FIN/FIN_ACK** finalization exchange (the server flushes its final storage accounting and confirms) and only then sends the done marker. Everything else uses the batched v2 PUT — which is unchanged.
- **Safe rollout / fallback**: `WORKFLOW_STREAM_WRITE_TRANSPORT` selects `auto` (default) | `websocket` | `put` (operational kill switch). In `auto`, a fatal channel failure circuit-breaks to batched PUT for a cooldown, **redelivering the writer's admitted-but-unconfirmed frames first** (markers dedupe any overlap), so a WS regression degrades to today's PUT path losslessly instead of failing streams.
- `StreamSocketWriter` (in world-vercel): evicts its replay buffer per ack (memory bounded by the in-flight window — 64 frames / 4 MB, deliberately under the server's 100-chunk per-connection backlog cap so a burst can never enter a shed→resend→shed loop), recycles connections proactively (~110 s), and survives unclean closes by resending unacked frames on a fresh channel, under consecutive + lifetime reconnect budgets. A 1009 close (chunk larger than the server's message cap) fails fast with a chunk-size error instead of burning the reconnect budget on a deterministic rejection. Liveness is bounded end to end: the upgrade handshake has a connect deadline, a rolling ack deadline replaces half-open connections that go silent, and a fully-drained channel is released after a short idle instead of pinning its socket until the recycle. All tuning knobs are env-overridable (`WORKFLOW_STREAM_WRITE_*`) and documented in the v5 runtime-tuning page.
- **framed-v2 everywhere it applies**: `getWritable()` object streams **and byte streams** (step-returned / workflow-argument `ReadableStream`s) emit framed-v2 when the target run's capability allows; read-side dedupe by `(writerId, seq)` makes resend overlap exactly-once, including with concurrent writers to one stream (forwarded writables mint their own writerId; framing is per-stream, carried in descriptors and through the workflow VM round-trip). Below the capability cutoff everything stays framed-v1/raw + batch writes with no retransmit grant — byte-identical legacy behavior.
- **Durability semantics** (now an explicit contract on `writeMulti`/`close`): `writeMulti` resolves on window admission (flushes pipeline instead of stop-and-wait); durability is confirmed by acks, `close()` resolving is the durability barrier for everything previously accepted, and an unrecoverable delivery failure surfaces on a later `writeMulti`/`close` (in practice it triggers the lossless PUT fallback instead). Each admitted batch registers an ack barrier with the platform's `waitUntil` so an invocation is never suspended while frames await confirmation.
- **Observability**: the WS upgrade is a client span with the standard run/stream/operation attributes and carries W3C trace context like every other backend request (chunks on the socket have no per-message headers, so the upgrade is where the trace link is established; covered in `trace-propagation.test.ts`). Each writer additionally emits one bounded summary span (`workflow.stream.ws_writer`) with outcome, reconnects, frame/byte counts, peak queue depth, and chunk-to-ack latency; reconnects and fallbacks log with reasons.
- The only new API surface is the v3 `.../ws` upgrade route (plus the existing v3 live-read GET): batched PUT writes, completion, and snapshot reads all stay on v2 exactly as today.

## Why

Today every active writer costs ~100 requests/second and a chunk is only durable-confirmed when its batch's PUT resolves. A streaming request body can't fix this on deployed infra (bodies are delivered to functions only at close — verified empirically), while WS messages arrive incrementally: the deployed probe measured **p50 75 ms chunk-to-ack**, with live readers seeing chunks immediately via per-chunk publish.

Throughput note: within one connection the backend persists chunks serially (reserve → write → publish per chunk), where the PUT batch path parallelized storage writes within a batch. In exchange the writer pipelines continuously instead of stop-and-waiting one round trip per 10 ms batch, so sustained throughput improves for realistic producers; only extreme small-chunk producers trade peak burst rate for the lower request overhead.

## Merge checklist (ordered)

1. **Backend PR deploys first** — this SDK's write channel targets the `/ws` upgrade route (and FIN/FIN_ACK protocol) added in vercel/workflow-server#584; merging this PR before that deploy would make every granted write fall back to batched PUT (functional, but the feature would ship dark).
2. Revert `WORKFLOW_SERVER_URL_OVERRIDE` to `''` in `packages/world-vercel/src/utils.ts` (the "No Test Overrides" check enforces this; it is expected-red until then).
3. **Bump the `framedStreamMarkers` cutoff to the first beta that actually ships this** (currently the next one, `beta.28` — `beta.26`/`beta.27` are published without marker support; the too-low cutoff is only safe on this branch, where writer and reader are always built together). A `TODO(release)` marks the line.

body:
Adds a way to identify which build is live.

- `version.py` reads the short commit hash (with `-dirty` for an unclean tree) **once at import** — refreshes on startup/`--reload`, never runs git per request. git is authoritative for the checkout deploy; `K0SNGIN_COMMIT` env is a fallback for `.git`-less environments (Docker).
- `main.py` emits it as the `X-K0sNgin-Commit` response header (in `SecurityHeadersMiddleware`, avoiding the catch-all route) and logs it at startup.

Verify after deploy: `curl -sI https://k0s.org | grep -i x-k0sngin-commit`.

Disclosure is intentionally public (decided with the owner); the repo is public, so the hash adds little recon value for this single-author site.
