author: ocrosby
body:
## Summary

Establish a uniform, low-indent NASM source style and apply it to every `docs/` chapter.

### New

- **`.editorconfig`** — repo-wide defaults. `*.asm` and most files get 4-space indent, `*.md` gets 2-space, `Makefile` keeps tabs (required by Make), LF line endings, UTF-8.
- **`.claude/rules/asm-style.md`** — the policy: 4-space indent inside sections, labels on their own line, file-level directives (`%define`, `default`, `global`, `extern`, `section`, …) at column 0, single space between mnemonic and operand, comments explain *intent* rather than restating the opcode.

### Reformatted

Every `` ```nasm `` block across 16 `docs/*.md` files was reflowed from the old 12-column "instruction field" convention:

```nasm
            global  _start

            section .text
_start:     mov     rax, 1          ; sys_write
            mov     rdi, 1          ; fd = stdout
```

…to the new 4-space style:

```nasm
global _start

section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1               ; sys_write
    mov rdi, 1               ; fd = stdout
```

**59 blocks reformatted across 16 files.** The reformat was done with a small Python script that only touched content between `` ```nasm `` and `` ``` `` fences, so all surrounding markdown — headings, prose, tables, the `## Runnable` and `## Next` sections — is unchanged.

### Updated index pointers

- `.claude/rules/README.md` — new entry for `asm-style`.
- `CLAUDE.md` — Project Rules index entry for `asm-style`.

### Out of scope

The `examples/*.asm` files are **not** touched here. They get the same reformat **plus** instructive inline comments in a follow-on PR — folding them in here would mix the mechanical style change with the educational content change and make this PR much harder to audit.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open any `docs/*.md` on GitHub and confirm the `nasm` blocks render with the new style (label on own line, 4-space body, comments around column 28).
- [ ] Confirm `.editorconfig` is honored by your editor — open a fresh `.asm` file and verify the indent is 4 spaces.
- [ ] Read `.claude/rules/asm-style.md` and confirm it captures the style you wanted.
- [ ] Spot-check `docs/13-loops.md` `sum_arr` and `docs/14-procedures.md` `square` — the most label-heavy examples.

author: ichi0g0y
body:
## Summary

Exiting the attached shell (terminal preview → `enter`/`t`, then `exit`) destroyed the shell tmux session, which made `tmux::attach` return an `Err`. That error propagated via `?` through `handle_key` → `run_loop` → `main`, terminating robco instead of returning to its TUI. This makes `exit` behave like a normal `ctrl-q` detach in both the outside-tmux and in-tmux cases.

## Changes

`src/tmux.rs` only (+50 / -6):

- `attach()`: after the blocking attach/switch + `binding.restore()`, if the session no longer exists, return cleanly and discard the attach error — a destroyed session is a normal return path, not a failure.
- `ReturnKeyBinding::restore()`: restore session-scoped `status` / `status-right` options only if the session still exists (`restore_session_option_if_present`), and restore the global `C-q` root binding only if the tmux server is still alive (`has_server`). This removes the fatal error in the outside-tmux case.
- `wait_for_return_key()`: spawn `tmux wait-for` as a child and poll every 100 ms; if the session disappears, kill the child and return `Ok`. Fixes the in-tmux hang where the `C-q` return signal never arrives because the user typed `exit` instead.

The `C-q` detach path and the agent (claude) attach path (where the session persists) are unchanged.

## Test Plan

Run from the task worktree:

- `cargo build` → ok
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` → ok (no warnings)
- `cargo test` → ok (14 passed, 0 failed)

Not performed (environment limitation): interactive tmux attach/`exit` cannot be exercised in the CI/sandbox (no TTY; tmux socket creation is blocked). Manual verification is recommended on a real terminal: attach to a shell both inside and outside tmux, type `exit`, confirm robco returns to its TUI without terminating, and confirm `C-q` detach and re-attach still work.

## Impact

- Fixes robco terminating when the user exits an attached shell. Scope limited to tmux attach/detach control flow; no behavior change for the agent attach path or `C-q` detach.

## Checklist

- [x] Build, clippy (`-D warnings`), and tests pass
- [x] Minimal diff (single file)
- [x] Per-task review (Codex) — Adopt, no blocking findings
- [x] Follow-up filed for the pre-existing `src/tmux.rs` >300-line size limit (#34)

author: jeffreysardella
body:
## Why
When an ETL job is hard-killed (OOM / exit 137) it never writes its terminal status, so its `etl_runs` row is stuck at `status='running'` forever. Those zombie rows make `/api/freshness` and pipeline-health look like a job is perpetually in flight — and clearing them has been a recurring manual `UPDATE` chore in the backlog.

## What
New `etl.clear_stale_runs` module resets any `'running'` row **older than a safety threshold** (default 6h — longer than any real job; the manual-ETL workflow caps at 4h) to `'error'`, leaving genuinely in-flight jobs untouched. Now a one-click job via the existing workflow:

```
gh workflow run run-etl.yml -f job=clear_stale_runs -f refresh_matviews=false
```

The threshold is a CLI arg; the query runs in the caller's transaction when a `conn`/session is injected (used by the test).

## Test
Integration test seeds a 2-day-old `running` row + a 30-min-old `running` row and asserts only the stale one flips to `error`. Runs in CI (no local test Postgres in dev env).

author: sorawit-w
body:
## What

Adds one code-standards rule and a cross-link — additive, non-breaking.

- **[working-patterns.md § Code Standards](skills/kerby/resources/references/working-patterns.md)** — new bullet **Hoist repeated literals to a single named source**, placed directly under "Prefer boring, readable solutions" as its flip side. Once a literal (especially an allowed-value *set*) is referenced at ≥2 real call sites — or would force multi-place edits if it changed — define it once as a named exported constant and import it. In TypeScript, derive the type from the constant (`as const` + `typeof X[number]`).
- **[validation.md](skills/kerby/resources/references/validation.md)** — one-line cross-link on the hardcoded-value bullet pointing to the new rule.

## Why — dedup != externalization

`working-patterns.md` already says *inline until a second caller forces the seam* but never said what to do **once the second caller arrives**, so agents re-type the same `['admin','editor','viewer']` array at each call site; copies drift and a bare literal has no IDE find-usages. The fix is **deduplication** (one named in-code constant), a distinct axis from **externalization** (config/env) — which `validation.md`'s hardcoded-value rule (env-varies-or-gates-risk) and `guardrails.md`'s secrets boundary still govern. The two were silently conflated; this names the move and draws the line.

## Scope / ring-fence

- `[behavioral]` rule — **no hook, lint, or `.eval` fixture** added (a naive duplicate-literal linter would over-fire against kerby's own "duplication beats premature abstraction").
- **No `.eval` change.** `.eval/triggers/kerby.json` tests skill *activation*, not rule adherence — untouched.
- Lone magic numbers deliberately not singled out in v1.
- Bumps to **5.8.0** (CHANGELOG + manifests + README); `check-skill-compat.py` passes, version parity OK.

## Validation

Ran `skill-evaluator` in-session (kerby's policy for a new directive): split-role executor+grader, **6 tests / 25 assertions, all pass**. The over-fire guard (single-use literal stays inline), the externalization boundary (env-varying URL → config, not an in-code constant), and the secret boundary (`sk_live_` key → `.env`, never an exported constant) all routed correctly. Verdict: ready-to-ship, 0 rule-text diffs needed.

For review — merge is yours.

author: reese8272
body:
## The "render loop"

A clip sat on the **"Rendering your clip… (~30s)"** spinner indefinitely.

### Root cause (frontend)
`ClipPlayer.triggerRender` sets `requesting=true` but only resets it on the non-409 *error* path — a 202/409 success never clears it. The spinner shows while `requesting || render_status==='running'` and clears only when a `render_uri` lands. So any render that never produces a `render_uri` spins **forever**, masking the real terminal state.

### What triggered it in prod
Clip `ebd4cee8` failed permanently — its source media was purged (`videos.source_uri IS NULL`), so the worker raised `ValueError("Source video not available")` and set `render_status=failed` in ~0.2s (never `running`). The UI should have shown "Render failed" + retry, but the latched `requesting` flag kept it spinning.

Verified via prod worker log (`render_clip_failed_permanent exc_type=ValueError`) + DB (`clips.render_status=failed`).

### Fix
Reset `requesting` in a `finally`, so the spinner is driven by server `render_status`. A fast-failing render now surfaces as **"Render failed" + retry** instead of spinning.

- Regression test `ClipPlayer.test.tsx`: "does not latch the spinner after a render request settles".
- Full frontend suite **217 passed**; `tsc` + `eslint` clean.

### Follow-up (not in this PR)
Logged a separate backend gap in `docs/OFF_COURSE_BUGS.md`: a clip whose source was purged offers a render/retry button that can never succeed, and `source_uri` was NULL only 3 days after a `done` ingest (purge-timing/ingest investigation needed).

body:
## Qué

Guardarraíl **determinista** de accesibilidad + viewports extremos en CI, sin tocar pantallas de features.

- **axe-core sobre la galería:** `@axe-core/playwright` (dev dep) recorre **cada caso** de la galería (`web/src/gallery/**`, pantallas reales con fixtures, sin login ni red) a **390×844** y falla solo con violaciones de impacto **serio/crítico**.
- **Viewport extremo 320px:** aserción `scrollWidth <= clientWidth` por pantalla (no-overflow horizontal en móvil pequeño).
- **Baseline** (`web/gallery-a11y-baseline.json`, como design-lint): congela la deuda previa para dejar `main` en verde; solo bloquean las regresiones **NUEVAS**. Dos listas: `axe` (huella = caso·regla·target) y `overflow` (id del caso). Regenerar a propósito: `A11Y_UPDATE_BASELINE=1 npm run a11y`.
- **CI:** job nuevo `a11y` (hermético, sin red externa, `GALLERY=1`, placeholders `VITE_*`), reusando el patrón de los E2E herméticos.

## Baseline congelado (pista para Fase 2)

- **11 violaciones `color-contrast` (serias)** en 3 pantallas: `crear-viaje` (captions de fecha, hints, labels), `home-con-datos` y `home-dashboard-lleno` (`feedCount`, `pinnedLabel`). Texto gris claro con contraste por debajo de WCAG AA.
- **2 overflows a 320px conocidos:** `tarjeta-resultado` (imagen de 1080px para compartir, no una pantalla responsive) y `editar-reto` (395px, deuda menor).

## Verificación del guardarraíl

Probado que **falla con violación nueva**: añadí temporalmente un caso de galería con texto de contraste insuficiente; el check reportó la `color-contrast` nueva (no estaba en el baseline) y el overflow del caso. Revertido tras confirmarlo.

`npm run format && lint && type-check && test (616) && build && design-lint && a11y` → todo verde.

## Coste de CI

Job aparte en paralelo a `quality`/`smoke`: ~20s de spec (un solo worker recorre los ~18 casos × axe a un viewport + overflow a 320px) + instalación de Chromium (cacheable). axe se limita a **un** viewport representativo; los 320px solo hacen la aserción barata de overflow, para no multiplicar el coste.

Closes #396

## Summary

Update `release.yml` Go version from 1.25 to 1.26 to match `go.mod`.

## Problem

The release workflow fails on every tag push because it installs Go 1.25 but `go.mod` requires Go 1.26:

```
go: go.mod requires go >= 1.26 (running go 1.25.11; GOTOOLCHAIN=local)
```

This blocked the `v0.0.3` and `v0.0.4` releases.

## Fix

One-line change: `go-version: '1.25'` → `go-version: '1.26'`

author: copilot
body:
Build dependencies (`build-essential`, `libffi-dev`) were installed in a separate layer from `pip install`, leaving the entire build toolchain in the final image — increasing image size and attack surface.

## Changes

- **Single RUN layer**: Merged apt install + pip install + cleanup into one layer to prevent intermediate build artifacts from persisting in the image
- **Purge build-only packages post-compilation**: `build-essential` and `libffi-dev` are removed after `pip install` completes, along with their transitive deps via `autoremove`
- **Explicit `libffi8` retention**: `libffi8` is listed as a manually-installed package so `autoremove` does not strip it — required at runtime by `cffi`/`cryptography` (transitive dep of `google-auth`)

```dockerfile
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    libffi-dev \
    libffi8 \
    && pip install -r requirements.txt \
    && apt-get purge -y build-essential libffi-dev \
    && apt-get autoremove -y \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

author: andytavares
body:
## What

Autosave was racing with the DB read that fires when navigating back to a note or diagram: the cleanup flush could write stale content to the DB *after* the fresh load had already read from it, silently discarding edits. This PR fixes the data loss by introducing an in-session `bodyCache` and `diagramCache` in the Zustand store. Both caches are written optimistically on every autosave (and on first DB fetch), so navigating back to a note or diagram always reads the latest in-memory content rather than going to the DB. The `NoteEditor` effect that forcefully re-synced the editor document with `initialDoc` is also removed — it was a symptom of the same race and is now unnecessary.

## How to test

1. Open a note and type several words, then immediately switch to a different note before the autosave debounce fires.
2. Navigate back to the first note and confirm the content you typed is still present.
3. Repeat with a diagram: draw something, switch away mid-autosave, return, and verify the drawing is intact.
4. Open a note, type, wait for the "saved" indicator, navigate away and back — confirm the sidebar title/preview updates immediately without a full list refresh.
5. Run the unit tests (`pnpm test` or equivalent) and confirm all new store specs pass.

author: teakbuilds
body:
Resolves C-844 — https://linear.app/teakio/issue/C-844

## What
Uncaught exceptions now emit the same observable `exception` log event the caught path already emits, so a host-app `LogListener` sees uncaught crashes the same way it sees caught ones. Follow-up to C-843 (iOS caught-path parity), which deliberately deferred the uncaught path.

## How
`Raven.uncaughtException` adds one call to the caught-path emit, `Teak.log.exception(ex, false)`:
- **Shape is identical to caught** — it reuses `throwableToMap`, producing `event_type "exception"`, level `ERROR`, `event_data {type, value, module, stacktrace}`. So Android stays internally consistent caught == uncaught.
- **`reportToRaven=false`** — the handler already reports to Sentry on the next line; `false` avoids a duplicate report through the SDK Raven. `reportToRaven` gates only the Sentry send, not the `log()` call.
- **Suppressions preserved** — the emit is gated on `!shouldSuppressThrowable(ex)` and stays inside the existing `OutOfMemoryError` guard, so signal-prefixed native crashes and OOM remain Sentry-only and emit no event.

## Cross-platform contract
The cross-platform guarantee is the `{type, value}` intersection. `module`/`stacktrace` are Android-only extras (iOS has neither) — already true on the caught path. The C-739 e2e must assert `{type, value}` only.

## Tests
`UncaughtExceptionLogEventTest` drives `raven.uncaughtException(thread, ex)` against the real handler:
- positively asserts the `LogListener` receives the event with `{type, value}` (fails if the emit is reverted — verified)
- signal-prefixed throwable → no event
- `OutOfMemoryError` → no event

Full debug suite: 94 tests, 0 failures.

author: robbiemckinstry
body:
## What

The local corpus loader (`collect_local_files` in `corpus.rs`) swept the `--input` directory **non-recursively** (a single-level `read_dir`). The downloaded CommonPile slice is laid out one subdirectory per source — `<source>/<source>.chunk.NN.jsonl.gz` — so pointing `wubbie tokenizer --input ./corpus` at it found **zero** shards and aborted with `no corpus files … found in directory`. The previous workaround was to flatten the tree into a directory of symlinks; this removes that need.

This replaces the single-level sweep with an iterative depth-first walk that discovers shards at any depth.

## Details

- **Recursive walk**: iterative DFS over a stack of directories; finds `.jsonl`/`.jsonl.gz`/`.txt`/… shards nested at any depth.
- **Deterministic order**: the full result is sorted, so shard order is independent of filesystem return order (the repo's no-flake testing policy).
- **Symlink-safe**: recursion decisions use `entry.file_type()` (does *not* follow symlinks), so symlinked directories are skipped and the walk can't follow a symlink cycle. File detection still uses `is_file()`, so a symlinked *shard* is still picked up.
- Updates the CLI `--input` help and the doc strings that described the old non-recursive sweep.
- Adds `collects_corpus_files_recursively_and_sorted` covering nested shards + ignored non-corpus files.
- Gitignores the local `./corpus` cache so the downloaded pretraining data is never accidentally committed.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --all` ✅
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace --locked -- -D warnings` ✅
- `cargo nextest run --workspace` — corpus/tokenizer tests pass, including the new one.
- **End-to-end**: ran the release binary against a tree mirroring `./corpus` (a `.jsonl` one level down, a `.jsonl.gz` two levels down, plus `README.md`/`manifest.json` to ignore). It discovered both shards, skipped the non-corpus files, trained, round-tripped, and wrote the tokenizer (exit 0).

body:
## Summary
Introduces a comprehensive admin-editable content management system for all public marketing pages. Admins can now edit hero sections, testimonials, CTAs, and other marketing copy directly from the admin panel without code changes. Content is validated, cached, and falls back to sensible defaults if edits are invalid.

## Key Changes

**Content Registry & Validation**
- Added `src/lib/site-content.ts`: A declarative registry of all editable sections (hero, trust strip, problem, promise, guide, plan, outcomes, glance, stories, FAQ, footer, etc.) with field definitions and default content
- Implemented Zod schema derivation from field descriptors for automatic validation
- `resolveContent()` merges stored edits over defaults and validates, ensuring bad edits never break the live site

**Admin UI**
- Added `src/components/admin/content-builder.tsx`: Full-featured editor with form generation from field descriptors, image upload/paste, list item management, and section visibility toggles
- Added `src/components/admin/image-field.tsx`: Image field with drag-drop upload, URL paste fallback, and live thumbnail preview
- New admin page at `/admin/content` to manage all editable sections, grouped by page with reordering and reset capabilities

**Database & Server Actions**
- Added `SiteSection` table to store editable content, visibility, and order per section
- `src/server/admin-content-actions.ts`: Server actions for update, toggle, reorder, and reset with audit logging
- `src/server/site-content.ts`: Cached reads with graceful fallback to defaults if DB is unavailable (supports prerendering without a database)

**Image Upload**
- Added `src/lib/blob.ts`: Minimal S3-compatible upload using AWS Signature V4 (no SDK dependency), works with AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO
- Added `src/app/api/upload/route.ts`: Authenticated image upload endpoint with file validation
- Configured `next.config.ts` to allow next/image to serve from the blob host

**Page Refactoring**
- Extracted hardcoded JSX from `src/app/page.tsx` and `src/app/organizations/page.tsx` into reusable section components
- Created `src/components/marketing/sections/home.tsx` and `src/components/marketing/sections/organizations.tsx` with all section renderers
- Added `src/components/marketing/sections/registry.tsx` to map section keys to components
- Pages now fetch content from the DB, resolve it, and render via the registry—identical visual output but fully editable

**Database & Seeding**
- Added migration to create `SiteSection` table with unique constraint on `key`
- Updated `prisma/seed.ts` to populate initial section rows from the registry on fresh installs

**Supporting Changes**
- Added `content:manage` capability to RBAC for admin access control
- Updated admin layout to include content editor link
- Updated `.env.example` with S3 configuration options
- Updated `LandingNav` to read from editable content
- Updated `Footer` component to accept editable content
- Updated various pages (login, enroll, book-a-call, confirmation) to fetch footer content

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Graceful degradation**: When S3 env is absent, image fields fall back to URL paste only; when DB is unreachable at build time, pages prerender from registry defaults
- **Cache invalidation**: `revalidateTag()` on edits keeps prerendered pages fresh
- **Type safety**: Field descriptors drive both the admin form generator and Zod schema derivation, eliminating duplication
- **Audit trail**: All edits are logged via the existing audit system
- **Core sections**: Funnel-critical sections (hero, CTAs) show a warning when hidden to prevent accidental removal of conversion paths

Now that the Cognito service team has approved our request to increase the number of resource servers allowed per user pool, we are able to include the full list of jurisdictions associated with the Social Work compact so that staff users can be added for any of those jurisdictions with needed permission scopes. 

This also enhances our mock license generation script to support creating test practitioners with matching single and multi-state licenses, and performs some light cleanup of an unused S3 bucket from the Cosm and Socw CDK apps.

### Testing List
- `yarn test:unit:all` should run without errors or warnings
- `yarn serve` should run without errors or warnings
- `yarn build` should run without errors or warnings
- For API configuration changes: CDK tests added/updated in `backend/compact-connect/tests/unit/test_api.py`
- For API endpoint changes: OpenAPI spec updated to show latest endpoint configuration `run compact-connect/bin/download_oas30.py`
- Code review

Closes #1703

  * Expanded supported jurisdiction coverage across configuration and API request/response schemas.
* **Bug Fixes / Behavior Changes**
  * Removed export-results bucket wiring from the search API and updated related test setup and cleanup to match.

author: samidarko
body:
## Why

mika#1679 reported that the mika#1383 auto-PR-create path opened **non-draft** rescue PRs that bypassed the mika#1613 recovery guards (evidence: #1678, #1683 — auto-merge-eligible without operator review). That diagnosis was correct but **incomplete**.

A confidence-check of the groomed plan against current code found the real shape: `dispatch-lib.sh` has **two** PR-creation paths firing on the *same* trigger (dev-pilot committed+pushed, no PR), and the first **shadows** the second:

- **Path A** — mika#1383 "structural completion gate" in `_post_flight_recovery()`: opened a non-draft PR, then set the **global `PR_URL`**.
- **Path B** — mika#1396 `commit-pushed-no-pr` rescue in `dispatch_claude_pilot()`, guarded by `[ -z "$PR_URL" ]`: already did the fully-correct thing (`--draft` + rescue header + `RECOVERY_PENDING: true` + `wip-rescue` label + canonical `PR:` line).

Path A ran first and set `PR_URL`, so Path B's guard was always false → Path B's `commit-pushed-no-pr` branch was **dead code**. The plan's four-edit fix would have made Path A *duplicate* Path B — two implementations of one safety contract that churned 4× in a week.

## Decision lineage

The cleaner fix (delete Path A's PR-creation) overturned the architect's GROOMED design + its explicit "out of scope: unification" note, so it was routed rather than taken unilaterally:
- **mika-arch** (session `2d397bee`): confirmed the shadowing, confirmed its own "refactor if further drift surfaces" criterion is met → **Disposition: ESCALATE**.
- **Mika Prime** (bearing): ruled **R2 / single-source-of-truth** — bearing-scope, ratified; required an explicit reachability pre-condition check.
- Plan revised via `/mika-revise-plan` → **mika-arch second-pass: Verdict GROOMED** (ratified the Guard-2 marker commit, Option a).

## What changed (`skills/bundled/_shared/dispatch-lib.sh`)

- **Edit 1** — delete Path A's Phase-B PR-creation (`gh pr list`/`gh pr create`); **keep** Phase A (trailing-dirty rescue, which advances `POST_RUN_HEAD`). With `PR_URL` left empty, Path B fires and owns the rescue PR. The "PR already exists" re-dispatch case stays safe (re-query sets `PR_URL` → Path B no-ops).
- **Edit 2** — add an empty `wip(mika#1383)` marker commit to Path B's `commit-pushed-no-pr` branch (scoped to that class only) so the PR head matches Guard 2's `^wip\(`. Idempotent on re-dispatch; push failure is surfaced (`rescue_marker_push.failed`) rather than silently swallowed.

**Reachability verified** (Prime's required pre-condition): `_check_pilot_force_push` returns 0 unconditionally for dev-pilot (`dispatch-lib.sh:1265`), so Path B is reachable once Path A's `PR_URL`-set is gone — no fail-silent-no-PR risk.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 — Path A's PR-creation removed (no `gh pr create` in `_post_flight_recovery`)
- [x] AC2 — Path A's Phase-A trailing-dirty rescue retained
- [x] AC3 — commit-pushed-no-pr rescue produced by Path B: draft + `RECOVERY_PENDING` + rescue header + `wip-rescue` label + `PR:` line
- [x] AC4 — reachability evidence (Path B fires; exactly one PR)
- [x] AC5 — regression: dirty-worktree class unchanged
- [x] AC6 — Guard-2 `wip(mika#1383)` marker commit (Option a), commit-pushed-no-pr only
- [x] AC7 — integration test (Test 15 rewritten + Test 15b added)

## Verification

- `bash skills/bundled/_shared/test-dispatch-lib.sh` → **298 passed, 0 failed**
- `shellcheck -S error` → clean; `make verify-bundled-skills` → pass; `bash scripts/verify-pipeline.sh` → pass
- Code review (correctness: clean; reliability: 2 findings — observable push failure + idempotency — both applied)

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-06-30-011-fix-1679-dispatch-lib-mika-1383-recovery-guards-plan.md` (rev 2)
Compound: `docs/solutions/workflow-issues/dispatch-lib-mika-1383-shadows-mika-1396-rescue-via-global-pr-url-2026-07-01.md`

Closes #1679
